672	title: "Synchronize Audio"
673	description: Line up a camera and a separate recorder, or any clips of the same moment, by matching their sound.
674	---
675	
676	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
677	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
678	
679	Synchronize Audio lines up two or more clips by their sound. The usual case is a camera clip and a separate audio recorder that captured the same moment. It finds where the sound matches, moves the clips into place and corrects any clock drift, all as one undo step.
680	
681	<AtAGlance
682	  menu="Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio"
683	  tools="sync_audio"
684	  needs="Nothing. The matching and the voice detection run on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
685	/>
686	
687	## Line up clips
688	
689	<Steps>
690	
691	1. Put each clip on its own track. They don't need to be close to each other.
692	
693	2. If the recorder holds several similar stretches, trim it roughly around the camera's sound, so it [matches the right one](#matching-by-sound).
694	
695	3. [Select the clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/).
696	
697	4. Choose **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**. It has no keyboard shortcut.
698	
699	5. Wait for the [Synchronizing Audio sheet](#the-synchronizing-audio-sheet) to finish.
700	
701	</Steps>
702	
703	One clip, the [anchor](#the-anchor), stays where it is. Every other clip slides along its own track until its sound plays at the same moment as the anchor's. The whole command is one undo step, named **Synchronize Audio**.
704	
705	If Frame Job is sure of the match, it's applied straight away. If it isn't, Frame Job [asks you first](/audio/weak-sync-matches/).
706	
707	It's all or nothing. If any clip can't be matched, nothing moves, and [the reasons are listed](#when-it-wont-run).
708	
709	If the clips are already in sync, nothing changes and Frame Job beeps. Choosing the command a second time on the same clips does this.
710	
711	## Which clips it takes
712	
713	**Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio** is available when at least two selected clips can play sound and aren't [nests](/editing/nests/).
714	
715	Anything else in the selection is left out without a message: a nest, a still, a title, a file with no audio track, a clip with its audio switched off. To line up clips inside a nest, open it with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and select them there.
716	
717	## The anchor
718	
719	Frame Job picks the anchor this way:
720	
721	1. Among the selected clips that have a picture, the one that starts earliest. If none has a picture, all of them are considered.
722	2. If two start at the same time, the one on the rearmost track.
723	3. If they're still tied, the one created first.
724	
725	So a camera clip stays put and the recorder moves to it. The anchor is never moved or trimmed, and its speed doesn't change.
726	
727	## Matching by sound
728	
729	Each file's sound is analysed once, after it's imported, into a form that isn't thrown off by differences in gain, microphone or room. Frame Job compares the files, not the clips, so a clip's volume and effects make no difference.
730	
731	- **Speech comes first.** When both clips hold at least 2 seconds of speech, as judged by the on-device voice model, only the speech is compared. Otherwise all the sound is.
732	- **The trimmed parts come first.** Frame Job looks within the parts each clip is trimmed to, when both are at least 2 seconds long. It searches the whole files only if that finds no usable match and at least one clip is trimmed.
733	
734	:::tip
735	A recording with two similar stretches can match the wrong one. Trimming the recorder roughly around the camera's sound tells Frame Job which one you mean.
736	:::
737	
738	## The waveform check
739	
740	Sounding alike isn't enough, because two takes of the same words can look like a match. So a match is used only if the two waveforms also line up there, as a clear peak within 48 ms. Frame Job checks up to 30 seconds of the overlap, where the sound agrees most, in the speech band of 300 to 3,400 Hz.
741	
742	The same check fine-tunes the offset to less than a frame.
743	
744	## Moves land on whole frames
745	
746	Clips move by a whole number of frames at the project's frame rate, so up to half a frame of constant offset can remain. At 30 fps that's about 17 ms.
747	
748	## The head trim
749	
750	If a clip would have to start before 0:00 to line up, it loses that much from its start instead, and starts at 0:00 in sync. Frame Job trims only what it has to. It won't do this if less than a frame of the clip would be left.
751	
752	## Drift correction
753	
754	Two devices' clocks never run at quite the same rate, so a recorder slowly falls out of sync over a long take. When the clips overlap for at least 60 seconds, Frame Job measures that drift in 20-second windows along the overlap and corrects it by playing the moved clip at a slightly different speed, at most 0.2 % from ×1.
755	
756	The correction is part of the same undo step. There's no drift figure to read. What changes is the clip's speed, and **Keep pitch** is turned off. The [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/) shows the rate to two decimal places, so a correction such as ×1.0004 still reads 1.00× there. The clip gets very slightly longer or shorter to match.
757	
758	Drift is left alone when:
759	
760	- it's under 5 ms across the overlap
761	- it's too small to tell from no drift, meaning under three times its own uncertainty
762	- correcting it would take more than 0.2 % from ×1
763	- too little of the overlap matches to measure it
764	
765	:::note
766	The correction plays the sound slightly faster or slower, as tape would, so the pitch moves very slightly with the speed. Like any clip with Keep pitch off at a speed other than ×1, the clip's sound is [rendered in the background](/speed/keep-pitch/#tape-pitch-is-rendered-in-the-background). It's briefly silent in the preview after the correction, and again after each trim, split or speed change. An export waits for it.
767	:::
768	
769	## The Synchronizing Audio sheet
770	
771	Matching runs in the background behind a **Synchronizing Audio** sheet, with a progress bar and the line "Matching the sound of N clips…". Nothing moves until a match is found.
772	
773	**Cancel** or <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the sheet and leaves everything as it was.
774	
775	If the project changes while the matching runs, for example because an agent edits it or moves in or out of a nest, nothing is applied. Frame Job beeps and the inspector says to choose Synchronize Audio again.
776	
777	## When it won't run
778	
779	Frame Job beeps and lists every reason in [the strip at the foot of the inspector](/getting-started/refused-edits/#the-refusal-strip), naming each clip by its number. The strip shows three lines, so hover over it to read a long one.
780	
781	It checks each clip first, and won't start matching until they all pass. A clip can't be lined up when it:
782	
783	- plays no sound in the timeline
784	- is still being analysed. Its sound or speech analysis hasn't finished, so try again in a moment.
785	- comes from a file with under 2 seconds of sound
786	- plays more than 0.2 % away from ×1. Set it back to ×1 first.
787	- plays at a different rate from the ×1 its speed shows, because its source is stretched
788	- plays [reversed](/speed/reverse/)
789	- [ramps its speed](/speed/speed-ramps/), because a speed action changes its rate over its length
790	
791	The rest come up during the matching:
792	
793	- Two of the clips are on one track. Each needs its own.
794	- A clip has no sound to line up by, because its analysis found no sound at all.
795	- Nothing matches. See [When nothing matches](/audio/weak-sync-matches/#when-nothing-matches).
796	- A clip matches the anchor's sound but the waveforms don't line up there, for example two takes of the same words. They aren't one recording.
797	- A clip matches the anchor's sound but the two share under 2 seconds of waveform there, too little to confirm it's one recording.
798	- A clip would lose so much of its head that less than a frame is left.
799	- A clip would never play at the same time as the anchor once lined up. Extend its trim, or the anchor's.
800	- A clip would overlap another clip on its own track after the move. Move that clip out of the way, or put this one on a free track.
801	
802	## With an agent
803	
804	`sync_audio` does the same thing. An agent can name the anchor, and it's told by name when it passes a nest or a clip that plays no sound, where the menu leaves those out. Its answer also gives each clip's offset, confidence, trim and drift, and clips already in sync are reported as such. See [Tools: audio](/mcp/tools-audio/).
805	
806	## Related
807	
808	- [Confident and weak matches](/audio/weak-sync-matches/)
809	- [The Speed section](/speed/speed-section/)
810	- [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/)
811	- [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/)
812	- [Nests](/editing/nests/)
813	---
814	title: Track compressor and limiter
815	description: Compress and limit a track's whole sound, or everything in a nest together, and know where the preview differs from the export.
816	---
817	
818	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
819	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
820	
821	A track can have its own compressor and limiter, acting on the sound of every clip on it together. Use them to even out a whole voice-over, or to hold a music bed under a ceiling, without setting each clip. This page covers a track's. A clip has its own [compressor](/audio/compressor/) and [limiter](/audio/limiter/).
822	
823	<AtAGlance
824	  menu="Track ▸ Mix…"
825	  where={['The sliders switch in the track header', "Mix… in the track's right-click menu"]}
826	  tools="set_track"
827	/>
828	
829	## Turn on a track's compressor or limiter
830	
831	<Steps>
832	
833	1. Open the [Track Mix panel](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/#open-the-track-mix-panel) for the track.
834	
835	2. Tick **Compressor** or **Limit peaks**, below **Pan**. Each turns on at its defaults, and its rows stop being greyed out.
836	
837	3. Adjust the rows.
838	
839	</Steps>
840	
841	Unticking throws the settings away, so ticking again starts from the defaults. **Reset** at the foot of the panel turns both off, and resets the track's volume and pan too.
842	
843	The header's sliders switch stays lit while either is on.
844	
845	## Where they sit
846	
847	Both act on the track's whole sound: every clip on it, after each clip's own processing, its volume, fades, crossfades and ducking, and after the track's volume and pan. The compressor runs first, then the limiter.
848	
849	A track's compressor and limiter hear the track after its fader. That's the difference from a clip's compressor, which hears the clip before its volume. Turning the track down turns down what reaches them, so a compressor at −20 dB over a track at −6 dB compresses less.
850	
851	## Compressor settings
852	
853	| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick picks |
854	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
855	| **Compressor** | Turns the track's compressor on. | on, off | off | |
856	| **Threshold** | The level above which it starts turning the track down. | −60 to 0 dB | −18 dB | −30, −24, −18, −12, −6 |
857	| **Ratio** | How strongly it turns down sound above the threshold. | 1 to 20 :1 | 3:1 | 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 8, 20 |
858	| **Attack** | How quickly it reacts. | 0 to 200 ms | 10 ms | 1, 5, 10, 30, 100 ms |
859	| **Release** | How quickly it lets go. | 10 to 2000 ms | 200 ms | 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000 ms |
860	| **Makeup** | Gain added afterwards. | 0 to 24 dB | 0 dB | 0, 3, 6, 12 |
861	
862	## Limiter settings
863	
864	| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick picks |
865	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
866	| **Limit peaks** | Turns the track's limiter on. | on, off | off | |
867	| **Ceiling** | The highest true peak the track may hand the mix. | −24 to 0 dBTP | −1 dBTP | −1, −2, −3, −6 |
868	| **Release** | How quickly the level recovers after a peak. | 1 to 1000 ms | 100 ms | 50, 100, 200, 500 ms |
869	
870	Each control is a slider and a field. A number typed outside the range goes to the nearest end of it.
871	
872	## Use a track as a nest's bus
873	
874	A bus is one path that several sounds share. A [nest's](/editing/nests/) whole mix plays through the track its nest clip sits on, so a compressor or limiter on that track acts on everything inside the nest together. Put a voice's clips in a nest and compress them as one, whatever tracks they're on inside it.
875	
876	A nest's own tracks have no compressor or limiter. Inside an open nest, both sections are greyed out, and their tooltip says "A nest's mix plays through the dynamics of the track that holds it." **Volume**, **Pan** and **Reset** still work there.
877	
878	Nesting a selection doesn't copy a compressor or limiter from the tracks it came from. The track the nest clip lands on keeps its own.
879	
880	## Exact in the export, approximate in the preview
881	
882	An export plays each track with a compressor or limiter through them on its own, before the tracks are mixed. That's exact, and a [stem](/export/stems/) of that track includes them. The [master limiter](/export/loudness/) still runs over the mix afterwards.
883	
884	The preview can only approximate this. Where a track's clips overlap, such as a crossfade or a nest's tracks, the preview plays the track's sound in more than one piece and runs the compressor and limiter on each piece separately. So the pieces can add up past a track limiter's ceiling while you edit, even though the export holds it.
885	
886	While any track has a compressor or limiter and the preview plays at normal speed, the [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/) says so in its footer: "The mix as the preview plays it, with track compressors and limiters approximate, before the export's loudness and master limiter."
887	
888	:::tip
889	Judge a track limiter's ceiling on the export, not on the preview's meters.
890	:::
891	
892	## What hears them
893	
894	| Hears them | Doesn't hear them |
895	| --- | --- |
896	| The preview, approximately | [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) |
897	| The [level meter](/audio/level-meter/) and the [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/), approximately | The [Loudness read-out](/audio/volume/#read-the-level) |
898	| Every export and stem, exactly | [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) and [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) |
899	| | A [scrub](/audio/scrub-audio/) |
900	
901	Normalize, the Loudness read-out, Enhance Voice and Match Audio work on the clip itself, before the track.
902	
903	## Good to know
904	
905	- A track's compressor and limiter are one setting for the whole track, and can't change over time. A track has no EQ or other effects.
906	- Each change is one undo step. Turning one on or off, a drag or a typed value is named "Track Compressor" or "Track Limiter", and **Reset** is named "Reset Track Mix".
907	- A track with a limiter plays 3.3 ms later in the preview, and Frame Job places it 3.3 ms earlier to match, so it stays in sync.
908	
909	## With an agent
910	
911	`set_track` sets both, through its `compressor` and `limiter` arguments. Each takes the whole setting at once, so any value you leave out goes to its default, and `null` turns it off. As in the panel, a nest's own tracks can't have them. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#a-tracks-compressor-and-limiter).
912	
913	## Related
914	
915	- [Track volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/)
916	- [Compressor](/audio/compressor/)
917	- [Limiter](/audio/limiter/)
918	- [The Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/)
919	- [Export loudness](/export/loudness/)
920	---
921	title: Track volume and pan
922	description: Set a whole track's level and left-right balance in the Track Mix panel, on top of what each clip already does.
923	---
924	
925	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
926	
927	Each track has its own volume and pan, applied on top of every clip on it. Use them to balance a music bed against a voice-over without touching each clip.
928	
929	<AtAGlance
930	  menu="Track ▸ Mix…"
931	  where={['The sliders switch in the track header', "Mix… in the track's right-click menu"]}
932	  tools="set_track"
933	/>
934	
935	## Open the Track Mix panel
936	
937	Click the sliders switch, the fifth in the track's header. **Mix…** in the track's right-click menu does the same. **Track ▸ Mix…** opens it for the [current track](/timeline/tracks/#the-current-track), and has no keyboard shortcut.
938	
939	A small panel opens beside the header, with the track's name at the top. It holds **Volume**, **Pan**, the track's [compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/), and **Reset**.
940	
941	There's one panel per timeline, so opening it on another track closes the first. Clicking away closes it, and so does anything that takes its track away: removing the track, undoing it away, or going into or out of a nest.
942	
943	The sliders switch is lit while the track's volume or pan is off its default, or a compressor or limiter is on.
944	
945	## Set a track's volume
946	
947	| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
948	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
949	| **Volume** | The track's level, as a slider and a field in dB. Beside them, a read-out shows the level as a percentage, or "Off". | Off (at −60) to +12 dB | 0 dB |
950	
951	The quick picks on the field are −12, −6, −3, 0, +3 and +6 dB. Drag the slider to its left end, or type −60, to turn the track off. A number typed outside the range goes to the nearest end of it.
952	
953	Track volume multiplies what's on the track. A clip at 200 % on a track at −12 dB plays at −6 dB. A muted track is silent whatever its volume.
954	
955	## Set a track's pan
956	
957	| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
958	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
959	| **Pan** | Leans the track's sound left or right, as a slider and a field. | −100 (left) to 100 (right) | 0 |
960	
961	The quick picks are −100, −50, 0, 50 and 100.
962	
963	Pan is a balance, like a [clip's pan](/audio/pan-and-mono/), and keeps the overall loudness steady as it moves. It applies after each clip's own pan, and two pans multiply, so a clip panned left on a track panned left leans further left. It has no effect on a mono source.
964	
965	## Reset the mix
966	
967	**Reset** puts the volume back to 0 dB and the pan to the centre, and turns the track's compressor and limiter off. Inside an open nest, it resets volume and pan only. It's greyed out when there's nothing to reset.
968	
969	Each change is one undo step. A drag, a typed value or a quick pick is named "Track Volume" or "Track Pan", and **Reset** is named "Reset Track Mix".
970	
971	## Track volume in a nest
972	
973	A clip inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) plays through its own track inside the nest, and through the track the nest clip sits on.
974	
975	- **Nesting from one track keeps its sound.** The nest's copy of that track starts at 0 dB and centre, because the track the nest clip lands on still applies.
976	- **Clips from the selection's other tracks** keep their own track's volume and pan inside the nest, and also get the destination track's.
977	- **Un-nesting** puts the clips back on the timeline's tracks without the nest's track settings.
978	- **Mix to mono on a nest clip** folds everything inside it, so the pans of the tracks inside no longer apply.
979	
980	## What hears track volume
981	
982	Track volume is part of what you hear, so it shows up wherever Frame Job measures the mix, and not where it measures a clip.
983	
984	| Hears it | Doesn't hear it |
985	| --- | --- |
986	| The preview and every export, which sound the same | [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) |
987	| The [level meter](/audio/level-meter/) | The [Loudness read-out](/audio/volume/#read-the-level) |
988	| [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) | A clip's [limiter](/audio/limiter/) |
989	
990	So a track turned up can take a limited clip past its ceiling. Use the track's own [limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) to hold what the whole track hands the mix.
991	
992	## Good to know
993	
994	A track's volume and pan are one value for the whole track, and can't change over time. To ride the level, use a clip's [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) or [actions](/audio/animate-sound/).
995	
996	## With an agent
997	
998	`set_track` sets both, with different scales from the panel. `volume` is a linear gain from 0 to 4, where 1 is 0 dB, 4 is +12 dB and 0 is silent. `pan` runs from −1 (left) to 1 (right). A value outside those ranges changes nothing, where a number typed in the panel goes to the nearest end. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#set_track).
999	
1000	## Related
1001	
1002	- [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/)
1003	- [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/)
1004	- [Clip volume](/audio/volume/)
1005	- [Pan and Mix to mono](/audio/pan-and-mono/)

1013	
1014	Voice Effect changes the character of a clip's sound: pitch a voice up or down, squeeze it into a phone line, or put it in a hall. A clip has one effect at a time.
1015

1	---
2	title: "Tools: clip sound (set_audio)"
3	description: "The Sound tab's settings through one agent tool: volume, fades, ducking, pan, EQ, dynamics, voice isolation and voice effects."
4	---
5	
6	`set_audio` is how an agent changes a clip's sound: its volume, fades, ducking, pan, EQ and every other control in the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/). You name the clips and send only what should change, and the rest of each clip's sound stays as it is.
7	
8	## `set_audio`
9	
10	Changes the base sound settings of one or more clips, as one undo step. Read them back with [`get_project`](/mcp/get-project/), where they're under each clip's `audio`.
11	
12	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
13	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
14	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clip ids. At least one. |
15	| `patch` | object | Yes | The settings to merge. Each key is described below. |
16	| `scope` | integer | No | Look the clips up inside this nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
17	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "clips": [12, 15],
22	  "patch": {
23	    "volume": 0.8,
24	    "eq": { "high_pass": { "frequency": 100 } },
25	    "gate": {}
26	  }
27	}
28	```
29	
30	The patch follows the rules of [Patches](/mcp/patches/):
31	
32	- A key you leave out keeps what's stored.
33	- `duck`, `compressor`, `limiter`, `eq` and each of its slots, `hum`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser` and `voice` are objects, and they merge key by key.
34	- `null` on one of those clears it, so `{"duck": null}` turns ducking off.
35	- An empty object turns `limiter`, `hum`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser` or an EQ slot on at its defaults, so `{"limiter": {}}` adds the limiter.
36	
37	**Answers** with the [project summary](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/). A patch that changes nothing answers "made no change".
38	
39	**Refuses** a key it doesn't know, naming its path, and a value out of range, naming the key and the value you sent. Nothing is clamped. A clip with no sound settings, such as a text clip, is refused by id.
40	
41	All times in the patch are ticks, 600,000 to the second.
42	
43	### Volume and mute
44	
45	| Key | Type | What it does |
46	| --- | --- | --- |
47	| `volume` | number | The clip's gain, from 0 to 32. 1 is unity. |
48	| `muted` | boolean | Mutes the clip. |
49	
50	See [Clip volume](/audio/volume/).
51	
52	### Fades and fade shapes
53	
54	| Key | Type | What it does |
55	| --- | --- | --- |
56	| `fade_in`, `fade_out` | integer | The fade's length in ticks, 0 or more. |
57	| `fade_in_shape`, `fade_out_shape` | string | The fade's curve: `linear` (the default), `s_curve`, `plus_3db` for a fast start or `minus_3db` for a slow one. |
58	
59	The shapes are the **Fades** section's **In shape** and **Out shape**. See [Audio fades](/audio/fades/).
60	
61	### Ducking
62	
63	`duck` lowers other sound while this clip plays, or only while its speech plays.
64	
65	| `duck` key | Range | Default | What it does |
66	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
67	| `level` | 0 to 1 | 0.2 | What the other sound is multiplied by. |
68	| `attack` | 0 or more ticks | 300,000 (0.5 s) | How long the sound takes to go down. |
69	| `release` | 0 or more ticks | 600,000 (1 s) | How long it takes to come back. |
70	| `mode` | `extent` or `speech` | `extent` | `extent` ducks for the clip's whole length. `speech` ducks only while its speech plays. |
71	| `pre_roll` | 0 or more ticks | 300,000 (0.5 s) | With `speech`, how far before each stretch of speech to start. |
72	| `hold` | 0 or more ticks | 300,000 (0.5 s) | With `speech`, how far after it to hold. |
73	
74	`mode: "speech"` is **Speech** in the **Ducking** section's **Duck by** pop-up. It saves the media's detected speech in the same undo step, so it needs on-device speech detection to have finished. It's an error for a clip that isn't a media clip with sound, and for one whose speech hasn't been detected yet, which says to try again in a moment. To write the speech spans yourself, use [`set_media_speech`](/mcp/tools-media/#set_media_speech).
75	
76	See [Ducking](/audio/ducking/) and [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/).
77	
78	### Mono, keep pitch, pan and channels
79	
80	| Key | Type | What it does |
81	| --- | --- | --- |
82	| `mono` | boolean | Plays the clip in mono. |
83	| `keep_pitch` | boolean | Keeps the sound's pitch at a new speed. A clip starts with this on. |
84	| `pan` | number | From −1 hard left to 1 hard right. |
85	| `channels` | string | `both` (the default), `left`, `right` or `swapped`. `left` and `right` play that channel of a stereo source from both sides, and `swapped` exchanges them. It comes after isolation and any voice effect, and a mono source ignores it. |
86	
87	See [Pan and Mix to mono](/audio/pan-and-mono/), [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) and [Channels](/audio/channels/).
88	
89	### Compressor and limiter
90	
91	| `compressor` key | Range | Default |
92	| --- | --- | --- |
93	| `threshold_db` | −60 to 0 dB | −18 |
94	| `ratio` | 1 to 20 | 3 |
95	| `attack` | 0 or more ticks | 6,000 (10 ms) |
96	| `release` | 0 or more ticks | 120,000 (200 ms) |
97	| `makeup_db` | 0 to 24 dB | 0 |
98	
99	`limiter` is a true-peak limiter, last in the clip's chain. Its ceiling holds after the clip's base volume.
100	
101	| `limiter` key | Range | Default |
102	| --- | --- | --- |
103	| `ceiling_db` | −24 to 0 dBTP | −1 |
104	| `release` | 600 to 600,000 ticks | 60,000 (100 ms) |
105	
106	See [Compressor](/audio/compressor/) and [Limiter](/audio/limiter/). A track has its own pair, set with [`set_track`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#a-tracks-compressor-and-limiter).
107	
108	### Noise reduction and voice isolation
109	
110	| Key | Range | What it does |
111	| --- | --- | --- |
112	| `noise_reduction` | 0 to 1 | Reduces noise in the clip's sound. |
113	| `isolation` | 0 to 1 | Isolates a voice with Apple's on-device model, which also reduces room echo. 0 is off, 0.8 is the app's default and 1 leaves silence between words. |
114	
115	Isolation is rendered offline. The clip plays without it until the render finishes, and an export waits for it. A clip not at ×1 plays without it.
116	
117	See [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/) and [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/).
118	
119	### EQ
120	
121	`eq` has seven slots, after the channel pick. Each slot is `null` for off, or an object.
122	
123	| Slot | Keys | Default |
124	| --- | --- | --- |
125	| `high_pass` | `frequency` 20 to 20,000 Hz, `slope` 12 or 24 dB/octave | 80 Hz, 12 |
126	| `low_shelf` | `frequency`, `gain_db` −24 to 24 dB | 100 Hz, 0 dB |
127	| `band_1`, `band_2`, `band_3` | `frequency`, `gain_db`, `q` 0.1 to 10 | 1,000 Hz, 0 dB, 1 |
128	| `high_shelf` | `frequency`, `gain_db` | 8,000 Hz, 0 dB |
129	| `low_pass` | `frequency`, `slope` | 12,000 Hz, 12 |
130	
131	`bypass: true` keeps the settings and silences them. `{"eq": {"high_pass": {}}}` turns one slot on at its defaults.
132	
133	The inspector's buttons are these moves:
134	
135	| Button | Patch |
136	| --- | --- |
137	| **Rumble Cut** | `high_pass` at 80 Hz, slope 24 |
138	| **De-mud** | `band_1` at 300 Hz, −3 dB, Q 1 |
139	| **Presence** | `band_3` at 4,000 Hz, +3 dB, Q 1 |
140	
141	See [EQ](/audio/eq/).
142	
143	### Hum removal
144	
145	`hum` notches out mains hum and its harmonics, after the EQ.
146	
147	| `hum` key | Range | Default |
148	| --- | --- | --- |
149	| `frequency` | 50 or 60 Hz | 60 |
150	| `depth_db` | 6 to 60 dB | 30 |
151	| `harmonics` | 1 to 8 | 4 |
152	
153	See [Hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/).
154	
155	### Gate
156	
157	`gate` turns the pauses down. It's a downward expander, after noise reduction. For each dB the sound falls below the threshold, the level drops by a further `ratio` − 1 dB, and never by more than `range_db` in all.
158	
159	| `gate` key | Range | Default |
160	| --- | --- | --- |
161	| `threshold_db` | −40 to 0 dB, relative to the clip's measured loudness | −10 |
162	| `ratio` | 1 to 20 | 4 |
163	| `range_db` | 1 to 80 dB | 20 |
164	| `attack` | 0 to 60,000 ticks | 600 (1 ms) |
165	| `hold` | 0 to 300,000 ticks | 30,000 (50 ms) |
166	| `release` | 600 to 1,200,000 ticks | 60,000 (100 ms) |
167	
168	The loudness it's relative to is what [`normalize_clip`](/mcp/tools-audio/#normalize_clip) reports, before the clip's volume. See [Gate](/audio/gate/).
169	
170	### Leveller
171	
172	`leveller` evens out a speaker who moves on and off the mic, after the gate. It's a gain curve made ahead of time from the clip's measured loudness and its speech, so it sounds the same in the preview and an export.
173	
174	| `leveller` key | Range | Default |
175	| --- | --- | --- |
176	| `target_db` | −20 to 10 dB, relative to the clip's loudness | 0 |
177	| `max_up_db` | 0 to 24 dB | 12 |
178	| `max_down_db` | 0 to 24 dB | 12 |
179	| `response` | 300,000 to 6,000,000 ticks | 1,200,000 (2 s) |
180	
181	Each phrase's level is brought to `target_db`, never more than the two limits. A pause holds the gain and glides to the next phrase over its last 0.25 s, and a phrase under 1 s takes its neighbour's gain.
182	
183	It waits for the clip's speech as well as its loudness. It does nothing where speech detection isn't available or no phrase has 1 s of speech. See [Leveller](/audio/leveller/).
184	
185	### De-esser
186	
187	`de_esser` comes after the leveller. It turns the band above `frequency` down on sibilance and never boosts it.
188	
189	| `de_esser` key | Range | Default |
190	| --- | --- | --- |
191	| `frequency` | 2,000 to 12,000 Hz | 6,000 |
192	| `threshold_db` | −30 to 20 dB, relative to the clip's loudness | 0 |
193	| `range_db` | 1 to 24 dB | 6 |
194	
195	The gate, leveller and de-esser act only once the clip's loudness is measured. Until then the clip plays without them, and an export waits. A clip too short or too quiet to measure plays without them, and on a nest clip they do nothing. See [De-esser](/audio/de-esser/).
196	
197	### Voice effects
198	
199	`voice` replaces the clip's sound with a rendered effect, after isolation and before the channel pick.
200	
201	| `voice` key | Range | Default | What it does |
202	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
203	| `kind` | See below | None | Which effect. Needed when the clip has no voice effect yet. |
204	| `amount` | 0 to 1 | 1 | How much of the effect. 0 plays the clip dry. |
205	| `pitch` | −12 to 12 semitones | The kind's own: 0 for `pitch`, +5 for `high`, −5 for `deep` | Read only by `pitch`, `high` and `deep`. |
206	
207	| Group | Kinds |
208	| --- | --- |
209	| Voice | `pitch`, `high`, `deep`, `robot` |
210	| Tone | `bass`, `treble`, `bright`, `telephone`, `radio` |
211	| Character | `lofi`, `distorted` |
212	| Space | `echo`, `room`, `hall`, `plate`, `cathedral` |
213	
214	A new `kind` keeps a stored `pitch` unless you send `pitch: null` with it. `{"voice": null}` clears the effect.
215	
216	The clip plays without the effect until its render finishes, and an export waits for it. A clip not at ×1 plays without it, and reverb and echo tails end with the clip. See [Voice effects](/audio/voice-effects/).
217	
218	## Animate sound
219	
220	`set_audio` sets the clip's base values. To change one over time, use an action's `set_action_end`. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/) and [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/).
221	
222	Volume, mute, the fades, `pan`, `mono`, `channels`, `eq`, `hum`, `noise_reduction`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser`, `compressor`, `limiter` and `isolation` can all animate. `duck`, `keep_pitch`, the fade shapes and `voice` can't, and only `set_audio` sets them.

232	title: "Tools: audio"
233	description: "The agent tools that detach and attach a clip's sound, normalise it, set it up for speech, match it to a reference and line clips up by their sound."
234	---
235	
236	These tools work on a clip's sound as a whole: split it off, set its level, set it up for speech, match it to another clip, or line clips up by what they hear. For single settings, use [`set_audio`](/mcp/tools-set-audio/).
237	
238	`normalize_clip`, `enhance_voice`, `match_audio` and `sync_audio` measure sound, so they share three things:
239	
240	- **They take no `scope`.** They work in whatever nest `set_scope` has open. To work inside a nest, open it first. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
241	- **They can take seconds**, and longer on a long clip. `enhance_voice` and `match_audio` render a clip to measure it, and so does `normalize_clip`'s loudness mode for a clip with processing.
242	- **They give up if the project changes meanwhile.** Nothing changes, and the answer says to call again.
243	
244	All four are one undo step, and a second identical call changes nothing.
245	
246	## `detach_audio`
247	
248	Splits a clip's sound onto its own clip on the track below. It's **Clip ▸ Detach Audio** (<kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd>), see [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
249	
250	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
251	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
252	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
253	| `scope` | integer | No | Look the clip up inside this nest. |
254	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
255	
256	The original keeps its picture with its audio switched off. The new clip plays the sound with its video switched off. When the clip is on the bottom track, a new track is added under it.
257	
258	The two are linked, and each names the other under `linked`. Moves, splits, ripples, nests and copies keep them in step. To make a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/), use `trim_start` or `trim_end` with `alone: true` on the sound. Speed and reverse edits are refused until [`attach_audio`](#attach_audio).
259	
260	**Answers** with `new_clips` and, when one was added, `new_tracks`, then the [project summary](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
261	
262	**Refuses**, saying why, a clip that isn't a media clip, media with no audio, a clip whose audio is off (which is also what an already detached clip reads as), and a sound clip that would overlap a clip on the track below.
263	
264	## `attach_audio`
265	
266	Merges a detached pair back into one clip. It's **Clip ▸ Attach Audio** (<kbd>⇧⌥⌘D</kbd>), see [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
267	
268	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
269	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
270	| `clip` | integer | Yes | Either half of the pair. |
271	| `scope` | integer | No | Look the clip up inside this nest. |
272	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
273	
274	The picture's audio comes back on with the sound clip's audio settings, and the sound clip goes. Its track stays.
275	
276	**Answers** with the project summary.
277	
278	**Refuses** a clip that isn't linked, and a pair that no longer covers the same time, such as a J-cut or L-cut. Trim them to match first.
279	
280	## `normalize_clip`
281	
282	Sets each clip's volume so its loudness, or its loudest moment, lands on a target. It's the **Normalize** button in the Clip tab's **Volume** section and **Clip ▸ Normalize**, see [Normalize](/audio/normalize/). Those follow the mode chosen in the section's **Normalize** row. The tool doesn't read that row: it goes by its own `mode`.
283	
284	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
285	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
286	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clip ids. At least one. |
287	| `mode` | string | No | `loudness` takes each clip's integrated loudness to `target_lufs`, under a −1 dBTP ceiling. `peak` takes each clip's loudest moment to `peak_db`. Default: `loudness`, or `peak` when you give `peak_db` and no mode. |
288	| `target_lufs` | number | No | Loudness mode only. The loudness to land at, −50 to −5 LUFS. Default: −16. −14 is YouTube's playback reference and −23 is EBU R 128's. |
289	| `peak_db` | number | No | Peak mode only. Where the loudest moment lands, −60 to 0 dBFS. Default: −1, which is what the button uses in Peak mode. |
290	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
291	
292	The level is measured before the clip's fader, over the part of the clip that plays. It knows nothing of the volume, fades, ducking, mute or solo already on the clip, because it's about the material, not the mix. Loudness is measured to BS.1770-4, gated, as the export plays the clip: a mono clip as dual mono, a stereo clip through its own mono and pan. That has three results:
293	
294	- It **replaces** the volume rather than multiplying it, so a second call answers "made no change".
295	- It writes the clip's base volume, even with the playhead inside an action.
296	- It leaves `muted` alone.
297	
298	In peak mode each clip gets its own gain to the same peak, so levels aren't matched across a selection. In loudness mode each clip goes to the one target, which does match them.
299	
300	The volume can't go past 32×, so a clip quieter than about −31 dBFS can't reach −1. It's still normalised as far as it goes, and the answer says where it landed.
301	
302	In loudness mode:
303	
304	- A clip whose true peak would pass −1 dBTP at the target, or that already has a limiter, gets the clip's [limiter](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#compressor-and-limiter) in the same edit. Its own is kept with the ceiling at −1 dBTP at most, otherwise it's the default.
305	- A clip with an active EQ, hum notch, voice isolation, noise reduction, gate, leveller, de-esser, compressor or voice effect is measured through that processing, rendered offline as the export plays it. It waits for any isolation or voice render.
306	- A worked-out volume within 0.05 dB of the clip's own is kept, so a second call still changes nothing.
307	
308	**Answers**, in peak mode, `peak_db` and a `normalized` list:
309	
310	| Key | What it says |
311	| --- | --- |
312	| `clip`, `media` | Which clip and file. |
313	| `measured_db` | The clip's measured peak. |
314	| `volume` | The volume written. |
315	| `result_db` | Where the peak lands. |
316	| `clamped` | True when the 32× ceiling stopped it short. |
317	
318	**Answers**, in loudness mode, `target_lufs`, `ceiling_dbtp` and a `normalized` list:
319	
320	| Key | What it says |
321	| --- | --- |
322	| `clip`, `media` | Which clip and file. |
323	| `measured_lufs`, `true_peak_dbtp` | The **Volume** section's Loudness readout. For a rendered clip the true peak is the processed one. |
324	| `processed_lufs` | The loudness through the clip's processing. `null` for a clip measured without a render. |
325	| `renders` | The renders it took. 0 for a clip measured without one. |
326	| `volume` | The volume written. |
327	| `limiter` | The clip's limiter after the edit, or `null` for a volume alone. |
328	| `result_lufs` | Where the clip lands. |
329	| `result_true_peak_dbtp` | Its true peak after the edit, held at the limiter's ceiling. |
330	| `limited_by` | `max_gain` when the volume ceiling stopped it short, otherwise `null`. |
331	
332	Either mode adds `skipped`, one sentence per clip it left out, and `note` when the ceiling stopped a clip short. The rest are still normalised.
333	
334	**Skips** by name a clip that plays no sound and a nest. Peak mode also skips one that's silent over the part that plays, or whose waveform hasn't been analysed yet. Loudness mode also skips one that plays under 0.4 s, is under −70 LUFS over the part that plays, or whose loudness hasn't been measured yet. In loudness mode a clip with processing is also skipped when its reversed copy is still being made, its processing can't be rendered, or it's under −70 LUFS after it. When every clip is skipped, the call fails with "Nothing could be normalised" and every reason.
335	
336	**Refuses** a `target_lufs` or `peak_db` out of range, and either one in the other's mode. Neither is clamped.
337	
338	## `enhance_voice`
339	
340	Sets each clip up for speech from its own measurements. It's **Clip ▸ Enhance Voice** and the **Enhance Voice** button in the Clip tab's **Volume** section, see [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/). Those use the **Normalize** row's target and show the Measuring Sound sheet while they work.
341	
342	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
343	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
344	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clip ids. At least one. |
345	| `target_lufs` | number | No | The loudness each clip should land at, −50 to −5 LUFS. Default: −16. −14 is YouTube's playback reference and −23 is EBU R 128's. |
346	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
347	
348	Speech detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload.
349	
350	It measures the clip before any of its settings, then writes ordinary settings you can see and change in each section:
351	
352	| Setting | When | What it sets |
353	| --- | --- | --- |
354	| EQ | Always | The **Rumble Cut** high-pass, 80 Hz at 24 dB/octave. The EQ's other slots stay. |
355	| Voice isolation and gate | When the pauses' floor is less than 45 dB under the clip's loudness | Isolation at 0.8, or noise reduction at 0.5 where isolation can't serve the clip (a speed other than 1, a ramp or a freeze). The gate opens 10 dB above the pauses' median true peak, held to −40 to −6 relative to the loudness. With quiet pauses all three are off, and with under 0.5 s of pause they're left as they are. |
356	| Leveller | When the speech's short-term loudness range is over 6 LU | The leveller at its defaults, otherwise off. With under 3 s of speech it's left as it is. |
357	| De-esser | When at least 5% of the speech has its 6 kHz band within 10 dB of the loudness | The de-esser at its defaults, otherwise off. |
358	| Compressor | Always | 3:1 at the speech's median true peak, with makeup that gives back what it takes. |
359	| Limiter | Always | The clip's own, with its ceiling at −1 dBTP at most, otherwise the default. |
360	| Volume | Always | What takes the clip to `target_lufs`, worked out on the clip rendered through these settings. |
361	
362	It overwrites only `eq`, `isolation`, `noise_reduction`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser`, `compressor`, `limiter` and `volume`. Hum, channels, pan, mono, fades, ducking and mute stay. It writes base settings even with the playhead inside an action.
363	
364	[`normalize_clip`](#normalize_clip) at the same target afterwards changes nothing, because it measures a processed clip the same way.
365	
366	**Answers** `target_lufs`, `ceiling_dbtp` and an `enhanced` list:
367	
368	| Key | What it says |
369	| --- | --- |
370	| `clip`, `media` | Which clip and file. |
371	| `measured_lufs`, `true_peak_dbtp` | The clip's loudness and true peak, before its settings. |
372	| `speech_seconds` | How much speech it found. |
373	| `floor_lufs`, `floor_gap_db`, `pause_peak_dbfs` | The pauses' floor, its gap under the loudness, and their median true peak. |
374	| `sibilance_share` | The share of the speech that's sibilant. |
375	| `speech_range_lu` | The speech's short-term loudness range. `null` under 3 s of speech. |
376	| `set` | Exactly the keys written, in `set_audio`'s spelling. |
377	| `reasons` | One sentence per rule: the measurement, the threshold and what it set. |
378	| `volume`, `processed_lufs`, `renders` | The volume written, the loudness through the new settings before it, and the renders it took. |
379	| `result_lufs`, `result_true_peak_dbtp`, `limited_by` | Where the last render lands, and `max_gain` when the volume ceiling stopped it short. |
380	
381	It adds `skipped` and `note` as `normalize_clip` does. A second call answers "Enhance Voice made no change".
382	
383	**Skips** by name a clip that plays no sound, is a nest, plays under 0.4 s, is under −70 LUFS, or has under 1 s of speech. So too a clip whose loudness or speech hasn't been analysed yet, whose reversed copy is still being made, whose processing can't be rendered, or that's under −70 LUFS after its processing. When every clip is skipped, the call fails with "Nothing could be enhanced" and every reason.
384	
385	**Refuses** a `target_lufs` out of range. It isn't clamped.
386	
387	## `match_audio`
388	
389	Gives clips the loudness and speech tone of a reference clip. It's **Clip ▸ Match Audio…**, see [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/), whose sheet picks the reference among the selected clips and has a **Loudness** and an **EQ** box.
390	
391	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
392	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
393	| `reference` | integer | Yes | The clip whose loudness and tone the others take. It isn't changed. |
394	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to change. At least one. |
395	| `loudness` | boolean | No | Match the loudness, through the volume and limiter. Default: true. |
396	| `eq` | boolean | No | Match the tone, through the EQ's shelves and bands. Default: true. |
397	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
398	
399	Speech detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload.
400	
401	The reference is rendered once as it plays, with its settings, limiter and volume but no fades, ducks or mute, and its loudness is read.
402	
403	**Loudness** is [`normalize_clip`](#normalize_clip)'s loudness mode at that target for every clip. It sets the volume, and the limiter when the peaks need it, worked out on the clip rendered through its new settings.
404	
405	**EQ** renders each clip with its shelves and bands off, keeping its high- and low-pass. Both clips' average spectra are measured over their speech only, needing about 1 s of it, in 23 third-octave bands from 79 Hz to 12.7 kHz. The difference between them, with the overall level taken out, is fitted by the EQ's low shelf, three bands and high shelf, with gains within ±12 dB and Q from 0.5 to 4. A band is used only where the difference is at least 0.5 dB. These replace the clip's own five, its high- and low-pass and hum stay, and `bypass` goes off.
406	
407	It writes only `volume`, `limiter` and `eq`, as base settings even inside an action.
408	
409	**Answers** `reference` (its `clip`, `media`, `lufs` and `speech_seconds`), `target_lufs` and a `matched` list:
410	
411	| Key | What it says |
412	| --- | --- |
413	| `clip`, `media` | Which clip and file. |
414	| `set` | Exactly the keys written. |
415	| `eq`, `eq_fit_rms_db` | The fitted EQ, and how far it is from the difference in dB RMS. |
416	| `volume`, `measured_lufs`, `processed_lufs`, `result_lufs`, `result_true_peak_dbtp`, `limited_by` | The same figures as `normalize_clip`. |
417	| `renders` | The renders it took. |
418	
419	It adds `skipped` and `note` as `normalize_clip` does. A second call answers "Match Audio made no change".
420	
421	**Refuses** a call with `loudness` and `eq` both false, and a reference that plays no sound, is a nest, plays under 0.4 s, is under −70 LUFS, hasn't been analysed yet or, with `eq`, has under 1 s of speech.
422	
423	**Skips** a clip that can't be matched for one of those reasons, or that is the reference. The rest are still matched.
424	
425	## `sync_audio`
426	
427	Lines clips up by their sound. One clip, the anchor, stays where it is. Every other clip moves along its own track by a whole number of frames, so its sound plays at the same moment as the anchor's. It's **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**, see [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/).
428	
429	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
430	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
431	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to line up. At least two, each on its own track. |
432	| `anchor` | integer | No | The clip that stays put, one of `clips`. Default: among the clips with pictures (all of them when none has), the earliest start, then the rearmost track, then the lowest id. |
433	| `accept_weak` | boolean | No | Apply a weak match. Default: false. |
434	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
435	
436	The matching runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload. The menu item leaves out a nest or a clip that plays no sound, where the tool stops and names it.
437	
438	### How a match is chosen
439	
440	Each file's sound is compared on features that ignore gain, microphone and room. When both stretches hold at least 2 s of speech, only their speech is compared. The clips' played windows are searched first, and the whole files only when that chooses nothing and a clip is trimmed.
441	
442	- A **confident** match has a confidence of at least 10 and is 1.5 above the next candidate.
443	- A **weak** match is the best peak within 3 s of where the clip already sits, with a confidence of at least 4.
444	
445	Either kind must then pass a check on the waveforms, which needs a clear peak, with a confidence of at least 15, within ±48 ms. A match that fails it is refused as not one recording, because features alone can match two takes of similar words.
446	
447	See [Confident and weak matches](/audio/weak-sync-matches/).
448	
449	### Apply a weak match
450	
451	A weak match that would move anything isn't applied. The answer is `moved: false`, with `weak` naming the clips, each row's move and a `note`, and nothing changes.
452	
453	:::caution
454	Pass `accept_weak: true` only after the person has agreed to that move, naming it. A weak match can be unrelated sound.
455	:::
456	
457	### What it does to a clip
458	
459	- **A clip that would start before 0** is trimmed at its head by that much and starts at 0. The anchor never moves or trims.
460	- **Clock drift** between the two recordings is measured over at least 60 s of overlap and corrected with a tiny speed change, as a resample. It's left alone when it's under 5 ms, under 3× its uncertainty, or would need a speed more than 0.2% from ×1, and `drift_note` says why.
461	
462	### What it answers
463	
464	An answer that isn't a refusal has `anchor`, `moved`, `weak` (the clip ids of weak moves) and a `synced` list. A second call answers `moved: false` and "already in sync".
465	
466	| Key | What it says |
467	| --- | --- |
468	| `clip`, `media` | Which clip and file. |
469	| `offset` | Anchor source minus clip source at the overlap's centre, refined, in ticks. |
470	| `coarse_offset` | The match before the waveform refinement. |
471	| `refined`, `refine_confidence` | `phat` when the waveform check refined it, otherwise `coarse`, and that check's confidence, or `null` when none ran. |
472	| `delta`, `start` | How far the clip moves, and its new start. |
473	| `confidence` | How strong the chosen match is. |
474	| `search` | `played` or `whole`. |
475	| `chosen_by` | `confidence`, or `placement` for the weak tier. |
476	| `matched_on` | `speech` or `sound`. |
477	| `candidates` | Each search's candidates, as `offset`, `delta` and `confidence`. |
478	| `trimmed` | The ticks cut off its head, 0 when none. |
479	| `speed` | The clip's speed after the call. |
480	| `drift_ppm`, `drift_ms`, `drift_error_ms` | The drift measured and its uncertainty. |
481	| `drift_on`, `drift_windows` | `features` or `phat`, the points the drift line went through, and how many windows it used. |
482	| `drift_corrected`, `residual_ms`, `drift_note` | Whether it was corrected, the error left, and why not. |
483	
484	### When it refuses
485	
486	It's all or nothing: when any clip can't be matched, nothing moves and every reason is named. When no match is chosen, the message gives each search's candidates as the move each would make and its confidence, so you can move the clip near one and call again.
487	
488	A clip can't be matched when it:
489	
490	- is a nest, or plays no sound
491	- is still being analysed
492	- holds under 2 s of sound
493	- plays more than 0.2% away from ×1, plays at a rate other than its speed, plays reversed, or has a speed ramp
494	- shares a track with another of the clips
495	- would be left with under a frame after its head trim
496	- would never play beside the anchor, or would overlap another clip on its track
497	
498	`anchor` must be one of `clips`.

516	
517	Every clip with sound is mixed by its own settings and then by its track's. This page is the map: where sound lives, the order it's processed in, and which page covers each job.
518	
519	<AtAGlance
520	  where={['The timeline', 'Clip tab ▸ Sound', 'The track header']}
521	  tools={['set_audio', 'set_track']}
522	/>
523	
524	## One kind of track for all sound
525	
526	Frame Job has no separate audio tracks. Any track can hold a clip with sound:
527	
528	- a video file
529	- an audio-only file, such as a voice-over, music or a recorder's take
530	- a microphone recording
531	- a clip split off with [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/)
532	- a [nest](/editing/nests/) that holds sound
533	
534	Each clip has its own processing on the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/). Each track can be [muted or soloed](/audio/mute-and-solo/) and has its own [volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/), [compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/).
535	
536	The preview and the export use the same mix, so what you hear while editing is what gets written. There are two exceptions:
537	
538	- The exported mix also passes through a master limiter the preview doesn't have, which holds its peaks under −1 dBTP unless an agent asks for another ceiling. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/).
539	- A track's compressor and limiter are exact in an export and approximate in the preview. See [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/).
540	
541	## Clip waveforms
542	
543	A clip with sound shows its waveform in the timeline, below the filmstrip when it has both. The waveform is the file's own level, so moving the **Volume** slider doesn't redraw it. The [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) over it shows what you actually hear. A nest clip draws no waveform, because it has no file of its own.
544	
545	The waveform is drawn faded when the clip is muted, when its track is muted, or when another track's solo silences it. A track holding only sound clips is drawn as a shorter lane than a track with pictures. [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/) covers everything a clip draws.
546	
547	## The fixed signal order
548	
549	Sound passes through a clip's settings in one fixed order. You can't rearrange it. The order matters because each stage hears what the one before it left: the compressor's threshold, for example, is read against sound the noise reducer has already cleaned.
550	
551	1. [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/)
552	2. [Voice Effect](/audio/voice-effects/)
553	3. [Channels](/audio/channels/)
554	4. [EQ](/audio/eq/)
555	5. [Hum](/audio/hum-removal/)
556	6. [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/)
557	7. [Gate](/audio/gate/)
558	8. [Leveller](/audio/leveller/)
559	9. [De-esser](/audio/de-esser/)
560	10. [Compressor](/audio/compressor/)
561	11. [Mix](/audio/pan-and-mono/): Mix to mono, then Pan
562	12. [Limiter](/audio/limiter/)
563	13. [Volume](/audio/volume/), [fades](/audio/fades/) and [ducking](/audio/ducking/)
564	
565	The last step works like a fader. Those three are the first sections on the Sound tab, because they're what you reach for most, but they're applied last. The other sections read down the tab in signal order.
566	
567	The limiter takes the clip's **Volume** into account, so its ceiling holds at the level you set, even though Volume comes after it in the list.
568	
569	## Sound on a nest
570	
571	A nest clip has the same Sound tab, but most of the controls don't reach the clips inside it.
572	
573	| On a nest clip | What it does |
574	| --- | --- |
575	| **Volume**, **Mute** and the fades | Scale everything inside. Turning a nest down turns all of it down, and muting it silences all of it. |
576	| **Mix to mono** | Folds the nest's whole mix. Pans on the tracks inside it no longer apply. |
577	| **Ducking** | Lowers the rest of the project for the nest's whole length. |
578	| Pan, Channels, EQ, Hum, Gate, Leveller, De-esser, Compressor, Voice Isolation, Voice Effect, Noise Reduction and Limiter | Nothing. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set them on the clips inside. |
579	
580	A nest clip draws no [volume line](/audio/volume-line/), and [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) and [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) pass over it, because its level lives in the clips inside. Alone in the selection it leaves both buttons disabled. Beside an ordinary clip, the ordinary clip is processed and the nest is skipped.
581	
582	## What a track adds
583	
584	A track acts as a bus, one shared channel for all its clips. Its volume, compressor and limiter work on everything on it, after each clip's own settings. Its pan works on everything on it too, right before each clip's Limiter, so a limited clip still holds its ceiling.
585	
586	A clip inside a nest plays through its own track in the nest and then through the track the nest clip sits on. Track volumes and pans multiply along the way, so a clip panned left on a track panned left leans further left. A nest's own tracks have no compressor or limiter, only volume and pan.
587	
588	## Sound analysis after import
589	
590	Frame Job analyses each file's sound on your Mac after import, with no key and no upload: first its waveform, then its loudness, then what Synchronize Audio matches on, and then where its speech is. Until that finishes:
591	
592	- The clip has no waveform yet.
593	- The **Loudness** read-out says "measuring…".
594	- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) and [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) skip the clip.
595	- [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) skips it, and if that leaves nothing to match, it says the clip "is still being analysed".
596	- [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) stops and says the clip "is still being analysed".
597	
598	Try again in a moment. Nothing needs starting by hand.
599	
600	## Find the right tool
601	
602	| To | Use |
603	| --- | --- |
604	| Set how loud a clip plays | [Clip volume](/audio/volume/) |
605	| Change the level over time | [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/) or [actions](/audio/animate-sound/) |
606	| Bring clips to one loudness | [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) |
607	| Clean up a voice recording in one step | [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) |
608	| Make one clip sound like another | [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) |
609	| Drop the music under a voice | [Ducking](/audio/ducking/) or [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/) |

611	| Move sound to its own clip, or make a J-cut | [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/), [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/) |
612	| Give many clips the same treatment | [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) copies the whole sound setup in one step |

614	| Check a mix by ear and by number | [The level meter](/audio/level-meter/) and [the Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/) |

640	## When the tab appears
641	
642	The Clip tab shows **Sound** when the selection includes at least one clip that plays sound. That means a clip whose file has an audio track with its sound switched on, or a nest that holds audio. A clip whose sound is [switched off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/) doesn't count.
643	
644	Click a clip on the timeline and the inspector moves to the **Clip** tab. An audio-only clip has no picture, so the tab opens straight on Sound. For a video clip, choose the **Sound** sub-tab.
645	
646	## The sections
647	
648	Each section header shows a one-line summary of its state, so you can read a clip's setup with every section closed. The summary is drawn a little stronger when the section differs from its default.
649	
650	| Section | What it's for | Its summary reads | **Reset** does |
651	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
652	| [Volume](/audio/volume/) | Level, read-outs, Mute, Normalize and Enhance Voice | "muted", "silent" at 0 %, or the gain, such as "+3.5 dB" | Volume to 100 %, Mute off |
653	| [Fades](/audio/fades/) | Fade in and fade out | Both lengths, such as "0.50 · 1.00 s", or "none" | Both lengths to 0 |
654	| [Ducking](/audio/ducking/) | Lowers every other clip while this one plays | The level, such as "20%", or "off" | Turns it off |
655	| [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) | Keeps the voice, removes what's around it | The amount, such as "80%", or "off" | Turns it off |
656	| [Voice Effect](/audio/voice-effects/) | One of sixteen effects | The effect and amount, such as "Space: Hall 100%", or "off" | Turns it off |
657	| [Channels](/audio/channels/) | Which channels of a stereo file play | "Both", "Left Only", "Right Only" or "Swap Left and Right" | Back to Both |
658	| [EQ](/audio/eq/) | Shapes the tone | Parts switched on, such as "2 on", "bypassed", or "off" | Turns it off |
659	| [Hum](/audio/hum-removal/) | Removes mains hum and its harmonics | The mains and harmonics, such as "60 Hz · 4", or "off" | Turns it off |
660	| [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/) | Lowers steady background noise | The amount, such as "50%", or "off" | Turns it off |
661	| [Gate](/audio/gate/) | Turns the pauses between phrases down | The threshold, such as "−10 dB", or "off" | Turns it off |
662	| [Leveller](/audio/leveller/) | Evens out a speaker who moves on and off the mic | The target, such as "0 dB", or "off" | Turns it off |
663	| [De-esser](/audio/de-esser/) | Tames harsh "s" sounds | The frequency, such as "6.0 kHz", or "off" | Turns it off |
664	| [Compressor](/audio/compressor/) | Smooths the volume | The ratio, such as "3.0:1", or "off" | Turns it off |
665	| [Mix](/audio/pan-and-mono/) | Pan, Mix to mono, Detach Audio and Attach Audio | "centre", "mono", or the pan, such as "left 40" | Pan to centre, Mix to mono off |
666	| [Limiter](/audio/limiter/) | Holds the clip's peaks under a ceiling | The ceiling, such as "−1.0 dBTP", or "off" | Turns it off |
667	
668	Voice Isolation through Limiter are in the order sound passes through them. Volume, the fades and ducking apply last, like a fader. See [The fixed signal order](/audio/how-audio-works/#the-fixed-signal-order).
669	
670	Click a header to open or close its section. Every section starts closed, and Frame Job remembers what you open and close. If the tab would show nothing but closed headers, the first section you haven't closed yourself opens.
671	
672	## Reset a section
673	
674	Each header has a **Reset** button that appears when the section differs from its default. It's one undo step, and it reaches every selected clip.
675	
676	Two resets leave something behind:
677	
678	- **Reset** on Fades clears the two lengths and keeps **In shape** and **Out shape**.
679	- **Reset** on Volume leaves the Limiter alone, even one that Normalize turned on.
680	
681	With an [action selected](/motion/select-an-action/), a section that can animate shows **Clear** in the same place, while the action sets something in it. **Clear** removes the section from the action. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
682	
683	## Pick a common value
684	
685	Most number fields have a chevron at their right end that opens a short menu of common values, beside the slider and the typed field. The current value is ticked. For example:
686	
687	| Control | Quick picks |
688	| --- | --- |
689	| **Volume** | 0, 50, 100, 150, 200, 400 % |
690	| **Fade in** and **Fade out** | 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2 s |
691	| **Limiter** ▸ **Ceiling** | −1, −2, −3, −6 dBTP |
692	
693	A number you type is held to the control's range. See [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/).
694	
695	## Edit several clips at once
696	
697	Select the clips and change a control. The change goes to every selected clip that has sound, as one undo step. A control whose clips hold different values is marked **mixed**.
698	
699	The sections with a tick box, such as Ducking and Compressor, work as one unit. Changing one of their controls gives every selected clip all of that section's values as the first clip has them, not only the value you changed.
700	
701	**Normalize** and **Enhance Voice** are the exceptions to one shared change. Each clip gets its own settings from its own measurement. The **Loudness** and **At volume** read-outs show "—" with several clips selected, because they describe one clip.
702	
703	## With an agent
704	
705	`set_audio` changes any of these settings on one or more clips in one call, and `get_project` reads them back. An agent sends only what should change, and everything else stays as it is. A value out of range is turned down with a message naming it, not adjusted to fit. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/).
706	
707	`set_audio` always writes the clip's own settings. To [animate one](/audio/animate-sound/), an agent uses an action instead.
708

733	## Set the volume
734	
735	Select the clip and open the **Volume** section. Drag the **Volume** slider, type in its field, or choose a value from the field's chevron: 0, 50, 100, 150, 200 or 400 %.
736	
737	| Control | Default | Range |
738	| --- | --- | --- |
739	| **Volume** | 100 % | 0 to 3200 % (+30.1 dB) |
740	
741	The slider stops at 400 %. To go higher, type in the field, up to 3200 %. Above 400 % the slider's knob stays at the right end. The high ceiling is there so that a quiet microphone recording can be brought up.
742	
743	To change the level partway through a clip, [add a point](/audio/volume-line/#add-a-point) on the volume line. With an [action selected](/audio/animate-sound/), **Volume** writes the level the action ends on, not the clip's own.
744	
745	## Mute a clip
746	
747	Tick **Mute** to silence the clip without changing its volume. It's off by default.
748	
749	A muted clip's waveform is drawn faded and its [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) lies along the bottom. To silence a whole track, use [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/).
750	
751	With an action selected, **Mute** switches at the action's end, and the row shows "at end".
752	
753	## Read the level
754	
755	Three rows report the clip's level. You can't edit them.
756	
757	### Gain
758	
759	**Gain** is the **Volume** in decibels, such as "+3.0 dB", or "silent" at 0 %. At 100 % it reads "+0.0 dB".
760	
761	### Loudness
762	
763	**Loudness** is the clip's integrated loudness and true peak at volume 100 %, such as "−41.7 LUFS · −18.5 dBTP". It's measured to BS.1770-4 over the part of the file the clip plays.
764	
765	On a stereo file, the reading includes the channel choice, Mix to mono and Pan. A mono clip counts as dual mono, as an export plays it, which reads about 3 dB louder than the file alone.
766	
767	It leaves out **Volume**, fades, ducking, **Mute** and solo, the track's volume, and EQ, Hum and the rest of the clip's processing.
768	
769	A clip at another speed, or a ramped one, reads within about 0.5 LU of what plays. A file with more than two channels is measured from a two-channel mix of it.
770	
771	### At volume
772	
773	**At volume** is the same reading with the clip's **Volume** applied, and through its [Limiter](/audio/limiter/) when that's on. With the limiter on, the true peak reads no higher than the ceiling. The row follows a **Volume** drag as you move.
774	
775	The fast reading can't hear EQ, Hum, Voice Isolation, Noise Reduction, the Gate, the Leveller, the De-esser, the Compressor or a Voice Effect. On a clip using any of them:
776	
777	- If [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode or [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) has measured the clip as it is now, the row reads that measurement.
778	- Otherwise the figure is the one before the processing and starts with "≈". Its tooltip says so.
779	
780	**At volume** doesn't measure on its own, so "≈" stays until you press one of those two.
781	
782	### What the read-outs can show instead
783	
784	| It reads | Because |
785	| --- | --- |
786	| "measuring…" | The clip's [sound analysis](/audio/how-audio-works/#sound-analysis-after-import) hasn't finished. |
787	| "—" | Several clips are selected, or a nest is, or the clip can't be measured. |
788	| "— LUFS" beside a peak | The clip plays for under 0.4 s, or it's quieter than −70 LUFS throughout. |
789	| "silent" (At volume) | **Volume** is 0 %. |
790	
791	## Reset the section
792	
793	**Reset** in the section's header puts **Volume** back to 100 % and turns **Mute** off. It leaves the Normalize row alone, and it leaves the [Limiter](/audio/limiter/) alone, including one Normalize turned on.
794	
795	## Good to know
796	
797	- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) and [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) sit at the bottom of this section. Both set **Volume** for you, and both leave **Mute** alone.
798	- On a [nest clip](/audio/how-audio-works/#sound-on-a-nest), **Volume** and **Mute** scale everything inside it.
799	- A muted clip that ducks still lowers the others. See [Ducking](/audio/ducking/).

830	## Normalize a clip
831	
832	<Steps>
833	
834	1. Select one or more clips.
835	
836	2. On the **Sound** sub-tab, open the **Volume** section and check the **Normalize** row: the mode, and in Loudness mode the target.
837	
838	3. Press **Normalize**, or choose **Clip ▸ Normalize**. The two do the same thing and follow that row. There's no keyboard shortcut.
839	
840	</Steps>
841	
842	However many clips are selected, it's one undo step, named "Normalize". That step also takes back any limiter it turned on.
843	
844	It replaces the clip's volume rather than adding to it, so pressing it a second time changes nothing, and that second press beeps. **Mute** is left as it is.
845	
846	## Choose a mode
847	
848	The first control in the **Normalize** row picks what Normalize aims at.
849	
850	| Mode | What it aims at | Matches clips? |
851	| --- | --- | --- |
852	| **Peak** | Each clip's loudest moment reaches −1 dBFS. | No |
853	| **Loudness** | Each clip's overall loudness reaches the target, −16 LUFS unless you choose another. This is the default. | Yes |
854	
855	The mode and the target belong to the app, not the project. They're kept between launches, and changing them isn't an undo step.
856	
857	## Set the loudness target
858	
859	The field beside the mode sets the level in LUFS, from −50 to −5. The default is −16, and it's only live in Loudness mode. The quick picks are:
860	
861	| Target | What it's for |
862	| --- | --- |
863	| −14 LUFS | YouTube's playback reference |
864	| −16 LUFS | The default |
865	| −23 LUFS | The EBU R 128 broadcast level |
866	
867	[Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) aims at the same target, and the [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/) draws it as a line.
868	
869	## Loudness mode
870	
871	Loudness mode sets each clip's volume so its integrated loudness reaches the target. That's the BS.1770 measure of the clip as a whole, as the export plays it, in LUFS, the unit of loudness. The volume can go down as well as up.
872	
873	- **It watches the peaks.** A clip whose true peak would pass −1 dBTP at that volume gets its [Limiter](/audio/limiter/) turned on at −1 dBTP in the same step, and the volume is the one that reaches the target through the limiter.
874	- **It keeps a limiter you set.** A clip that already has one keeps it, with its ceiling lowered to −1 dBTP if it was higher.
875	- **It stops at 3200 %.** A clip that would need more stops there and lands quieter than the target.
876	
877	## Peak mode
878	
879	Peak mode sets each clip's volume so its loudest moment reaches −1 dBFS. The level is fixed, and it happens at once, with no sheet. It reads the file's waveform, so the clip's EQ, clean-up and other processing don't count.
880	
881	Each clip gets its own gain, so levels don't match across a selection: a sparse voice still sounds quieter than a dense one. A clip whose peak is quieter than about −31 dBFS can't reach −1 dBFS. It's turned up to 3200 % and stops there.
882	
883	## What Normalize measures
884	
885	Normalize measures the clip, not the mix. It reads the clip's waveform (Peak) or loudness analysis (Loudness) over the part of the file that actually plays, so a trimmed clip is measured on what's left.
886	
887	The clip's volume, fades, ducking, mute and solo don't affect the reading, and neither do its track's volume and pan. In Loudness mode, the clip's own **Channels**, **Mix to mono** and **Pan** do count on a stereo clip. A mono clip is measured on both channels, as the export plays it, which reads 3 dB louder than the file on its own.
888	
889	## Measure through a clip's processing
890	
891	Cleaning up a clip changes how loud it measures, so the analysis alone would miss the target. In Loudness mode, a clip with any of these is rendered through them as the export plays it, and its volume is set from what comes out:
892	
893	- An active [EQ](/audio/eq/)

18	## Animate a sound setting
19	
20	<Steps>
21	
22	1. Select the clip, move the playhead to where the change should start, and [add an action](/motion/add-an-action/) with <kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>. The new action lasts 1 second and is already selected.
23	
24	2. Open the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
25	
26	3. Set the controls to how they should be when the action ends.
27	
28	4. To make the change take longer, [drag the end of the action's band](/motion/change-an-action/).
29	
30	</Steps>
31	
32	To come back to an action later, [select it](/motion/select-an-action/) first. Otherwise the Sound tab changes the clip's own settings.
33	
34	For the level alone, it's quicker to <kbd>⌥</kbd>-click the [volume line](/audio/volume-line/#add-a-point).

36	## What an action can animate
37	
38	With an action selected, these write that action's end state instead of the clip's own settings:
39	
40	- **Volume**, **Mute** and the fade lengths
41	- **Pan** and **Mix to mono**
42	- **Channels**
43	- the **EQ** and **Hum**
44	- **Amount** in Voice Isolation
45	- **Noise Reduction**
46	- the **Gate**, the **Leveller** and the **De-esser**
47	- the **Compressor** and the **Limiter**
48	
49	## Numbers glide, switches jump
50	
51	Numbers move smoothly across the action's span. Switches hold their start value and change at the action's end, with no glide, as at a cut between two clips.
52	
53	These are the switches:
54	
55	- **Mute**, **Mix to mono** and **EQ** Bypass
56	- turning a section or an EQ slot on or off
57	- **Channels**
58	- a pass filter's slope
59	- **Hum**'s mains and harmonics
60	- the **Leveller**'s Response
61	
62	Unticking a section or an EQ slot with an action selected turns it off at the action's end.
63	
64	A number only glides while its section is on at both ends of the action. A section an action turns on arrives at its end values when the action ends. Voice Isolation's **Amount** and Noise Reduction's **Remove noise** are the exceptions. Each is one amount, and 0 is its off, so it glides up from 0 or down to it.
65	
66	## What can't be animated
67	
68	These always change the clip's own settings, even with an action selected:
69	
70	- **Ducking**
71	- **Keep pitch**
72	- the fade shapes, **In shape** and **Out shape**
73	- the **Voice Effect**
74	- a nest clip's **Mix to mono**
75	
76	A row like this shows ⊘ in front of its label while an action is selected. See [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).
77	
78	A voice effect is made from the clip's own Voice Isolation **Amount**, not an animated one.
79	
80	[Normalize](/audio/normalize/), [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) and [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) also write the clip's own settings with an action selected. The **Normalize** button carries a small boxed "clip" tag to show this.
81	
82	## Processing turned on by an action
83	
84	A clip gets whatever preparation its sound needs when an action asks for it, even if the clip's own setting is off:
85	
86	- The isolated voice is made when an action raises **Amount**, on a clip whose own Voice Isolation is off.
87	- The Gate, the Leveller and the De-esser measure the clip's loudness when an action turns them on.
88	- A Limiter or Noise Reduction turned on by an action is set up for the clip's whole track, as one set on the clip itself is, so the sound's timing doesn't shift at the moment it comes on.
89	
90	## With an agent
91	
92	`set_audio` only reaches a clip's own settings. To animate, an agent uses `add_action` and then `set_action_end`. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).
93

106	
107	**Channels** chooses which channels of a stereo file a clip plays. It's the fix for a microphone recorded onto one side of a stereo file, which otherwise plays from one speaker only.
108	
109	<AtAGlance
110	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound sub-tab ▸ Channels section"
111	  tools="set_audio"
112	/>
113	
114	## Choose channels
115	
116	Open the **Channels** section and pick from **Play**. With several clips selected, the choice goes to all of them.
117	
118	| **Play** | What you hear |
119	| --- | --- |
120	| **Both** | The file as it is. This is the default. |
121	| **Left Only** | The left channel, from both speakers. |
122	| **Right Only** | The right channel, from both speakers. |
123	| **Swap Left and Right** | The two channels exchanged. |
124	
125	For a microphone on one channel, choose **Left Only** or **Right Only**. The voice then plays from both speakers at its own level. [Mix to mono](/audio/pan-and-mono/#mix-to-mono) would also put it in both speakers, but averaging it with the silent channel halves its level.
126	
127	The header of the section shows the current choice. **Reset** there puts it back to **Both**.
128	
129	## Good to know
130	
131	- A mono file has only one channel, so the choice has no effect on it.
132	- On a nest clip the choice has no effect. Set it on the clips inside.
133	- The Volume section's **Loudness** read-out counts the choice, and so does [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode. Normalize in Peak mode reads the file's waveform and doesn't.
134	- The choice comes after [voice isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) and any [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/), and before the [EQ](/audio/eq/) and [Mix to mono](/audio/pan-and-mono/#mix-to-mono). So on a stereo file with a voice effect, it picks from the sound after the effect.
135	- With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, the choice is what the action changes to. It switches at the action's end with no glide, and its row says "at end".
136	
137	## With an agent
138	
139	`set_audio` sets this with `channels`: `both`, `left`, `right` or `swapped`. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#mono-keep-pitch-pan-and-channels).
