147	title: Compressor
148	description: Even out a clip's loud and quiet passages by turning down whatever goes above a threshold.
149	---
150	
151	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
152	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
153	
154	The compressor evens out a clip's loud and quiet passages by turning down whatever goes above a threshold. It reacts moment by moment and acts only on what's over the threshold. For a voice that drifts on and off the microphone, the [Leveller](/audio/leveller/) is the better fit. This page covers a clip's compressor. A track has one of its own, on [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/).
155	
156	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Compressor" tools="set_audio" />
157	
158	## Smooth volume levels
159	
160	<Steps>
161	
162	1. Select the clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab. The **Compressor** section starts closed, so open it.
163	
164	2. Tick **Smooth volume levels**. It turns on at a gentle setting for speech: −18 dB, 3:1, a 10 ms attack and a 200 ms release, with no makeup.
165	
166	3. Play the clip. Lower [**Threshold**](#threshold) until the loud passages come down, and raise [**Ratio**](#ratio) if you want it to act harder.
167	
168	4. Add [**Makeup**](#makeup) to win back the level it took.
169	
170	</Steps>
171	
172	The section's header shows the ratio, such as "3.0:1", or "off". **Reset** appears there once the compressor has settings, and turns it off. Unticking **Smooth volume levels** also throws away its settings, so ticking it again starts from the defaults.
173	
174	## The controls
175	
176	| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick picks |
177	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
178	| **Threshold** | The level above which it starts turning the sound down. | −60 to 0 dB | −18 dB | −30, −24, −18, −12, −6 |
179	| **Ratio** | How strongly it turns down sound above the threshold. | 1 to 20 :1 | 3:1 | 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 8, 20 |
180	| **Attack** | How quickly it reacts when the level rises. | 0 to 200 ms | 10 ms | 1, 5, 10, 30, 100 ms |
181	| **Release** | How quickly it lets go when the level falls. | 10 to 2000 ms | 200 ms | 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000 ms |
182	| **Makeup** | Gain added afterwards to make up what the compressor took away. | 0 to 24 dB | 0 dB | 0, 3, 6, 12 |
183	
184	A number typed outside the range goes to the nearest end of it.
185	
186	### Threshold
187	
188	The threshold is a fixed level, not a distance from the clip's loudness as the [Gate](/audio/gate/)'s is. A quiet recording may never reach the default of −18 dB, and then the compressor does nothing until you lower it.
189	
190	### Ratio
191	
192	At 3:1, sound 3 dB over the threshold comes out 1 dB over it. 1:1 turns nothing down, and 20:1 acts like a limiter.
193	
194	### Attack
195	
196	A short attack catches the start of a word or a sudden peak. A longer one lets those through before the compressor closes in. The time is in milliseconds and isn't rounded to frames.
197	
198	### Release
199	
200	A short release recovers quickly after a loud moment. A longer one lets go more gradually. Like Attack, it isn't rounded to frames.
201	
202	### Makeup
203	
204	Makeup adds a fixed gain after the compressor, so it applies even at 1:1.
205	
206	## Change the compressor over time
207	
208	With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, the controls write the action's end, and each number moves smoothly across the action. Turning the compressor on or off changes at the action's end, with no glide.
209	
210	## Good to know
211	
212	- The compressor acts before the clip's volume, fades and ducking, so moving the Volume slider doesn't change how hard it compresses.
213	- It runs after [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/), the [Gate](/audio/gate/), the [Leveller](/audio/leveller/) and the [De-esser](/audio/de-esser/), so the threshold is compared with sound they've already worked on.
214	- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode measures through it.
215	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) sets a compressor for you, with its threshold at the speech's typical peak and makeup that gives back the loudness it takes.
216	- On a nest clip the compressor has no effect. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
217	
218	## With an agent
219	
220	`set_audio` sets the same controls through its `compressor` argument, and `null` turns the compressor off. An agent isn't held to the inspector's Attack and Release ranges, and gives both times in [its own units](/mcp/units-and-ids/). See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/).
221	
222	## Related
223

225	- [Leveller](/audio/leveller/)
226	- [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/)
227	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)

230	title: "Crossfades"
231	description: "Fade one clip's sound into the next across a transition, choose the shape of the fade, and crossfade clips that have no picture."
232	---
233	
234	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
235	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
236	
237	When two clips on a track overlap with a transition, the transition can fade the outgoing sound out and the incoming sound in, so the cut isn't heard as a jump.
238	
239	<AtAGlance
240	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Transition section"
241	  tools="set_transition_style"
242	/>
243	
244	## Crossfade audio
245	
246	A new transition already crossfades its sound, at the **+3 dB** shape, so most of the time there's nothing to do. Open the section to turn the crossfade off, or to change its shape.
247	
248	<Steps>
249	
250	1. Select the later of the two overlapping clips, on its own. The **Transition** section only appears for a single clip that overlaps the clip before it.
251	
252	2. In the Clip tab, choose the **Clip** sub-tab and open **Transition**.
253	
254	3. Tick or untick **Crossfade Audio**.
255	
256	</Steps>
257	
258	| **Crossfade Audio** | What you hear across the overlap |
259	| --- | --- |
260	| On | The outgoing sound fades out and the incoming sound fades in. If only one of the two clips has sound, that clip still fades. |
261	| Off | Both clips play at their own level for the whole overlap, mixed together. |
262	
263	The fade follows the transition's **Curve**, so an eased transition eases its sound too. A new transition is **Ease In Out**. **Curve** and **Crossfade Audio** are separate settings, and changing one leaves the other alone.
264	
265	To change the overlap's length, use the **Duration** row. See [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
266	
267	## Choose a crossfade shape
268	
269	**Crossfade Shape** sets the curve of the fade. It's available while **Crossfade Audio** is on, and the default is **+3 dB**. The incoming clip follows the shape, and the outgoing clip follows it in reverse.
270	
271	| **Crossfade Shape** | What it does | Each clip's level halfway through the fade |
272	| --- | --- | --- |
273	| **Linear** | A straight-line pair. It dips 3 dB in the middle of two unrelated takes, but suits two parts of the same sound. | About −6 dB |
274	| **S-Curve** | A fade that does most of its changing in the middle of the overlap and moves slowly at both ends. | About −6 dB |
275	| **+3 dB** | Constant power, which holds the level steady across two unrelated takes. | About −3 dB |
276	| **−3 dB** | A slow start. The incoming sound rises late and the outgoing sound falls early, so the middle of the overlap is the quietest of the four. | About −11 dB |
277	
278	## Audio-only transitions
279	
280	Two overlapping clips with no picture get the same **Transition** section, on the same sub-tab. Only their sound changes. **Crossfade Audio**, **Crossfade Shape** and **Curve** control the fade, **Duration** sets its length, and **Kind** has no visible effect.
281	
282	Whenever an edit makes a clip overlap the one before it, Frame Job adds a transition, for audio clips as for any other. So overlapping two music clips crossfades them straight away. See [Add or remove a transition](/motion/add-a-transition/) for the other ways to make one.
283	
284	## Crossfade after Detach Audio
285	
286	[Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) moves a clip's sound to its own clip on the track below and switches it off on the picture clip, so **Crossfade Audio** on the transition between two picture clips no longer fades that sound. The fade belongs to the detached audio clips instead.
287	
288	Detach both clips of an overlap and their audio clips overlap on that track, which gives them a transition of their own that crossfades them. Audio clips that don't overlap yet get one as soon as you overlap them. Select the later audio clip to change it.
289	
290	## Good to know
291	
292	- The crossfade multiplies whatever else is happening to the sound. Mute, solo, ducking, volume and a clip's own fades still apply on top.
293	- With **Kind** set to **None**, an overlap has no transition of its own. It plays as a linear cross dissolve with no sound crossfade, and the section shows **Linear** and **Crossfade Audio** off. Changing either of them gives the overlap a transition with exactly the values shown.
294	- Choosing another style from **Clip ▸ Transition** on a clip that already has a transition keeps its curve and its crossfade.
295	- A transition on a nest clip fades all the sound inside the nest. A crossfade between clips inside the nest still happens too, and you hear both.
296	- Each clip's [limiter](/audio/limiter/) holds that clip alone, so two limited clips can add up past the ceiling during an overlap. An export's master limiter catches this, but the preview has none, so it can sound louder while you edit. A [track compressor or limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) is also approximate in the preview where clips overlap.
297	
298	## With an agent
299	
300	`set_transition_style` sets the crossfade with `audio` (true or false) and its shape with `audio_shape`: `plus_3db`, `linear`, `s_curve` or `minus_3db`. A key you leave out keeps what's there. See [Tools: transitions](/mcp/tools-transitions/#set_transition_style).
301	
302	## Related
303	
304	- [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/)
305	- [Audio fades](/audio/fades/)
306	- [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/)
307	- [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/)

309	title: "De-esser"
310	description: "Tame the hard s, sh and t sounds a close microphone exaggerates, turning down only the top of the voice while they last."
311	---
312	
313	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
314	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
315	
316	The de-esser tames sibilance, the hard "s", "sh" and "t" sounds a close microphone exaggerates. It listens to the sound above its frequency and turns only that band down while it's over the threshold, so the rest of the voice keeps its level.
317	
318	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ De-esser" tools="set_audio" />
319	
320	## Reduce sibilance
321	
322	<Steps>
323	
324	1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **De-esser** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
325	
326	2. Tick **Reduce sibilance**. It starts at 6,000 Hz, a threshold of 0 dB and a range of 6 dB.
327	
328	3. Play a part with hard "s" sounds. If they're still sharp, lower **Threshold** or raise **Range**.
329	
330	4. If the voice sounds dull or lisped, raise **Threshold** or lower **Range**. Move **Frequency** to where the sibilance sits in this voice.
331	
332	</Steps>
333	
334	The other controls are dimmed until **Reduce sibilance** is ticked. **Reset** in the section's header turns the de-esser off.
335	
336	## The controls
337	
338	| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick values |
339	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
340	| **Frequency** | Where the sibilant band starts. | 2,000 to 12,000 Hz | 6,000 Hz | 4,000, 5,000, 6,000, 8,000 |
341	| **Threshold** | How loud the band must get, relative to the clip's loudness, before it's turned down. | −30 to +20 dB | 0 dB | −6, −3, 0, 3 |
342	| **Range** | The most the band is turned down. | 1 to 24 dB | 6 dB | 3, 6, 10 |
343	
344	The de-esser never makes any frequency louder. Right at **Frequency** it takes less than half the range, about 2.5 dB of the default 6 dB, and about 5.5 dB an octave above.
345	
346	It reacts in 1 ms and lets go over 60 ms. You can't change those times.
347	
348	## Read Status and Loudness
349	
350	**Threshold** follows the clip's own loudness, the way the [Gate's](/audio/gate/#the-threshold-follows-the-clip) does, so a trim, a pan change or a different channel choice moves it. Two read-outs show what it means for this clip. With several clips selected, **Loudness** reads "—". **Status** does too, unless the de-esser is off on the first of them, when it reads "off".
351	
352	**Loudness** is the level the threshold is measured from, for example "−41.7 LUFS". It reads "measuring…" until the clip has been measured.
353	
354	**Status** says where the de-esser acts, or why it isn't working:
355	
356	| Status | What it means |
357	| --- | --- |
358	| off | **Reduce sibilance** isn't ticked. |
359	| Acts above −41.7 dBFS | The clip's loudness plus the **Threshold**. |
360	| Waits for its loudness | The clip hasn't been measured yet. |
361	| Not de-essing: too short | The clip plays for under 0.4 s, too short to measure. |
362	| Not de-essing: too quiet | The clip is too quiet to measure. |
363	| Not de-essing: no sound | The clip plays no sound in this timeline, or it's a nest clip. |
364	
365	Until the clip's loudness is measured it plays without the de-esser, and an export waits. See [Before the clip's loudness is measured](/audio/gate/#before-the-clips-loudness-is-measured).
366	
367	## Good to know
368	
369	- The de-esser runs after the [gate](/audio/gate/) and the [leveller](/audio/leveller/), and before the [compressor](/audio/compressor/). See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
370	- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, these controls set where the action ends. The numbers glide across the action, and turning the de-esser on or off changes at the action's end.
371	- The de-esser does nothing on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
372	
373	## With an agent
374	
375	`set_audio` sets the same controls through `de_esser`, with `frequency`, `threshold_db` and `range_db`. An empty `de_esser` turns it on at the defaults and `null` turns it off. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#de-esser).
376	
377	## Related
378	
379	- [Gate](/audio/gate/)
380	- [EQ](/audio/eq/)
381	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)
382	- [Compressor](/audio/compressor/)
383	---
384	title: Detach and Attach Audio
385	description: Split a clip's sound onto a linked clip of its own, keep the two in step, and merge them back into one clip.
386	---
387	
388	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
389	
390	Detach Audio splits a clip's sound onto its own clip, so you can trim, move or process the sound apart from the picture. Attach Audio merges the two back into one clip.
391	
392	<AtAGlance
393	  menu={['Clip ▸ Detach Audio', 'Clip ▸ Attach Audio']}
394	  keys={['⌥⌘D', '⇧⌥⌘D']}
395	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Mix"
396	  tools={['detach_audio', 'attach_audio', 'set_enabled']}
397	/>
398	
399	## Detach audio
400	
401	Select one or more clips and press <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd>. **Clip ▸ Detach Audio** and the **Detach Audio** button in the [Mix section](/audio/pan-and-mono/) of the Sound sub-tab do the same. The menu item is greyed out until something is selected.
402	
403	Each selected clip splits in two, as one undo step named "Detach Audio":
404	
405	- The original clip keeps its picture, and its audio is switched off.
406	- A new clip appears on the track directly below. It plays only sound, from the same file, with the same in point, length and speed, and it keeps the original's audio settings and actions.
407	
408	If the clip is already on the bottom track, Frame Job adds a new track underneath for the sound. Otherwise the sound always goes on the next track down, so make room there first, or drag the sound to another track afterwards.
409	
410	The two clips are now a **linked pair**. Trim the sound on its own to make a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/).
411	
412	### When Detach Audio won't work
413	
414	Frame Job beeps, changes nothing and shows the reason at the foot of the inspector:
415	
416	| The reason says | What it means |
417	| --- | --- |
418	| "…media 2 has no audio track" | The clip's file has no sound. |
419	| "…its audio is switched off" | The clip has already been detached, or its sound is otherwise off. |
420	| "…it is not a media clip" | The clip is text, a shape, a graphic, a picture, a freeze frame, a nest or an adjustment clip. |
421	| "clips 4 and 7 would overlap by…, more than half of the shorter clip…" | The track below already has a clip where the sound would land. |
422	| "clip 4 would overlap more than one neighbour on one side…" | The sound would reach more than one clip on the track below. |
423	| "clips 4 and 7 would overlap, and clip 7 is an adjustment clip…" | The track below has an adjustment clip where the sound would land. |
424	
425	Any other overlap with one clip on the track below, up to half the shorter clip, is allowed and becomes a cross dissolve between the two.
426	
427	With several clips selected, the ones that can be detached are, and the rest are skipped. You only see a reason when none of them could be.
428	
429	## See which clips are linked
430	
431	Each half of a linked pair shows a link symbol after its kind symbol, in the clip's name strip. Select one and the other gets a dashed ring in your Mac's accent colour, because edits to one move both. See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/#linked-clips).
432	
433	### A clip with its audio off
434	
435	A clip whose audio is off shows no waveform and no fade handles. A clip with its picture and its sound both off is drawn dimmed. The picture half of a linked pair has no Sound sub-tab, so select the sound half to change anything about the sound. See [Turn a clip's picture or sound off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/).
436	
437	## What stays in sync
438	
439	A linked picture and sound stay in step in time through your edits.
440	
441	| Edit | What happens to the pair |
442	| --- | --- |
443	| Move | Moving either clip moves both by the same amount. Only the clip you drag changes track, so you can drag the sound to another track and its picture stays where it is. When a move would take either clip past the start of the timeline, both stop together. |
444	| [Split](/editing/splitting/) | A split through both pairs the two halves on each side of the cut. When the cut only crosses one of the clips, the other stays linked to the piece it shares more time with, and the other piece loses its link. |
445	| [Duplicate](/editing/duplicate-clips/), [Nest](/editing/nests/) and [Ripple Delete](/editing/delete-clips/) | Take both clips. |
446	| [Copy and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/) | A selected picture brings its sound, so the pair pastes as a pair. A selected sound is copied on its own, and the pasted copy isn't linked to anything. |
447	| Ripple edits, [Close Gap and Insert Time](/editing/close-gaps/) | Move the other half too. |
448	| [Trim and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/#move-a-sound-clips-edge-alone) | On the picture, the edit carries to the sound when their edges line up. On the sound, it moves the sound alone. |
449	| [Slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/#slip-a-clip) | Slips both, as far as the one with less room allows. |
450	| Delete | Deleting the picture deletes its sound too. See [Remove a clip's sound](#remove-a-clips-sound). |
451	| [Speed](/speed/change-speed/) and [Reverse](/speed/reverse/) | Frame Job won't do these on a linked clip. See [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed). |
452	
453	A ripple edit that would push a sound starting before its picture past the start of the timeline doesn't happen at all. The reason at the foot of the inspector says the sound "would start before 0".
454	
455	Locks win over links. A partner on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/#lock-track) isn't moved, split, trimmed, slipped, duplicated, nested or deleted with its clip. **Copy** is the exception: a selected picture brings its sound even from a locked track.
456	
457	## Remove a clip's sound
458	
459	To drop a clip's sound for good, detach it, select the sound half and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>. The picture stays, silent, and its link is gone.
460	
461	Undo brings the sound back. Once the sound clip is gone, no control in the app turns the picture's own audio back on.
462	
463	## Attach audio
464	
465	Select either half of a pair and press <kbd>⇧⌥⌘D</kbd>, or choose **Clip ▸ Attach Audio**. The **Attach Audio** button in the Mix section does the same, but it's only there with the sound half selected, because the picture half has no Sound sub-tab.
466	
467	The picture's audio comes back on with the sound clip's audio settings, and the sound clip is removed. Its track stays, empty if nothing else is on it. With several pairs selected, each one merges, as one undo step named "Attach Audio".
468	
469	**Clip ▸ Attach Audio** is greyed out until the selection holds a linked clip. The button stays live, and beeps if the selection holds none.
470	
471	### When Attach Audio won't work
472	
473	The two halves have to match, because they're becoming one clip. They need the same start, length, in point and speed, and the same actions at the same times with the same curves. Otherwise the reason at the foot of the inspector says "clip 4's picture and clip 5's sound do not cover the same time; trim them to match before Attach Audio". This is what a J-cut or an L-cut does on purpose. Trim the two to the same start and end first, and remove or match any action you added to only one half.
474	
475	## Actions and speed
476	
477	The new sound clip gets a copy of every action, so volume actions keep working. An action that only changes the picture does nothing on the sound clip. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/#detach-audio).
478	
479	A clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) keeps it: the sound clip's copy of the Speed actions gives it the same ramp, so the two stay in step.
480	
481	Frame Job won't change the speed or direction of either half while they're linked, because the two would have to be re-timed identically. That covers Speed, Reverse, rate stretch, [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/), and adding, moving, changing or removing a Speed action. The reason at the foot of the inspector says "clip 4 is linked to clip 5: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction". During a drag, such as a rate stretch, nothing moves and no reason appears. Attach, make the change, then detach again.
482	
483	Attaching keeps the sound's work. The picture takes the sound clip's audio settings, and each of its actions takes the audio values of the sound clip's action at the same place.
484	
485	## With an agent
486	
487	`detach_audio` and `attach_audio` do what the **Clip** menu does, for the one clip you name in `clip`. For `attach_audio`, either half will do. See [Tools: audio](/mcp/tools-audio/).
488	
489	`set_enabled` turns a clip's picture or sound on or off directly, which no control in the app does. After a detached sound has been deleted, it's the way to switch the picture's own audio back on. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#set_enabled).
490	
491	## Related

499	title: Duck by Speech
500	description: Lower the other clips only while this clip's speech plays, so the music comes back up in the pauses.
501	---
502	
503	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
504	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
505	
506	Duck by Speech lowers the other clips only around this clip's stretches of speech, so the music rises again when the voice stops. It's [Ducking](/audio/ducking/) with **Duck by** set to **Speech**.
507	
508	<AtAGlance
509	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Ducking ▸ Duck by"
510	  tools={['set_audio', 'set_media_speech']}
511	  needs="Nothing. Speech is detected on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
512	/>
513	
514	## Duck only while someone speaks
515	
516	<Steps>
517	
518	1. Select the voice clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab.
519	
520	2. In the **Ducking** section, tick **Duck other audio**.
521	
522	3. Set **Duck by** to **Speech**.
523	
524	4. Adjust [Pre-roll and Hold](#set-pre-roll-and-hold) if the music moves too early or too late.
525	
526	</Steps>
527	
528	Level, Attack and Release work as they do for [ducking by clip length](/audio/ducking/#the-controls), but apply to each stretch of speech rather than to the whole clip.
529	
530	## How it follows the speech
531	
532	For each stretch of speech, the attack starts Pre-roll before the first word, the others hold at Level until Hold after the last word, and the release follows.
533	
534	The pauses decide how often the music moves:
535	
536	- A breath under 0.2 s between words doesn't count as a pause.
537	- Stretches whose Pre-roll and Hold meet count as one. At the defaults, that keeps the music down through any pause of 1 s or less.
538	- Where one stretch's release meets the next one's attack, the others follow whichever is lower, so the level never dips below Level.
539	
540	Only the speech in the part of the file the clip plays counts. The stretches follow the clip's speed, reverse and speed ramps.
541	
542	## Set Pre-roll and Hold
543	
544	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
545	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
546	| **Pre-roll** | How long before each stretch of speech the others start going down. Quick picks: 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 s. | 0.5 s | 0–5 s |
547	| **Hold** | How long after each stretch of speech the others stay down before the release. Quick picks: 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 s. | 0.5 s | 0–5 s |
548	
549	Both are greyed out until **Duck by** is **Speech**, and both keep the length you type, not rounded to whole frames.
550	
551	They can reach past the clip's ends. If the speech starts on the clip's first frame, the others start going down Pre-roll before the clip does. As with [the release](/audio/ducking/#good-to-know), a clip that ends right before this one starts may stay at full level.
552	
553	## Where the speech comes from
554	
555	Frame Job detects speech in every file with sound when it's imported, on your Mac, with the same detection [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) uses.
556	
557	Choosing **Speech** saves where that file's speech is in the project, in the same undo step. The preview, every export and an agent then all follow the same stretches. A file keeps the speech it was given and isn't detected again, so another clip of the same file uses the same stretches.
558	
559	**Duck by** is greyed out, so you can't choose **Speech**, in two cases:
560	
561	- A selected file's speech is still being detected. Try again in a moment.
562	- A selected clip isn't a clip of a file with sound, such as a nest.
563	
564	Relinking the clip's file to a shorter one keeps the speech that still fits. Relinking it to a file with no sound forgets the speech, and the clip no longer ducks anything.
565	
566	A file with no speech in it ducks nothing.
567	
568	## The line on the timeline
569	
570	A clip that ducks by speech has a thin yellow line across its waveform, so you can see what it's doing to the others. The line is high where they play at full level and low where they're ducked, and it follows the clip's speed, reverse and speed ramps.
571	
572	On a file with no speech the line stays flat along the top. There's no room for it on a very short waveform, and a clip ducking by Clip Length has no line at all. See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/).
573	
574	## Good to know
575	
576	Everything on [Ducking](/audio/ducking/#good-to-know) applies here too. Overlapping ducking clips multiply, a muted clip still ducks, and ducking can't be animated.
577	
578	## With an agent
579	
580	An agent turns on Duck by Speech with `set_audio`'s `duck`, setting `mode` to `speech` with `pre_roll` and `hold` if it wants them, and the file's speech is saved in the same step. It can't do so before the speech is detected, or on a clip that isn't a file with sound.
581	
582	An agent can also do something the inspector can't: give a file stretches of speech of its own with `set_media_speech`, in place of the detected ones, and read them back from `get_project` as `media[].speech`. The times are positions in the file played forward, so they don't change with a clip's speed or direction.
583	
584	It takes up to 100,000 stretches, in order, inside the file's length and not overlapping, though two may touch. Frame Job won't save them for a file with no sound. An empty list says the file has no speech. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/#set_media_speech).
585	
586	## Related
587	
588	- [Ducking](/audio/ducking/)
589	- [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/)
590	- [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/)
591	- [What counts as silent](/cleanup/voice-or-level/)

593	title: Ducking
594	description: Lower the other clips while this one plays, so music drops under a voice-over and comes back up after it.
595	---
596	
597	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
598	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
599	
600	Ducking lowers the other clips while this one plays. The usual use is a voice-over: turn ducking on for the voice, and the music drops under it.
601	
602	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Ducking" tools="set_audio" />
603	
604	## Duck the music under a voice-over
605	
606	Set ducking on the clip you want to hear, not on the clip that should get quieter.
607	
608	<Steps>
609	
610	1. Select the voice clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab.
611	
612	2. Open the **Ducking** section and tick **Duck other audio**.
613	
614	3. Set **Level** to how loud the music should be under the voice.
615	
616	</Steps>
617	
618	Ticking the box starts from the defaults: down to 20 %, over 0.5 s, and back up over 1 s. Unticking it, or choosing **Reset** in the section's header, turns ducking off and forgets the settings. The header shows the level, such as "20%", or "off".
619	
620	## The controls
621	
622	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
623	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
624	| **Duck other audio** | Turns ducking on for this clip. | Off | |
625	| **Duck by** | What the ducking follows. See [Choose what it follows](#choose-what-it-follows). | Clip Length | Clip Length, Speech |
626	| **Level** | How loud the other clips are while this one plays. Quick picks: 0, 10, 20, 30 and 50 %. | 20 % | 0–100 % |
627	| **Attack** | How long the other clips take to fall to Level, starting from this clip's first frame. Quick picks: 0.1, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 s. | 0.5 s | 0–5 s |
628	| **Release** | How long they take to come back up, starting after this clip ends. Quick picks: 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 s. | 1 s | 0–5 s |
629	| **Pre-roll**, **Hold** | Only for Duck by Speech. See [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/#set-pre-roll-and-hold). | 0.5 s each | 0–5 s |
630	
631	Every control but **Duck other audio** is greyed out until ducking is on. With several clips selected, changing one gives every selected clip all the first clip's ducking settings. See [Edit several clips at once](/audio/sound-tab/#edit-several-clips-at-once).
632	
633	**Level** multiplies whatever the other clips are already doing, so at 20 % a clip at half volume plays at a tenth of its full level. Their own volume, fades and actions still apply underneath.
634	
635	**Attack** and **Release** keep the length you type. They aren't rounded to whole frames. At 0 the level jumps instead of ramping.
636	
637	## Choose what it follows
638	
639	**Duck by** has two choices.
640	
641	**Clip Length** keeps the others down for as long as the clip sits on the timeline, whether or not it's making a sound. They stay lowered through the pauses, so you can see exactly when ducking applies by looking at the timeline, and nothing extra is drawn on the clip.
642	
643	**Speech** lowers them only while this clip's speech plays, so the music comes back up in the pauses. It works only on a clip of a file with sound, and **Duck by** stays greyed out until Frame Job has finished detecting that file's speech. A thin yellow line on the clip shows where the others go down. See [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/).
644	
645	## How the level moves
646	
647	The others ramp down from the ducking clip's first frame, hold at Level, and start ramping back up only once the clip has ended. So the music doesn't lift under the last words of a voice-over, and it's still coming back up after the clip has gone.
648	
649	If the Attack is longer than the clip, the others never reach Level, and the release starts from wherever they got to.
650	
651	Each ducked clip's [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) moves with this, so you can see the dip on the clips it lowers.
652	
653	## Good to know
654	
655	- **Overlapping ducking clips multiply.** Two at 50 % give 25 %.
656	- **A silent ducking clip still ducks.** A clip that's muted, silenced by a solo or has its audio switched off still lowers the others. Turn ducking off to stop it. A clip with its audio switched off has no **Sound** sub-tab, so switch its audio back on first.
657	- **Inside a nest**, a ducking clip lowers the rest of the project over the part of it that plays.
658	- **On a nest clip**, ducking lowers everything for the nest's whole length, and that includes the clips inside the nest. To leave one of them at full level, set ducking on that clip instead, inside the nest.
659	- **The release can miss a clip that follows.** Every clip that overlaps the ducking clip is lowered. A clip that starts after it ends, inside the release, may play at full level. Frame Job can play a clip that follows in the same audio lane as the ducking clip, and a ducking clip never lowers its own lane.
660	- **Ducking can't be animated.** The section is marked ⊘ inside an [action](/audio/animate-sound/), and a change there still applies to the whole clip.
661	
662	## With an agent
663	
664	An agent sets ducking with `set_audio`'s `duck`: a `level` from 0 to 1, an `attack` and a `release`, and a `mode` of `extent` for Clip Length or `speech` for Speech. Its `attack` and `release` can run past the inspector's 5 s. `{"duck": null}` turns ducking off. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#ducking).
665	
666	## Related
667	
668	- [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/)
669	- [Clip volume](/audio/volume/)
670	- [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/)
671	- [Nests](/editing/nests/)

673	title: EQ
674	description: Shape a clip's tone with a high-pass, two shelves, three bands and a low-pass, or start from the Rumble Cut, De-mud and Presence presets.
675	---
676	
677	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
678	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
679	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
680	
681	The EQ turns parts of a clip's sound up or down by frequency. Use it to take out rumble, thin out a boomy voice or make words easier to follow.
682	
683	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ EQ" tools="set_audio" />
684	
685	<Shot
686	  name="09b-clip-sound-eq.inspector"
687	  alt="The EQ section of the Sound sub-tab, reading 2 on, with a Reset button. A response curve falls away below 80 Hz and has four narrow hum notches and a small lift around 4 kHz. Below it are the Bypass checkbox, the Rumble Cut, De-mud and Presence buttons, High-pass ticked at 80 Hz and 24 dB/oct, and Low shelf unticked with its controls greyed out."
688	/>
689	
690	## Shape a clip's tone
691	
692	<Steps>
693	
694	1. Select the clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab. The **EQ** section starts closed, so open it.
695	
696	2. For a voice, press a [preset](#presets). Otherwise tick the [part](#the-seven-parts) you want.
697	
698	3. Set its [Frequency, and its Gain, Q or Slope](#frequency-gain-q-and-slope). The [curve](#the-response-curve) at the top of the section shows the result.
699	
700	4. Tick [**Bypass**](#bypass) to compare with and without.
701	
702	</Steps>
703	
704	The section's header shows how many parts are on, such as "2 on", or "bypassed", or "off". **Reset** appears there once the EQ has settings, and turns the whole EQ off.
705	
706	## Presets
707	
708	Each preset sets one part and turns Bypass off. It leaves the other parts alone, so the three combine.
709	
710	| Preset | What it sets |
711	| --- | --- |
712	| **Rumble Cut** | High-pass on at 80 Hz, 24 dB/oct |
713	| **De-mud** | Band 1 at 300 Hz, −3 dB, Q 1 |
714	| **Presence** | Band 3 at 4 kHz, +3 dB, Q 1 |
715	
716	A preset replaces whatever its part held. Press **De-mud** after setting up Band 1 by hand and your Band 1 settings are gone.
717	
718	## The seven parts
719	
720	The EQ has seven parts, each with its own checkbox, and the sound passes through them in this order. Ticking a part turns it on at its default. Unticking it clears that part's settings and leaves the others as they are, so ticking it again starts from the default. To switch parts off without losing them, use [Bypass](#bypass).
721	
722	A shelf or band starts at 0 dB, and a Gain of 0 dB changes nothing, so you won't hear one until you move its **Gain**. The High-pass and Low-pass take effect as soon as you tick them.
723	
724	### High-pass
725	
726	Turns down everything below its **Frequency**. It starts at 80 Hz and 12 dB/oct, and its quick picks are 40, 60, 80, 100 and 120 Hz.
727	
728	### Low shelf
729	
730	Turns everything below its **Frequency** up or down by its **Gain**. It starts at 100 Hz and 0 dB, and its quick picks are 80, 100, 150 and 200 Hz.
731	
732	### Band 1, 2 and 3
733	
734	Each band turns the frequencies around its **Frequency** up or down by its **Gain**, and **Q** sets how narrow the affected range is. The bands start at 300 Hz, 1000 Hz and 4000 Hz, all at 0 dB and Q 1. All three have the same frequency quick picks: 100, 300, 1000, 2500, 4000 and 8000 Hz.
735	
736	### High shelf
737	
738	Turns everything above its **Frequency** up or down by its **Gain**. It starts at 8000 Hz and 0 dB, and its quick picks are 6000, 8000, 10000 and 12000 Hz.
739	
740	### Low-pass
741	
742	Turns down everything above its **Frequency**. It starts at 12000 Hz and 12 dB/oct, and its quick picks are 8000, 10000, 12000 and 16000 Hz.
743	
744	## Frequency, Gain, Q and Slope
745	
746	A part's controls are greyed out until you tick it. Which ones it has depends on its kind.
747	
748	| Control | What it does | On | Range | Default |
749	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
750	| **Frequency** | Where the part acts: the corner of a pass or shelf, the centre of a band. It's a typed field with quick picks and no slider. | Every part | 20 to 20000 Hz | See [the seven parts](#the-seven-parts) |
751	| **Gain** | How far a shelf or band turns the sound up or down. Quick picks: −6, −3, 0, 3, 6. | Shelves and bands | −24 to +24 dB | 0 dB |
752	| **Q** | How narrow a band is. Higher is narrower. Quick picks: 0.5, 0.7, 1, 2, 4. | Bands | 0.1 to 10 | 1 |
753	| **Slope** | How steeply a pass falls away, in decibels per octave. 24 is the steeper. | High-pass and Low-pass | 12 dB/oct or 24 dB/oct | 12 dB/oct |
754	
755	A number typed outside the range goes to the nearest end of it.
756	
757	## The response curve
758	
759	The first row of the section draws how much each frequency from 20 Hz to 20 kHz is turned up or down. The middle line is 0 dB. Upright lines mark 100 Hz, 1 kHz and 10 kHz, and level lines mark +12 and −12 dB. The curve covers ±24 dB, and anything past that sits at the edge.
760	
761	The notches from [Hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/) are drawn on the same curve, so you see the two together.
762	
763	The curve only shows the result. It has no handles to drag. It's greyed while Bypass is on, and it isn't drawn when the selected clips have different EQ or hum settings.
764	
765	## Bypass
766	
767	Tick **Bypass** to silence the EQ and keep its settings, so you can compare with and without. It's off by default, and it's greyed out until the clip has an EQ. Pressing a preset turns it off.
768	
769	## Change the EQ over time
770	
771	With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, the EQ's controls write the action's end. **Frequency**, **Gain** and **Q** move smoothly across the action. **Slope**, **Bypass** and turning a part on or off change at the action's end, with no glide. Unticking a part with an action selected turns it off at the end of the action.
772	
773	**Frequency** has no slider, so when the value at the playhead differs from the one shown, the row says so in words, such as "now 450 Hz".
774	
775	## Good to know
776	
777	- The EQ runs after [Channels](/audio/channels/), and before [Hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/) and [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/). [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/#the-fixed-signal-order) has the whole order.
778	- The EQ doesn't change the Loudness read-out in the Volume section, but [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode measures through it.
779	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) presses Rumble Cut for you. [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) with its **EQ** option on replaces the Low shelf, the three bands and the High shelf, keeps the High-pass and Low-pass, and turns Bypass off.
780	- At a cut between two clips, the EQ's settings switch with no glide.
781	- On a nest clip the EQ has no effect. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
782	
783	## With an agent
784	
785	`set_audio` sets the same parts through its `eq` argument. A part it leaves out keeps what it holds, `null` turns one part off, and `"eq": null` turns the whole EQ off. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/).
786	
787	Two things differ from the inspector. Turning a band on at its defaults starts it at 1000 Hz whichever band it is, where the inspector starts the three at 300, 1000 and 4000 Hz. And a value outside its range is an error that changes nothing, where the inspector moves it to the nearest end.
788	
789	To switch one part off at the end of an action, an agent names it in the action's `off` list. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).
790	
791	## Related
792	
793	- [Hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/)
794	- [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/)
795	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)
796	- [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/)
797	- [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/)

799	title: "Audio fades"
800	description: Fade a clip's sound in and out from the inspector or the handles on the clip, and choose the shape of each fade.
801	---
802	
803	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
804	
805	A fade brings a clip's sound up from silence at its start or down to silence at its end, so it doesn't begin or stop abruptly. Fades change the sound only.
806	
807	<AtAGlance
808	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Fades', 'The fade handles on a clip']}
809	  tools="set_audio"
810	/>
811	
812	## Set a fade length
813	
814	Open the **Fades** section on the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/) and set the lengths.
815	
816	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
817	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
818	| **Fade in** | How long the sound takes to rise from silence at the clip's start. | 0 | 0 to 10 s |
819	| **Fade out** | How long the sound takes to fall to silence at the clip's end. | 0 | 0 to 10 s |
820	
821	The field's chevron offers 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 s. A length you type here is kept exactly as typed, not rounded to whole frames.
822	
823	The section's summary shows both lengths, such as "0.50 · 1.00 s", or "none". **Reset** clears both lengths and leaves the shapes as they are.
824	
825	With an [action selected](/audio/animate-sound/), these two rows write the action's end state.
826	
827	## Drag a fade handle
828	
829	Every clip with sound has a small square handle at each top corner of its audio part. Drag the left handle inward to set the fade in, or the right handle inward to set the fade out. The handle then sits at the end of the fade.
830	
831	The handles and the inspector rows change the same two settings, with these differences:
832	
833	- A handle's length snaps to whole frames.
834	- A handle can go past 10 s, up to the length of the clip. The 10 s limit is the inspector's.
835	- A handle changes that one clip, not the whole selection, and it doesn't select the clip.
836	- A handle changes the clip's own fade, even with an action selected.
837	
838	Each drag is one undo step, "Set Fade". Handles don't snap to clip edges, markers or the playhead, because a fade is a length, not a position.
839	
840	Handles don't respond on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). They aren't drawn when the clip's audio part is under 10 pt tall.
841	
842	## Choose a fade shape
843	
844	**In shape** and **Out shape** set how the level moves across each fade. The default for both is **Linear**.
845	
846	| Shape | On a fade in | On a fade out | Level halfway |
847	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
848	| **Linear** | A straight ramp, the same amount every moment. | The same in reverse. | 50 % |
849	| **S-Curve** | Starts and ends gently, moving fastest in the middle. | The same. | 50 % |
850	| **+3 dB** | Rises quickly, then levels off. Good for a fade in that should be heard straight away. | Holds up, then falls quickly at the end. | 71 %, 3 dB under full |
851	| **−3 dB** | Starts slowly and gathers speed. | Falls quickly, then trails away. Good for a fade out that should feel long. | 29 %, about 11 dB under full |
852	
853	The shapes always belong to the clip itself. With an action selected they're marked ⊘ and still change the clip's own setting, and an action can't [animate](/audio/animate-sound/#what-cant-be-animated) them.
854	
855	A crossfade between two clips has its own shape, with the same four choices. See [Crossfades](/audio/crossfades/).
856	
857	## When a clip moves or is trimmed
858	
859	A fade is measured from the clip's own edges:
860	
861	- **Move** a clip and the fade travels with it.
862	- **Trim** a clip and the fade stays at the edge, the same length.
863	- **Split** a clip and both halves keep both fade lengths, so a fade in also starts the second half and a fade out also ends the first.
864	
865	Where a fade in and a fade out overlap, the two multiply. That gives a dip in the middle rather than a jump. A length you type can be longer than the clip, and that fade is then cut off at the clip's other edge, so the sound never reaches full level.
866	
867	## Good to know
868	
869	- On a [nest clip](/audio/how-audio-works/#sound-on-a-nest), fades scale everything inside the nest.
870	- The [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) shows a clip's fades, so you can see them against the level.
871	
872	## With an agent
873	
874	`set_audio` sets a fade's length and shape on one or more clips, with `fade_in`, `fade_out`, `fade_in_shape` and `fade_out_shape`. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/). A crossfade is set with `set_transition_style` instead. See [Crossfades](/audio/crossfades/).

881	---
882	title: "Gate"
883	description: "Turn a clip down in the pauses between phrases, so room noise and breaths get quieter while the speech stays as it is."
884	---
885	
886	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
887	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
888	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
889	
890	The gate turns a clip down in its pauses. When the sound falls below the threshold it's pushed further down, so room noise and breaths between phrases get quieter while the speech itself is untouched. Above the threshold the gate is open and leaves the sound alone. It turns the pauses down, it doesn't cut them out. To take pauses out of the timeline, use [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/).
891	
892	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Gate" tools="set_audio" />
893	
894	<Shot
895	  name="09c-clip-sound-dynamics.inspector"
896	  alt="The Gate section of the Sound tab with Gate pauses ticked: Threshold −10 dB, Ratio 4.0:1, Range 20 dB, Attack 1 ms, Hold 50 ms, Release 100 ms, Status reading Opens above −31.8 dBFS, and Loudness −21.8 LUFS."
897	/>
898	
899	## Gate the pauses
900	
901	<Steps>
902	
903	1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **Gate** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
904	
905	2. Tick **Gate pauses**. It starts at the [defaults](#the-controls), which work from the clip's own loudness.
906	
907	3. Play the clip. If the ends of words are being cut, raise **Hold** or lower **Threshold**.
908	
909	4. If the pauses aren't quiet enough, raise **Range**. If they sound too empty, lower it.
910	
911	</Steps>
912	
913	The other controls are dimmed until **Gate pauses** is ticked. **Reset** in the section's header turns the gate off.
914	
915	## The controls
916	
917	| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick values |
918	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
919	| **Threshold** | How far under the clip's loudness the gate opens. | −40 to 0 dB | −10 dB | −20, −15, −10, −6 |
920	| **Ratio** | How strongly sound under the threshold is turned down. At 4:1, each dB under the threshold becomes 3 dB further down. | 1:1 to 20:1 | 4:1 | 2, 4, 10, 20 |
921	| **Range** | The most the gate ever takes away. | 1 to 80 dB | 20 dB | 10, 20, 40, 80 |
922	| **Attack** | How quickly it opens when the sound rises. | 0 to 100 ms | 1 ms | 1, 5, 10 |
923	| **Hold** | How long it stays open after the sound falls, so the ends of words aren't clipped. | 0 to 500 ms | 50 ms | 0, 50, 100, 200 |
924	| **Release** | How quickly it closes after the hold. | 1 to 2,000 ms | 100 ms | 50, 100, 250, 500 |
925	
926	## The threshold follows the clip
927	
928	**Threshold** is set in dB under the clip's own loudness, not at a fixed level, so the same setting works on a quiet recording and a loud one. A trim, a pan change or a different channel choice moves the loudness, and the threshold moves with it.
929	
930	That loudness is the Loudness figure in the [Volume](/audio/volume/) section. It's measured before noise reduction, the compressor, the volume, the fades and ducking, so moving the Volume slider doesn't change where the gate opens.
931	
932	## Read Status and Loudness
933	
934	Two read-outs at the foot of the section show what the threshold means for this clip. With several clips selected, **Loudness** reads "—". **Status** does too, unless the gate is off on the first of them, when it reads "off".
935	
936	**Loudness** is the level the threshold is measured from, for example "−21.8 LUFS". It reads "measuring…" until the clip has been measured.
937	
938	**Status** says where the gate opens, or why it isn't working:
939	
940	| Status | What it means |
941	| --- | --- |
942	| off | **Gate pauses** isn't ticked. |
943	| Opens above −31.8 dBFS | The clip's loudness plus the **Threshold**. Here, −21.8 LUFS with a −10 dB threshold. |
944	| Waits for its loudness | The clip hasn't been measured yet. See below. |
945	| Not gating: too short | The clip plays for under 0.4 s, too short to measure. |
946	| Not gating: too quiet | The clip is too quiet to measure. |
947	| Not gating: no sound | The clip plays no sound in this timeline, or it's a nest clip. |
948	
949	## Before the clip's loudness is measured
950	
951	The gate, the [leveller](/audio/leveller/) and the [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) all depend on the clip's measured loudness. Until it's measured, the clip plays without them, and the preview picks them up by itself.
952	
953	An export waits until every gated, levelled or de-essed clip has been measured. After five minutes without a measurement it stops, saying that the clip's loudness or speech hasn't been measured yet, and to wait for the Status rows to show the clip's loudness and export again.
954	
955	A clip that can't be measured, because it's under 0.4 s or too quiet, plays and exports without them, and the export doesn't wait for it.
956

2	title: Leveller
3	description: Even out a voice that moves on and off the microphone by bringing each phrase toward a target level, ahead of time.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	The leveller evens out a speaker who moves on and off the microphone. It turns each phrase up or down toward a target, working from the whole clip ahead of time, so a phrase starts at its own level and doesn't catch up after it begins. To tame sudden loud moments use the [Compressor](/audio/compressor/), and to bring a whole clip to a delivery loudness use [Normalize](/audio/normalize/).
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Leveller"
13	  tools="set_audio"
14	  needs="The clip's loudness and its speech, both measured on your Mac with no key and no upload."
15	/>
16	
17	## Ride the level
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Select the clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab. The **Leveller** section starts closed, so open it.
22	
23	2. Tick **Ride the level**. It turns on at the [defaults](#the-controls).
24	
25	3. Read **Status**. If it says **Aims at** and a level, the clip is being levelled. If it [says anything else](#status-and-loudness-read-outs), it's waiting or it can't work on this clip.
26	
27	4. Play the clip, and adjust the controls if a phrase is still too quiet or too loud.
28	
29	</Steps>
30	
31	The section's header shows the target, such as "0 dB", or "off". **Reset** appears there once the leveller has settings, and turns it off. Unticking **Ride the level** also throws away its settings, so ticking it again starts from the defaults.
32	
33	## How it levels
34	
35	The leveller looks at the clip's speech and splits it into phrases. A pause in the speech of at least half a second ends a phrase, and a shorter gap stays inside it.
36	
37	- **In a phrase**, it measures the level the way a loudness meter does, over about three seconds of speech at a time. It never reaches across a pause into the next phrase.
38	- **In a pause**, it holds the gain it had and doesn't follow the room. In the last quarter of a second of the pause it moves to the next phrase's level.
39	- **A phrase with under a second of speech** takes the level of the last longer phrase before it, or, when there's none, the first one after it. A short "yes" doesn't get a level of its own.
40	
41	## The controls
42	
43	| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick picks |
44	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
45	| **Target** | Where it aims. | −20 to 10 dB | 0 dB | −6, −3, 0, 3 |
46	| **Max Boost** | The most it turns the clip up. | 0 to 24 dB | 12 dB | 6, 12, 18 |
47	| **Max Cut** | The most it turns the clip down. | 0 to 24 dB | 12 dB | 3, 6, 12 |
48	| **Response** | How smoothly it follows the voice within a phrase. | 0.5 to 10 s | 2 s | 1, 2, 4 s |
49	
50	A number typed outside the range goes to the nearest end of it.
51	
52	### Target
53	
54	The target is in dB from the clip's own loudness, not an absolute level. At 0 dB each phrase aims at the clip's loudness, and at −3 dB it aims 3 dB under that. Because it follows the clip's loudness, a trim that changes what plays moves the level it aims at.
55	
56	### Max Boost
57	
58	Caps how far a quiet phrase is turned up. Lower it if a faint background voice or a distant mumble is being pulled up too far. At 0 dB the leveller never turns anything up.
59	
60	### Max Cut
61	
62	Caps how far a loud phrase is turned down. At 0 dB the leveller never turns anything down.
63	
64	### Response
65	
66	Changes in a phrase's level shorter than this are smoothed out, before and after alike. A longer Response follows the voice more slowly, and a shorter one follows it more closely.
67	
68	## Status and Loudness read-outs
69	
70	**Status** says where the leveller is aiming, what it's waiting for, or why it isn't levelling.
71	
72	| Status says | What it means |
73	| --- | --- |
74	| "Aims at −41.7 LUFS" | It's levelling, toward that level: the clip's loudness plus the Target. |
75	| "Waits for its loudness" | The clip's sound analysis hasn't finished. |
76	| "Waits for its speech" | Speech in the clip hasn't been found yet. |
77	| "Not levelling: it plays no sound in this timeline" | The clip has nothing to measure here. |
78	| "Not levelling: it plays for under 0.4 s" | The clip is too short to measure. |
79	| "Not levelling: it is too quiet to measure" | The clip has no measurable loudness. |
80	| "Not levelling: it has no phrase with 1 s of speech" | No phrase is long enough to measure. |
81	| "Not levelling: speech detection is unavailable" | Speech detection isn't available, and the media has no saved speech. |
82	| "off" | **Ride the level** isn't ticked. |
83	| "—" | Several clips are selected, so select one to read it, or the clip is a nest, where the leveller has no effect. |
84	
85	**Loudness** shows the clip's loudness, which the target is measured from, such as "−41.7 LUFS". LUFS is the unit of loudness. It reads "measuring…" while that's being worked out, and "—" with several clips selected or when there's no reading. It's measured over the part of the clip that plays, before the clip's volume, so moving the Volume slider doesn't change it.
86	
87	## Change the leveller over time
88	
89	With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, the controls write the action's end. **Target**, **Max Boost** and **Max Cut** move smoothly across the action. **Response** changes at the action's end, and so does turning the leveller on or off.
90	
91	## Good to know
92	
93	- The leveller works from the speech found by the clip's sound analysis, or the speech saved for [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/).
94	- Until the clip's loudness and speech are both measured, it plays without levelling. An export waits for them for up to five minutes, then stops with a message naming the clip. Wait for **Status** to show the clip's loudness and export again.
95	- A clip it can't level, for one of the "Not levelling" reasons above, plays and exports without it.
96	- It works the same in the preview and in an export, from wherever playback starts.
97	- It runs after the [Gate](/audio/gate/) and before the [De-esser](/audio/de-esser/) and the [Compressor](/audio/compressor/), which then get the levelled voice.
98	- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode measures through it.
99	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) turns the leveller on at its defaults when the speech's loudness varies a lot, and off when it doesn't.
100	- On a nest clip the leveller has no effect. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
101	
102	## With an agent
103	
104	`set_audio` sets the same controls through its `leveller` argument. `{}` turns the leveller on at its defaults, and `null` turns it off. A value outside its range is an error that changes nothing. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/).
105	
106	## Related
107	
108	- [Compressor](/audio/compressor/)
109	- [Gate](/audio/gate/)
110	- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/)
111	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)
112	- [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/)

114	title: Limiter
115	description: Hold a clip's peaks under a ceiling, so a quiet recording can be turned up without its loudest moments clipping.
116	---
117	
118	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
119	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
120	
121	The limiter holds a clip's peaks under a ceiling, so a quiet recording can be turned up without its loudest moments clipping. This page covers a clip's limiter. A track has one of its own, on [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/), and an export has a master limiter, on [Export loudness](/export/loudness/).
122	
123	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Limiter" tools="set_audio" />
124	
125	## Limit peaks
126	
127	<Steps>
128	
129	1. Select the clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab. The **Limiter** section starts closed, so open it.
130	
131	2. Tick **Limit peaks**. It turns on with a [ceiling](#ceiling) of −1 dBTP and a [release](#release) of 100 ms.
132	
133	3. Turn the clip's volume up as far as you need. The ceiling holds.
134	
135	</Steps>
136	
137	It's a true-peak limiter, which is why its ceiling is in dBTP, decibels of true peak. It looks between the samples, where a peak can sit higher than any sample, and it looks a little ahead, so it turns the sound down smoothly just before a peak and not after it.
138	
139	The section's header shows the ceiling, such as "−1.0 dBTP", or "off". **Reset** appears there once the limiter has settings, and turns it off. Unticking **Limit peaks** also throws away its settings, so ticking it again starts from the defaults.
140	
141	[Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode turns the limiter on for you when a clip needs it, and [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) always does.
142	
143	## Ceiling
144	
145	The highest true peak the clip may reach, from −24 to 0 dBTP. The default is −1 dBTP, and the quick picks are −1, −2, −3 and −6.
146	
147	The ceiling is where the clip's peaks land after its Volume slider, so turning the volume up makes the limiter work harder and doesn't push the clip past the ceiling. Fades and ducking only turn a clip down, so they never take it over either.
148	
149	## Release
150	
151	How quickly the level recovers after a peak, from 1 to 1000 ms. The default is 100 ms, and the quick picks are 50, 100, 200 and 500. The time isn't rounded to frames.
152	
153	A number typed outside either range goes to the nearest end of it.
154	
155	## What it doesn't hold
156	
157	Each clip's limiter holds that clip alone. All of these can go past the ceiling:
158	
159	- Two limited clips that overlap, in a transition or on two tracks.
160	- A clip whose volume an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) raises above its own Volume setting.
161	- A clip inside a nest, when the nest's volume is above 100 %.
162	- The first moments after a hard cut from a louder clip on the same track, while the level settles.
163	
164	In an export, the [master limiter](/export/loudness/#the-master-limiter) holds the whole mix at its own ceiling, whichever of these happens. A [stem](/export/stems/) doesn't go through it. The preview has no master limiter, so they can sound louder while you edit than they do in the file.
165	
166	## Latency compensation
167	
168	Looking ahead delays the sound by 3.3 ms. Frame Job makes up for this on its own: on a track with a limited clip, it starts every clip 3.3 ms early, and the delay brings each one back onto its frame. There's nothing to set.
169	
170	That has two small side effects on such a track. A clip that starts within the first 3.3 ms of the timeline loses up to that much of its start, and the last 3.3 ms of the track aren't heard. [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/) has the same effect, with its own delay.
171	
172	## Change the limiter over time
173	
174	With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, the controls write the action's end. **Ceiling** and **Release** move smoothly across the action, and turning the limiter on or off changes at the action's end, with no glide. A limiter turned on by an action only limits from the action's end, but its [delay](#latency-compensation) applies to the clip's whole track from the start, as one set on the clip itself does.
175	
176	## Good to know
177	
178	- The limiter is last in the clip's chain, after the [**Mix**](/audio/pan-and-mono/) section. [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/#the-fixed-signal-order) has the whole order.
179	- On a nest clip the limiter has no effect. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
180	
181	## With an agent
182	
183	`set_audio` sets the same controls through its `limiter` argument. `{}` turns the limiter on at its defaults, and `null` turns it off. A value outside its range is an error that changes nothing. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/).
184	
185	## Related
186	
187	- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/)
188	- [Compressor](/audio/compressor/)
189	- [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/)
190	- [Export loudness](/export/loudness/)
191	- [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/)

193	title: "The Loudness Meter"
194	description: Show a live column beside the preview that measures your mix in LUFS and true peak while it plays at normal speed.
195	---
196	
197	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
198	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
199	
200	The Loudness Meter tells you how loud your mix really is, measured the way the loudness standards EBU R 128 and ITU-R BS.1770 measure it, while the preview plays at normal speed.
201	
202	<AtAGlance
203	  menu="View ▸ Loudness Meter"
204	  keys="⌃⌘L"
205	  where="A column at the right of the preview, left of the scopes"
206	/>
207	
208	<Shot
209	  name="04c-editor-loudness.preview"
210	  alt="The preview with the Loudness column at its right edge, before anything has played. The column has a Reset arrow at the top, M and S bars on a scale from 0 to −48 with a thin blue line across them just above −18, then Momentary, Short-term, Integrated and True peak max, each reading a dash, and a note saying this is the mix as the preview plays it, before the export's loudness and master limiter."
211	/>
212	
213	## Show the meter
214	
215	Choose **View ▸ Loudness Meter** or press <kbd>⌃⌘L</kbd>. The same command hides it, and the menu item has a tick while the column is showing. The column is 132 points wide and as tall as the preview pane, and the picture makes room for it. The command is always available.
216	
217	Then play the timeline at normal speed. The figures start at "—" and fill in as Frame Job measures.
218	
219	To measure a whole timeline, start at the beginning and play it through without jumping. **Integrated** is then the loudness of everything that played.
220	
221	## What it measures
222	
223	The meter measures the mix you hear, at the level you hear it. It only reads what plays, so it never changes the project or an export.
224	
225	Measuring carries on while the column is hidden. If you show it partway through a pass, the figures already include what has played.
226	
227	A mono track counts in both channels. A track with more than two channels counts by its first two.
228	
229	## The four figures
230	
231	| Figure | What it measures |
232	| --- | --- |
233	| **Momentary** | The last 0.4 seconds. |
234	| **Short-term** | The last 3 seconds. |
235	| **Integrated** | Everything measured since the last reset, with quiet passages left out as the standard says. |
236	| **True peak max** | The highest true peak since the last reset. It turns coral above −1 dBTP. |
237	
238	Figures have one decimal place, such as `−18.4 LUFS` or `−0.6 dBTP`. LUFS is the standard unit of loudness, and a step of 1 LU on its scale is 1 dB. A true peak is the highest point the sound reaches, including between samples, and dBTP is its level in decibels.
239	
240	| You see | It means |
241	| --- | --- |
242	| "—" | There's no figure yet. Momentary needs 0.4 seconds of measuring and Short-term needs 3. Integrated stays at "—" until something loud enough to count has played, so it stays there through digital silence. |
243	| "−∞" | Digital silence. |
244	
245	## The M and S bars
246	
247	The two bars show Momentary (**M**) and Short-term (**S**) on a scale from −48 to 0 LUFS, with a tick every 6 LU. A bar is empty while its figure is "—", and during digital silence.
248	
249	## The target line
250	
251	A thin line in the accent colour crosses both bars at the target in the [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) row, which is −16 LUFS unless you've changed it. It shows you where the mix sits against the level Normalize aims for.
252	
253	The line moves as soon as you change the target, even while the preview is paused. The target can go as low as −50 LUFS, and anything below −48 draws at the bottom of the scale. The line stays at the stored target when Normalize is in Peak mode.
254	
255	## Start measuring again
256	
257	Click the **Reset** button, the ↺ at the top of the column. All four figures go back to "—" and the next sound starts a new measurement.
258	
259	The meter also starts again by itself when you jump somewhere else, such as a seek, the loop going round, or playing from another place. It does the same if Frame Job can't keep up with the audio, because a measurement with a hole in it would be wrong.
260	
261	These don't restart it:
262	
263	- Pausing and playing on. Nothing is counted twice.
264	- An edit.
265	- A gap between clips.
266	- Holding a menu open.
267	- Stepping back by less than a second.
268	
269	When playback stops, the figures stay where they were.
270	
271	## Measuring only at normal speed
272	
273	The meter measures at ×1 only. At any other speed, such as while you [shuttle](/timeline/playback/):
274	
275	- Momentary and Short-term show "—" and their bars go empty.
276	- The note reads "Measured only at normal speed."
277	- Integrated and True peak max keep their values.
278	
279	When you stop, Momentary and Short-term go back to their last normal-speed values.
280	
281	## The note under the figures
282	
283	The note says what's being measured, and when to take the figures with care.
284	
285	| The note says | When |
286	| --- | --- |
287	| "The mix as the preview plays it, before the export's loudness and master limiter." | Usually. |
288	| "The mix as the preview plays it, with track compressors and limiters approximate, before the export's loudness and master limiter." | While any track has a [compressor or limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/). They're approximate in the preview and exact in an export. |
289	| "Measured only at normal speed." | While playing at any other speed. |
290	
291	An export with a loudness target changes the level after this point, and the master limiter holds its peaks under the ceiling, so the export's own report can differ from what you see here. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/).
292	
293	## Good to know
294	
295	- The meter belongs to its window. A new window starts with the column off and the meter empty.
296	- Nothing is saved. Closing the window ends the measurement, and the column is off the next time you open the project.
297	
298	## With an agent
299	
300	No agent tool shows this meter or reads it. An agent reads a mix's loudness from an export's report, and `normalize_clip` reports a clip's measured loudness as it sets the volume. See [Tools: rendering and export](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/) and [Tools: audio](/mcp/tools-audio/).
301	
302	## Related
303	
304	- [The level meter](/audio/level-meter/)
305	- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/)
306	- [Export loudness](/export/loudness/)
307	- [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/)

309	title: "Match Audio"
310	description: "Give several clips the loudness and speech tone of one of them, so takes from different microphones or rooms sit together, in one undo step."
311	---
312	
313	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
314	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
315	
316	Match Audio makes selected clips sound like one of them, the reference. It sets each other clip's loudness and speech tone in one undo step, which helps when two takes came from different microphones or rooms.
317	
318	<AtAGlance
319	  menu="Clip ▸ Match Audio…"
320	  tools="match_audio"
321	  needs="Nothing. Speech detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
322	/>
323	
324	## Match clips to a reference
325	
326	<Steps>
327	
328	1. Select the clips, including the one that already sounds right. You need at least two clips that could play sound. A nest clip or a clip with no sound doesn't count, and with fewer than two the menu item is dimmed.
329	
330	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Match Audio…**.
331	
332	3. In **Match to:**, choose the reference.
333	
334	4. Leave **Loudness** and **EQ** ticked, or untick the one you don't want. **Match** is greyed out with both off.
335	
336	5. Choose **Match**.
337	
338	</Steps>
339	
340	The Measuring Sound sheet stays up while each clip is measured, which takes a moment on a long clip. It counts "Clip 1 of 3…" as it goes. Nothing changes until every clip is measured, and **Cancel** leaves everything as it is.
341	
342	When it finishes, the change is one undo step called "Match Audio". The results are ordinary settings in the [Volume](/audio/volume/), [Limiter](/audio/limiter/) and [EQ](/audio/eq/) sections, so you can adjust them afterwards.
343	
344	The sheet opens with both boxes ticked and the first clip chosen every time. It doesn't remember your last choice.
345	
346	## Choose the reference
347	
348	**Match to:** lists the clips in timeline order, by start time and then by track, and the first is chosen. Each row reads `name — track — m:ss (clip id)`, for example `Interview — Track 1 — 0:42 (clip 12)`, so you can tell two clips with the same name apart.
349	
350	The reference itself isn't changed. Frame Job measures it once as it sounds in the timeline: through its own settings, its limiter and its volume, but without its fades, ducking or Mute. Its loudness at that point is the target for the other clips.
351	
352	## What Loudness sets
353	
354	**Loudness** runs [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode on each other clip, with the reference's loudness as the target. It sets the clip's volume, measured through the clip's settings as they'll be after the match. When the clip's peaks would pass −1 dBTP at that loudness, it also sets the clip's limiter at that ceiling.
355	
356	A clip so quiet that it needs more than the volume's ceiling of 32× stops there and ends up quieter than the reference.
357	
358	Loudness doesn't need speech, so you can use it on music by unticking **EQ**.
359	
360	## What EQ sets
361	
362	**EQ** gives each other clip the tone of the reference's voice. Frame Job compares the average spectrum of each clip's speech with the reference's, in 23 third-octave bands from 79 Hz to 12.7 kHz. Only speech counts. Frame Job uses the speech saved for [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/) if the clip has any, and otherwise what speech detection found in the file. A clip needs about a second of speech.
363	
364	Each clip is measured with its EQ's shelves and bands off. The difference, less the overall level, is then fitted with the EQ's low shelf, three bands and high shelf:
365	
366	- Each gain stays within ±12 dB.
367	- Each band's Q stays between 0.5 and 4.
368	- A band is only used where the difference is at least 0.5 dB.
369	
370	Those five parts replace the clip's own. Its high-pass, low-pass and [hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/) stay as they were, and **Bypass** is turned off.
371	
372	## What stays the same
373	
374	Match Audio changes only the volume, limiter and EQ. Every other section, the fades, ducking, pan and Mute are left alone.
375	
376	Choosing **Match** again with the same choice changes nothing. Frame Job beeps and adds no undo step.
377	
378	## When a clip can't be matched
379	
380	A clip that can't be matched is skipped, and the others are still matched. No message names a skipped clip, so if one sounds unchanged, check it against the list below.
381	
382	If the reference can't be used, or nothing can be matched, Frame Job beeps, changes nothing and puts the reason at the foot of the inspector. When the reference is the problem, the message starts "The reference, clip 12,". When every clip fails, it starts "Nothing could be matched." and gives each clip's reason.
383	
384	| The reason says | What it means | What to do |
385	| --- | --- | --- |
386	| "is still being analysed — its loudness has not been measured yet" | Frame Job hasn't finished with the file, which often happens straight after an import. | Try again in a moment. |
387	| "is still being analysed — its speech has not been detected yet" | The same, for speech. This only applies with **EQ** on. | Try again in a moment, or untick **EQ**. |
388	| "plays no sound in this timeline" | Nothing from this clip reaches the mix. | Choose another clip. |
389	| "plays for under 0.4 s" | The clip is too short to have a loudness. | Choose a longer clip, or trim this one longer. |
390	| "is under −70 LUFS" | There's no sound to match. | Choose another clip. |
391	| "has under 1 s of speech" | The part that plays has too little speech to measure a tone. | Untick **EQ**, or choose a clip with more speech. |
392	| "has under 12 third-octave bands within 50 dB of its loudest" | The reference's sound is too narrow to match a tone to. | Choose another reference, or untick **EQ**. |
393	| "shares under 12 third-octave bands with the reference" | This clip and the reference have too little of the spectrum in common. | Match this clip again with **EQ** unticked. |
394	
395	If the project changes while the clips are being measured, nothing is applied. Frame Job beeps, and the foot of the inspector says "the project changed while its sound was being measured, so nothing changed. Choose Match Audio again."
396	
397	## Good to know
398	
399	- Match Audio matches the average tone of speech. It doesn't match the room, reverb, noise or dynamics. For those, see [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/), [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/) and the [Compressor](/audio/compressor/).
400	- You match to a clip, not to a track or a whole mix. To bring clips to a loudness you choose rather than to one another, use [Normalize](/audio/normalize/).
401	- Like Normalize, it changes each clip's own settings even with an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected. The action itself stays as it was.
402	- With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, it works on the clips inside the nest.
403	
404	## With an agent
405	
406	`match_audio` takes the reference and the clips directly, with no sheet. Unlike the menu, it reports what happened to each clip: the settings it changed, the loudness figures, how closely the EQ fits, and each skipped clip with its reason. The call can take seconds on a long clip. A nest can't be matched or used as the reference, the call fails if Loudness and EQ are both off, and a second identical call reports "Match Audio made no change". See [Tools: audio](/mcp/tools-audio/).
407	
408	## Related

413	- [Limiter](/audio/limiter/)
