415	title: Mute and solo tracks
416	description: Silence a track, or hear only the tracks you pick, and see what that does to the picture, nests and an export.
417	---
418	
419	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
420	
421	Mute silences one track. Solo silences every other track, so you can hear one part of the mix by itself. Neither touches the picture.
422	
423	<AtAGlance
424	  menu={['Track ▸ Mute Audio', 'Track ▸ Solo']}
425	  where={['The speaker and headphones switches in the track header', "The track's right-click menu"]}
426	  tools="set_track"
427	/>
428	
429	## Mute a track
430	
431	Click the speaker switch in the track's header. Every clip on the track goes silent, and the picture is unaffected. Click it again to bring the sound back.
432	
433	**Mute Audio** in the track's right-click menu does the same for the track you clicked. **Track ▸ Mute Audio** acts on the [current track](/timeline/tracks/#the-current-track): the track of the first selected clip, or the front track when nothing is selected.
434	
435	To silence one clip and not its whole track, use its own [**Mute**](/audio/volume/#mute-a-clip).
436	
437	## Solo a track
438	
439	Click the headphones switch in the track's header, or choose **Solo** in the track's right-click menu or the **Track** menu. The tracks beside it go silent: the other timeline tracks or, inside a nest, that nest's other tracks.
440	
441	You can solo several tracks. All the soloed tracks play, and the rest are silenced.
442	
443	**Solo** shows a checkmark in the **Track** menu while it's on. Neither **Solo** nor **Mute Audio** has a keyboard shortcut. Each click is one undo step, named "Mute Track" or "Solo Track".
444	
445	## How mute and solo combine
446	
447	- **Mute always wins.** A track that's both muted and soloed stays silent.
448	- **Solo doesn't look at what's on the track.** A soloed track with nothing on it still silences the rest, as a mixer's solo button does.
449	- **Pictures stay.** A silenced track still draws. To take a picture out, use [Hide Video](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/#hide-video), which leaves the sound playing.
450	
451	## See what a solo silences
452	
453	Under a solo, the waveforms on silenced tracks draw faded, as they do on a muted track. Their speaker switches stay unlit, because a speaker shows that track's own setting and not what a solo is doing to it. So the waveform tells you what you'll hear, and the switch tells you what you've set.
454	
455	## Mute and solo in nests
456	
457	A solo only reaches the tracks beside it:
458	
459	- A solo on a timeline track silences the other timeline tracks, and a nest playing on one of them goes silent with it.
460	- A solo on a track inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) affects only that nest's other tracks.
461	
462	Muting the track a nest clip sits on silences everything inside the nest. A new nest's tracks copy the mute and solo of the tracks they came from, so a muted track's clips stay silent once they're nested. Un-nesting doesn't keep what's set on the nest's tracks.
463	
464	## In an export
465	
466	Mute and solo are part of the project, so the export hears what you hear. A silenced track isn't in the exported mix, and it writes no [stem](/export/stems/). If every track is silenced, Frame Job won't write stems.
467	
468	:::caution
469	A solo left on silences the rest of the export. Check the header switches before you export.
470	:::
471	
472	## Good to know
473	
474	- The switches are plain toggles. <kbd>⌥</kbd>-clicking one does what a click does, and <kbd>⌥</kbd>-clicking the header away from its switches [selects the track's clips](/timeline/tracks/#the-track-header).
475	- A [scrub](/audio/scrub-audio/) plays the same mix, so mute and solo silence it too.
476	- The header's other switches are on [The track header](/timeline/tracks/#the-track-header).
477	
478	## With an agent
479	
480	`set_track` sets the same switches. Name the `track` and pass `muted` or `solo` as true or false. It's a direct setting, not a toggle, so asking for what's already set changes nothing. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#set_track).
481	
482	## Related
483	
484	- [Track volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/)
485	- [Clip volume](/audio/volume/)
486	- [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/)

489	title: "Noise Reduction"
490	description: "Turn down steady background noise such as hiss, hum and fans, under speech as well as between words, with no noise sample needed."
491	---
492	
493	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
494	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
495	
496	Noise Reduction turns down steady background noise such as hiss, hum and fan noise. It works out the noise level from the clip itself, so you don't need to give it a sample of the noise or a stretch of silence.
497	
498	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Noise Reduction" tools="set_audio" />
499	
500	## Remove noise
501	
502	<Steps>
503	
504	1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **Noise Reduction** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
505	
506	2. Raise **Remove noise** while you listen, until the noise is low enough and the voice still sounds natural.
507	
508	</Steps>
509	
510	| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
511	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
512	| **Remove noise** | How much steady background noise to remove. Quick values: 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 %. | 0 to 100 % | 0 % (off) |
513	| **Depth** | Read-only. See [The Depth read-out](#the-depth-read-out). | | off |
514	
515	**Reset** in the section's header sets **Remove noise** back to 0.
516	
517	## The Depth read-out
518	
519	**Depth** tells you the most any part of the sound can be turned down at this setting. It follows **Remove noise**:
520	
521	| Remove noise | Depth reads |
522	| --- | --- |
523	| 0 % | off |
524	| 25 % | 2 dB at most |
525	| 50 % | 6 dB at most |
526	| 75 % | 12 dB at most |
527	| 100 % | floor removed |
528	
529	Between those it climbs with the setting, so 90 % reads "20 dB at most".
530	
531	Noise Reduction never removes more than the noise level it found, so a higher setting isn't a stronger cut across the whole sound.
532	
533	## What it can't do
534	
535	Noise Reduction isn't a gate. It works under speech as well as between words, and it doesn't silence the gaps. To turn the pauses down, use the [Gate](/audio/gate/).
536	
537	It can't remove a sound that isn't steady, such as a door slam or a cough. A long held note may eventually be treated as noise.
538	
539	To reduce the echo of a room, use [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/). The two work together: Noise Reduction then works on the isolated sound.
540	
541	## Good to know
542	
543	- It runs after the EQ and [hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/), and before the [Gate](/audio/gate/) and the [Compressor](/audio/compressor/). See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
544	- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, **Remove noise** sets where the action ends and the amount glides across the action.
545	- Noise Reduction set on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip has no effect. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
546	
547	## With an agent
548	
549	`set_audio` sets the amount as `noise_reduction`, from 0 to 1. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/).
550	
551	## Related

554	- [Hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/)

556	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)

558	title: "Pan and Mix to mono"
559	description: "Move a stereo clip's balance left or right, fold its channels into one, and place a sound anywhere between the speakers."
560	---
561	
562	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
563	
564	The **Mix** section places a clip's sound between the speakers. **Pan** moves a stereo clip's balance, and **Mix to mono** folds its channels into one.
565	
566	<AtAGlance
567	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound sub-tab ▸ Mix section"
568	  tools="set_audio"
569	/>
570	
571	The section's header summarises it: "centre", "mono", or the pan position. **Detach Audio** and **Attach Audio** are on the same section, and have [their own page](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
572	
573	## Pan a clip
574	
575	Drag **Pan**, type a number from −100 to 100, or use a quick pick: −100, −50, 0, 50 or 100. Negative numbers go left, positive numbers go right, and the default is 0.
576	
577	**Position**, under it, reads the result in words: "centre", "left 30" or "right 100". It's a read-out, so there's nothing to set there.
578	
579	On a stereo clip, **Pan** is a balance control. It doesn't move the left channel's sound across to the right:
580	
581	- At the centre, nothing changes.
582	- Moving it one way turns that side up and the other side down, keeping the total power steady.
583	- At −100 or 100, the side it went to is about 3 dB louder than at the centre, and the other side is silent.
584	
585	Pan has no effect on a mono file. See [Good to know](#good-to-know).
586	
587	## Mix to mono
588	
589	**Mix to mono** averages all of the clip's channels into one and sends that to every channel. It's off by default.
590	
591	On a one-channel file it does nothing, because there's nothing to fold.
592	
593	If only one channel of a stereo file has anything on it, use [Channels](/audio/channels/) instead. Averaging a voice with a silent channel halves its level.
594	
595	## Place a stereo clip's sound anywhere
596	
597	To hear a true pan, tick **Mix to mono** as well as setting **Pan**. The fold happens before the pan, so both channels carry the same sound, and **Pan** places that one sound anywhere from left to right.
598	
599	## Animate them
600	
601	With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, both controls write what the action changes to. **Pan** glides there across the action. **Mix to mono** is a switch, so it changes at the action's end, and its row says "at end". See [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/).
602	
603	## Reset the section
604	
605	**Reset** on the section's header sets the pan back to centre and turns mono off. It appears while the section differs from its default and no action is selected. See [Reset a section](/getting-started/inspector-fields/#reset-a-section).
606	
607	## Good to know
608	
609	- Pan has no effect on a mono file, with or without **Mix to mono**, because the file still has only one channel when Pan acts on it. A [track's pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/) can't move it either.
610	- On a nest clip, **Pan** has no effect. Set it on the clips inside.
611	- **Mix to mono** on a nest clip does work: it folds everything inside the nest, and that flattens any panning on the clips and tracks in it.
612	- The Volume section's **Loudness** read-out counts Pan and Mix to mono on a stereo clip, and so does [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode.
613	- In the clip's chain of sound processing, this section comes after the [compressor](/audio/compressor/) and before the [limiter](/audio/limiter/).
614	
615	## With an agent
616	
617	`set_audio` sets these with `pan`, from −1 for hard left to 1 for hard right (the inspector's −100 to 100), and `mono`, true or false. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#mono-keep-pitch-pan-and-channels).
618

626	title: Hear a scrub
627	description: Hear the sound under the playhead as you click or drag along the timeline ruler, to find a word or a beat.
628	---
629	
630	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
631	
632	When you click or drag along the ruler, you hear the sound under the playhead. Use it to find a word or a beat by ear.
633	
634	<AtAGlance where="Click or drag along the timeline ruler" />
635	
636	## Scrub the sound
637	
638	Drag along the [ruler](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/). Playback pauses first if it was running. As the playhead reaches new frames, Frame Job plays about 80 ms of the mix forward from it, with a 5 ms fade at each end so the pieces don't click. A fast drag skips frames, because each new piece waits until the last one has almost played.
639	
640	- A click on the ruler plays one piece.
641	- Hold the mouse still and the sound stops within about a tenth of a second.
642	- Let go and it stops.
643	
644	Dragging left plays each piece forwards from the playhead, not backwards, so a word stays recognisable.
645	
646	## What you hear
647	
648	A scrub plays the mix you'd hear in playback: each clip's volume, fades, ducking, pan and mono, each track's volume and pan, mute and solo, and each clip's sound processing.
649	
650	Three things differ from playback:
651	
652	- A clip's sound processing, such as its compressor or noise reduction, starts fresh in each piece, so it can sound different from a steady play.
653	- A track's [compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) aren't in a scrub.
654	- The [level meter](/audio/level-meter/) stays still.
655	
656	## Silence a scrub
657	
658	Scrub audio is always on, with no setting, no key and no agent tool. To silence it, [mute or solo](/audio/mute-and-solo/) tracks, or turn down your Mac's volume.
659	
660	## Good to know
661	
662	- Only a scrub on the ruler is heard. Stepping with <kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd>, **Go** in the [Markers list](/timeline/markers/#the-markers-list), and an agent moving the playhead are all silent.
663	- A scrub doesn't use the microphone, so it never asks for that permission.
664

672	title: "Synchronize Audio"
673	description: Line up a camera and a separate recorder, or any clips of the same moment, by matching their sound.
674	---
675	
676	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
677	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
678	
679	Synchronize Audio lines up two or more clips by their sound. The usual case is a camera clip and a separate audio recorder that captured the same moment. It finds where the sound matches, moves the clips into place and corrects any clock drift, all as one undo step.
680	
681	<AtAGlance
682	  menu="Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio"
683	  tools="sync_audio"
684	  needs="Nothing. The matching and the voice detection run on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
685	/>
686	
687	## Line up clips
688	
689	<Steps>
690	
691	1. Put each clip on its own track. They don't need to be close to each other.
692	
693	2. If the recorder holds several similar stretches, trim it roughly around the camera's sound, so it [matches the right one](#matching-by-sound).
694	
695	3. [Select the clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/).
696	
697	4. Choose **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**. It has no keyboard shortcut.
698	
699	5. Wait for the [Synchronizing Audio sheet](#the-synchronizing-audio-sheet) to finish.
700	
701	</Steps>
702	
703	One clip, the [anchor](#the-anchor), stays where it is. Every other clip slides along its own track until its sound plays at the same moment as the anchor's. The whole command is one undo step, named **Synchronize Audio**.
704	
705	If Frame Job is sure of the match, it's applied straight away. If it isn't, Frame Job [asks you first](/audio/weak-sync-matches/).
706	
707	It's all or nothing. If any clip can't be matched, nothing moves, and [the reasons are listed](#when-it-wont-run).
708	
709	If the clips are already in sync, nothing changes and Frame Job beeps. Choosing the command a second time on the same clips does this.
710	
711	## Which clips it takes
712	
713	**Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio** is available when at least two selected clips can play sound and aren't [nests](/editing/nests/).
714	
715	Anything else in the selection is left out without a message: a nest, a still, a title, a file with no audio track, a clip with its audio switched off. To line up clips inside a nest, open it with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and select them there.
716	
717	## The anchor
718	
719	Frame Job picks the anchor this way:
720	
721	1. Among the selected clips that have a picture, the one that starts earliest. If none has a picture, all of them are considered.
722	2. If two start at the same time, the one on the rearmost track.
723	3. If they're still tied, the one created first.
724	
725	So a camera clip stays put and the recorder moves to it. The anchor is never moved or trimmed, and its speed doesn't change.
726	
727	## Matching by sound
728	
729	Each file's sound is analysed once, after it's imported, into a form that isn't thrown off by differences in gain, microphone or room. Frame Job compares the files, not the clips, so a clip's volume and effects make no difference.
730	
731	- **Speech comes first.** When both clips hold at least 2 seconds of speech, as judged by the on-device voice model, only the speech is compared. Otherwise all the sound is.
732	- **The trimmed parts come first.** Frame Job looks within the parts each clip is trimmed to, when both are at least 2 seconds long. It searches the whole files only if that finds no usable match and at least one clip is trimmed.
733	
734	:::tip
735	A recording with two similar stretches can match the wrong one. Trimming the recorder roughly around the camera's sound tells Frame Job which one you mean.
736	:::
737	
738	## The waveform check
739	
740	Sounding alike isn't enough, because two takes of the same words can look like a match. So a match is used only if the two waveforms also line up there, as a clear peak within 48 ms. Frame Job checks up to 30 seconds of the overlap, where the sound agrees most, in the speech band of 300 to 3,400 Hz.
741	
742	The same check fine-tunes the offset to less than a frame.
743	
744	## Moves land on whole frames
745	
746	Clips move by a whole number of frames at the project's frame rate, so up to half a frame of constant offset can remain. At 30 fps that's about 17 ms.
747	
748	## The head trim
749	
750	If a clip would have to start before 0:00 to line up, it loses that much from its start instead, and starts at 0:00 in sync. Frame Job trims only what it has to. It won't do this if less than a frame of the clip would be left.
751	
752	## Drift correction
753	
754	Two devices' clocks never run at quite the same rate, so a recorder slowly falls out of sync over a long take. When the clips overlap for at least 60 seconds, Frame Job measures that drift in 20-second windows along the overlap and corrects it by playing the moved clip at a slightly different speed, at most 0.2 % from ×1.
755	
756	The correction is part of the same undo step. There's no drift figure to read. What changes is the clip's speed, and **Keep pitch** is turned off. The [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/) shows the rate to two decimal places, so a correction such as ×1.0004 still reads 1.00× there. The clip gets very slightly longer or shorter to match.
757	
758	Drift is left alone when:
759	
760	- it's under 5 ms across the overlap
761	- it's too small to tell from no drift, meaning under three times its own uncertainty
762	- correcting it would take more than 0.2 % from ×1
763	- too little of the overlap matches to measure it
764	
765	:::note
766	The correction plays the sound slightly faster or slower, as tape would, so the pitch moves very slightly with the speed. Like any clip with Keep pitch off at a speed other than ×1, the clip's sound is [rendered in the background](/speed/keep-pitch/#tape-pitch-is-rendered-in-the-background). It's briefly silent in the preview after the correction, and again after each trim, split or speed change. An export waits for it.
767	:::
768	
769	## The Synchronizing Audio sheet
770	
771	Matching runs in the background behind a **Synchronizing Audio** sheet, with a progress bar and the line "Matching the sound of N clips…". Nothing moves until a match is found.
772	
773	**Cancel** or <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the sheet and leaves everything as it was.
774	
775	If the project changes while the matching runs, for example because an agent edits it or moves in or out of a nest, nothing is applied. Frame Job beeps and the inspector says to choose Synchronize Audio again.
776	
777	## When it won't run
778	
779	Frame Job beeps and lists every reason in [the strip at the foot of the inspector](/getting-started/refused-edits/#the-refusal-strip), naming each clip by its number. The strip shows three lines, so hover over it to read a long one.
780	
781	It checks each clip first, and won't start matching until they all pass. A clip can't be lined up when it:
782	
783	- plays no sound in the timeline
784	- is still being analysed. Its sound or speech analysis hasn't finished, so try again in a moment.
785	- comes from a file with under 2 seconds of sound
786	- plays more than 0.2 % away from ×1. Set it back to ×1 first.
787	- plays at a different rate from the ×1 its speed shows, because its source is stretched
788	- plays [reversed](/speed/reverse/)
789	- [ramps its speed](/speed/speed-ramps/), because a speed action changes its rate over its length
790	
791	The rest come up during the matching:
792	
793	- Two of the clips are on one track. Each needs its own.
794	- A clip has no sound to line up by, because its analysis found no sound at all.
795	- Nothing matches. See [When nothing matches](/audio/weak-sync-matches/#when-nothing-matches).
796	- A clip matches the anchor's sound but the waveforms don't line up there, for example two takes of the same words. They aren't one recording.
797	- A clip matches the anchor's sound but the two share under 2 seconds of waveform there, too little to confirm it's one recording.
798	- A clip would lose so much of its head that less than a frame is left.
799	- A clip would never play at the same time as the anchor once lined up. Extend its trim, or the anchor's.
800	- A clip would overlap another clip on its own track after the move. Move that clip out of the way, or put this one on a free track.
801	
802	## With an agent
803	
804	`sync_audio` does the same thing. An agent can name the anchor, and it's told by name when it passes a nest or a clip that plays no sound, where the menu leaves those out. Its answer also gives each clip's offset, confidence, trim and drift, and clips already in sync are reported as such. See [Tools: audio](/mcp/tools-audio/).
805	
806	## Related
807	
808	- [Confident and weak matches](/audio/weak-sync-matches/)
809	- [The Speed section](/speed/speed-section/)
810	- [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/)
811	- [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/)
812	- [Nests](/editing/nests/)
813	---
814	title: Track compressor and limiter
815	description: Compress and limit a track's whole sound, or everything in a nest together, and know where the preview differs from the export.
816	---
817	
818	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
819	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
820	
821	A track can have its own compressor and limiter, acting on the sound of every clip on it together. Use them to even out a whole voice-over, or to hold a music bed under a ceiling, without setting each clip. This page covers a track's. A clip has its own [compressor](/audio/compressor/) and [limiter](/audio/limiter/).
822	
823	<AtAGlance
824	  menu="Track ▸ Mix…"
825	  where={['The sliders switch in the track header', "Mix… in the track's right-click menu"]}
826	  tools="set_track"
827	/>
828	
829	## Turn on a track's compressor or limiter
830	
831	<Steps>
832	
833	1. Open the [Track Mix panel](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/#open-the-track-mix-panel) for the track.
834	
835	2. Tick **Compressor** or **Limit peaks**, below **Pan**. Each turns on at its defaults, and its rows stop being greyed out.
836	
837	3. Adjust the rows.
838	
839	</Steps>
840	
841	Unticking throws the settings away, so ticking again starts from the defaults. **Reset** at the foot of the panel turns both off, and resets the track's volume and pan too.
842	
843	The header's sliders switch stays lit while either is on.
844	
845	## Where they sit
846	
847	Both act on the track's whole sound: every clip on it, after each clip's own processing, its volume, fades, crossfades and ducking, and after the track's volume and pan. The compressor runs first, then the limiter.
848	
849	A track's compressor and limiter hear the track after its fader. That's the difference from a clip's compressor, which hears the clip before its volume. Turning the track down turns down what reaches them, so a compressor at −20 dB over a track at −6 dB compresses less.
850	
851	## Compressor settings
852	
853	| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick picks |
854	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
855	| **Compressor** | Turns the track's compressor on. | on, off | off | |
856	| **Threshold** | The level above which it starts turning the track down. | −60 to 0 dB | −18 dB | −30, −24, −18, −12, −6 |
857	| **Ratio** | How strongly it turns down sound above the threshold. | 1 to 20 :1 | 3:1 | 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 8, 20 |
858	| **Attack** | How quickly it reacts. | 0 to 200 ms | 10 ms | 1, 5, 10, 30, 100 ms |
859	| **Release** | How quickly it lets go. | 10 to 2000 ms | 200 ms | 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000 ms |
860	| **Makeup** | Gain added afterwards. | 0 to 24 dB | 0 dB | 0, 3, 6, 12 |
861	
862	## Limiter settings
863	
864	| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick picks |
865	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
866	| **Limit peaks** | Turns the track's limiter on. | on, off | off | |
867	| **Ceiling** | The highest true peak the track may hand the mix. | −24 to 0 dBTP | −1 dBTP | −1, −2, −3, −6 |
868	| **Release** | How quickly the level recovers after a peak. | 1 to 1000 ms | 100 ms | 50, 100, 200, 500 ms |
869	
870	Each control is a slider and a field. A number typed outside the range goes to the nearest end of it.
871	
872	## Use a track as a nest's bus
873	
874	A bus is one path that several sounds share. A [nest's](/editing/nests/) whole mix plays through the track its nest clip sits on, so a compressor or limiter on that track acts on everything inside the nest together. Put a voice's clips in a nest and compress them as one, whatever tracks they're on inside it.
875	
876	A nest's own tracks have no compressor or limiter. Inside an open nest, both sections are greyed out, and their tooltip says "A nest's mix plays through the dynamics of the track that holds it." **Volume**, **Pan** and **Reset** still work there.
877	
878	Nesting a selection doesn't copy a compressor or limiter from the tracks it came from. The track the nest clip lands on keeps its own.
879	
880	## Exact in the export, approximate in the preview
881	
882	An export plays each track with a compressor or limiter through them on its own, before the tracks are mixed. That's exact, and a [stem](/export/stems/) of that track includes them. The [master limiter](/export/loudness/) still runs over the mix afterwards.
883	
884	The preview can only approximate this. Where a track's clips overlap, such as a crossfade or a nest's tracks, the preview plays the track's sound in more than one piece and runs the compressor and limiter on each piece separately. So the pieces can add up past a track limiter's ceiling while you edit, even though the export holds it.
885	
886	While any track has a compressor or limiter and the preview plays at normal speed, the [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/) says so in its footer: "The mix as the preview plays it, with track compressors and limiters approximate, before the export's loudness and master limiter."
887	
888	:::tip
889	Judge a track limiter's ceiling on the export, not on the preview's meters.
890	:::
891	
892	## What hears them
893	
894	| Hears them | Doesn't hear them |
895	| --- | --- |
896	| The preview, approximately | [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) |
897	| The [level meter](/audio/level-meter/) and the [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/), approximately | The [Loudness read-out](/audio/volume/#read-the-level) |
898	| Every export and stem, exactly | [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) and [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) |
899	| | A [scrub](/audio/scrub-audio/) |
900	
901	Normalize, the Loudness read-out, Enhance Voice and Match Audio work on the clip itself, before the track.
902	
903	## Good to know
904	
905	- A track's compressor and limiter are one setting for the whole track, and can't change over time. A track has no EQ or other effects.
906	- Each change is one undo step. Turning one on or off, a drag or a typed value is named "Track Compressor" or "Track Limiter", and **Reset** is named "Reset Track Mix".
907	- A track with a limiter plays 3.3 ms later in the preview, and Frame Job places it 3.3 ms earlier to match, so it stays in sync.
908	
909	## With an agent
910	
911	`set_track` sets both, through its `compressor` and `limiter` arguments. Each takes the whole setting at once, so any value you leave out goes to its default, and `null` turns it off. As in the panel, a nest's own tracks can't have them. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#a-tracks-compressor-and-limiter).
912	
913	## Related
914	
915	- [Track volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/)
916	- [Compressor](/audio/compressor/)
917	- [Limiter](/audio/limiter/)
918	- [The Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/)
919	- [Export loudness](/export/loudness/)
920	---
921	title: Track volume and pan
922	description: Set a whole track's level and left-right balance in the Track Mix panel, on top of what each clip already does.
923	---
924	
925	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
926	
927	Each track has its own volume and pan, applied on top of every clip on it. Use them to balance a music bed against a voice-over without touching each clip.
928	
929	<AtAGlance
930	  menu="Track ▸ Mix…"
931	  where={['The sliders switch in the track header', "Mix… in the track's right-click menu"]}
932	  tools="set_track"
933	/>
934	
935	## Open the Track Mix panel
936	
937	Click the sliders switch, the fifth in the track's header. **Mix…** in the track's right-click menu does the same. **Track ▸ Mix…** opens it for the [current track](/timeline/tracks/#the-current-track), and has no keyboard shortcut.
938	
939	A small panel opens beside the header, with the track's name at the top. It holds **Volume**, **Pan**, the track's [compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/), and **Reset**.
940	
941	There's one panel per timeline, so opening it on another track closes the first. Clicking away closes it, and so does anything that takes its track away: removing the track, undoing it away, or going into or out of a nest.
942	
943	The sliders switch is lit while the track's volume or pan is off its default, or a compressor or limiter is on.
944	
945	## Set a track's volume
946	
947	| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
948	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
949	| **Volume** | The track's level, as a slider and a field in dB. Beside them, a read-out shows the level as a percentage, or "Off". | Off (at −60) to +12 dB | 0 dB |
950	
951	The quick picks on the field are −12, −6, −3, 0, +3 and +6 dB. Drag the slider to its left end, or type −60, to turn the track off. A number typed outside the range goes to the nearest end of it.
952	
953	Track volume multiplies what's on the track. A clip at 200 % on a track at −12 dB plays at −6 dB. A muted track is silent whatever its volume.
954	
955	## Set a track's pan
956	
957	| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
958	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
959	| **Pan** | Leans the track's sound left or right, as a slider and a field. | −100 (left) to 100 (right) | 0 |
960	
961	The quick picks are −100, −50, 0, 50 and 100.
962	
963	Pan is a balance, like a [clip's pan](/audio/pan-and-mono/), and keeps the overall loudness steady as it moves. It applies after each clip's own pan, and two pans multiply, so a clip panned left on a track panned left leans further left. It has no effect on a mono source.
964	
965	## Reset the mix
966	
967	**Reset** puts the volume back to 0 dB and the pan to the centre, and turns the track's compressor and limiter off. Inside an open nest, it resets volume and pan only. It's greyed out when there's nothing to reset.
968	
969	Each change is one undo step. A drag, a typed value or a quick pick is named "Track Volume" or "Track Pan", and **Reset** is named "Reset Track Mix".
970	
971	## Track volume in a nest
972	
973	A clip inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) plays through its own track inside the nest, and through the track the nest clip sits on.
974	
975	- **Nesting from one track keeps its sound.** The nest's copy of that track starts at 0 dB and centre, because the track the nest clip lands on still applies.
976	- **Clips from the selection's other tracks** keep their own track's volume and pan inside the nest, and also get the destination track's.
977	- **Un-nesting** puts the clips back on the timeline's tracks without the nest's track settings.
978	- **Mix to mono on a nest clip** folds everything inside it, so the pans of the tracks inside no longer apply.
979	
980	## What hears track volume
981	
982	Track volume is part of what you hear, so it shows up wherever Frame Job measures the mix, and not where it measures a clip.
983	
984	| Hears it | Doesn't hear it |
985	| --- | --- |
986	| The preview and every export, which sound the same | [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) |
987	| The [level meter](/audio/level-meter/) | The [Loudness read-out](/audio/volume/#read-the-level) |
988	| [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) | A clip's [limiter](/audio/limiter/) |
989	
990	So a track turned up can take a limited clip past its ceiling. Use the track's own [limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) to hold what the whole track hands the mix.
991	
992	## Good to know
993	
994	A track's volume and pan are one value for the whole track, and can't change over time. To ride the level, use a clip's [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) or [actions](/audio/animate-sound/).
995	
996	## With an agent
997	
998	`set_track` sets both, with different scales from the panel. `volume` is a linear gain from 0 to 4, where 1 is 0 dB, 4 is +12 dB and 0 is silent. `pan` runs from −1 (left) to 1 (right). A value outside those ranges changes nothing, where a number typed in the panel goes to the nearest end. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#set_track).
999	
1000	## Related
1001	
1002	- [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/)
1003	- [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/)
1004	- [Clip volume](/audio/volume/)
1005	- [Pan and Mix to mono](/audio/pan-and-mono/)
1006	---
1007	title: Voice effects
1008	description: Give a clip's sound one of sixteen effects, from a pitch shift or a phone line to a cathedral, and set how much of it you hear.
1009	---
1010	
1011	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
1012	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1013	
1014	Voice Effect changes the character of a clip's sound: pitch a voice up or down, squeeze it into a phone line, or put it in a hall. A clip has one effect at a time.
1015	
1016	<AtAGlance

890	
891	Cleaning up a clip changes how loud it measures, so the analysis alone would miss the target. In Loudness mode, a clip with any of these is rendered through them as the export plays it, and its volume is set from what comes out:
892	
893	- An active [EQ](/audio/eq/)
894	- [Hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/)
895	- [Voice isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/)
896	- [Noise reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/)
897	- A [gate](/audio/gate/)
898	- The [leveller](/audio/leveller/)
899	- A [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/)
900	- A [compressor](/audio/compressor/)
901	- A [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/)
902	
903	With the limiter on as well, Normalize renders again at the volume it chose, and adjusts until the result is within 0.1 LU of the target, at most three times. A clip measured this way keeps its volume when the new one is within 0.05 dB of it and its limiter hasn't changed, so a second press still changes nothing.
904	
905	This takes a moment per clip, seconds on a long one, and the first press waits for the clip's voice isolation or voice effect to render. A clip with none of this processing is measured from the analysis at once.
906	
907	Until Normalize or Enhance Voice has measured such a clip, the **At volume** read-out shows "≈" in front of its figures, because they're from before the processing. See [Clip volume](/audio/volume/).
908	
909	## The Measuring Sound sheet
910	
911	While clips are rendered through their processing, a **Measuring Sound** sheet shows a progress bar and "Clip 1 of 2…", counting only the clips that need a render. Editing commands are off until it closes. [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) and [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) use the same sheet.
912	
913	Nothing changes until every clip is measured, and **Cancel** leaves everything as it is. If the project changes while it measures, nothing changes, Frame Job beeps, and a sentence at the foot of the inspector says to choose the command again.
914	
915	## Clips Normalize skips
916	
917	Normalize leaves out the clips below and still does the rest. The button and the menu item are dimmed when no selected clip plays sound, or when only nests are selected. A press that changes nothing beeps, and neither the button nor the menu says which clips were skipped or why.
918	
919	| Skipped | Why | Mode |
920	| --- | --- | --- |
921	| Nests | Their level lives in the clips inside them. Open the nest and normalize those, or set the nest clip's volume by hand. | Both |
922	| Shapes, titles, stills and movies with no sound | There's no sound to measure. A clip with its sound switched off counts too. | Both |
923	| A clip not analysed yet | Its waveform or loudness is still being worked out, which often happens straight after an import. The **Loudness** read-out says "measuring…" meanwhile. | Both |
924	| A silent clip | It's silent over the part that plays. In Loudness mode that means quieter than −70 LUFS throughout. | Both |
925	| A very short clip | It plays for under 0.4 s, too short for a loudness measurement. | Loudness |
926	| A clip whose reversed copy is still being made | It can't be rendered yet. | Loudness, through processing |
927	| A clip whose processing can't be rendered | There's nothing to measure. | Loudness, through processing |
928	| A clip that's too quiet after its processing | It's quieter than −70 LUFS after it. | Loudness, through processing |
929	
930	## Good to know
931	
932	- Normalize writes the clip's base level, even with the playhead inside an action. With an action selected, the button carries a small boxed "clip" tag to show this. If an action animates the volume, its values still win for as long as it runs.
933	- It can go past the slider's 400 %, up to the 3200 % ceiling, about +30 dB.
934	- The result for a limited clip with no other processing is worked out from the analysis, not rendered, so the export can land slightly off it.
935	- A clip played at a speed other than ×1, or ramped, reads to within about 0.5 LU of what plays. A file with more than two channels has its loudness measured from a two-channel mix of it.
936	
937	## With an agent
938	
939	`normalize_clip` names its own mode and doesn't read the **Normalize** row. In Peak mode it can aim anywhere from −60 to 0 dBFS, and it reports what each clip measured, where it landed, and each skipped clip with its reason. See [Tools: audio](/mcp/tools-audio/).
940	
941	## Related
942	
943	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)
944	- [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/)
945	- [Clip volume](/audio/volume/)
946	- [Limiter](/audio/limiter/)
947	- [Export loudness](/export/loudness/)
948	---
949	title: "Enhance Voice"
950	description: "Measure a voice recording and set up its cleaning, dynamics and volume in one step, with ordinary settings you can see and change."
951	---
952	
953	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
954	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
955	
956	Enhance Voice sets a clip up for speech in one step. It measures the voice and the pauses, chooses the clean-up and dynamics the recording needs, and sets the volume that reaches your loudness target.
957	
958	<AtAGlance
959	  menu="Clip ▸ Enhance Voice"
960	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound sub-tab ▸ Volume section"
961	  tools="enhance_voice"
962	  needs="Nothing. Speech detection and voice isolation run on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
963	/>
964	
965	## Enhance a voice
966	
967	<Steps>
968	
969	1. Select one or more clips with speech in them.
970	
971	2. Check the target in the **Normalize** row of the **Volume** section. It's −16 LUFS unless you've [chosen another](/audio/normalize/#set-the-loudness-target).
972	
973	3. Press **Enhance Voice**, or choose **Clip ▸ Enhance Voice**.
974	
975	4. Wait for the [Measuring Sound sheet](/audio/normalize/#the-measuring-sound-sheet) to finish.
976	
977	</Steps>
978	
979	However many clips are selected, it's one undo step, named "Enhance Voice". **Cancel** in the sheet changes nothing. If the project changes while it measures, nothing changes either, and a sentence at the foot of the inspector says to choose the command again.
980	
981	Everything it writes is an ordinary setting, so you can see and change each one in its own section. Pressing it again changes nothing and beeps, and so does [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) at the same target afterwards.
982	
983	To run it on a recording as soon as the recording lands, see [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).
984	
985	## What it measures
986	
987	It reads the clip before any of the settings it's about to write: its loudness and true peak, and, every 10 ms of the part that plays, whether the clip is speaking or pausing. It needs at least a second of speech, and half a second of pause to measure the noise between words.
988	
989	## What it sets
990	
991	Each of these is a separate decision, made from the clip's own measurements.
992	
993	### Rumble cut
994	
995	It always sets the [EQ](/audio/eq/)'s **Rumble Cut**, a high-pass at 80 Hz, 24 dB/oct, to take out low rumble, and keeps the EQ's other parts.
996	
997	### Noisy pauses
998	
999	The pauses count as noisy when their median loudness is less than 45 dB under the voice.
1000	
1001	| The pauses are | What it does |
1002	| --- | --- |
1003	| Noisy | Turns on [voice isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) at 80 % with noise reduction off, and fits a [gate](/audio/gate/) to the pauses. |
1004	| Noisy, on a clip with a speed change, a ramp or a freeze frame | Turns on [noise reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/) at 50 % with voice isolation off, because isolation can't serve that clip, and fits the gate. |
1005	| Quiet | Turns voice isolation, noise reduction and the gate off. |
1006	| Under half a second long in total | Leaves all three as they are, because there's nothing to measure. |
1007	
1008	The gate opens 10 dB above the pauses' median true peak, held between −40 and −6 dB relative to the clip's loudness.
1009	
1010	### Leveller
1011	
1012	It turns on the [leveller](/audio/leveller/) at its defaults when the speech's loudness varies a lot from moment to moment, meaning its short-term loudness range is over 6 LU. The range is measured over 3-second stretches of the speech alone. At or under 6 LU the leveller is turned off, and with under 3 seconds of speech it's left as it is.
1013	
1014	### De-esser
1015	
1016	It turns on the [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) at its defaults when at least 5 % of the speech has a hot "s" band: 6 kHz and up, within 10 dB of the clip's loudness. Otherwise it's turned off.
1017	
1018	### Compressor, limiter and final volume
1019	
1020	Every clip it enhances gets all three, whatever else it measured.
1021	
1022	- A [compressor](/audio/compressor/) at 3:1, its threshold at the speech's median true peak, with makeup that gives back the loudness it takes.
1023	- The [limiter](/audio/limiter/). The clip keeps its own, with the ceiling at most −1 dBTP, or gets the default.
1024	- The volume that takes the clip to the **Normalize** row's target, measured through everything above as the export plays it. It's checked by rendering, to within 0.1 LU, up to three times.
1025	
1026	The target is used even when the row is set to Peak and the field is dimmed. Enhance Voice always aims at a loudness.
1027	
1028	## What it leaves alone
1029	
1030	Hum removal, the channel choice, pan, mono, fades, ducking, **Mute**, **Keep pitch** and the EQ's other parts all stay as they are. Like Normalize, it writes the clip's base settings, even with the playhead inside an action.
1031	
1032	## Clips Enhance Voice skips
1033	
1034	It's offered where [Normalize](/audio/normalize/#clips-normalize-skips) is, and it leaves out the same clips as Normalize in Loudness mode, plus two more. The rest of the selection is still enhanced. With nothing to enhance, the press beeps, and neither the button nor the menu says why.
1035	
1036	| Skipped | Why |
1037	| --- | --- |
1038	| A clip that plays no sound, or a nest | There's no voice of its own to measure. Open a nest to enhance the clips inside. |
1039	| A clip that plays for under 0.4 s | It's too short for a loudness measurement. |
1040	| A clip quieter than −70 LUFS, before or after its processing | There's no voice to work with. |
1041	| A clip with under 1 second of speech | There's too little to measure a voice from. |
1042	| A clip not analysed yet | See [Wait for analysis](#wait-for-analysis). |
1043	| A clip whose reversed copy is still being made | It can't be rendered yet. |
1044	| A clip whose processing can't be rendered | There's nothing to measure. |
1045	
1046	## Wait for analysis
1047	
1048	Enhance Voice needs two results that are worked out on your Mac after a file is imported: the clip's loudness and its speech. A clip without both yet is skipped, which often happens straight after an import. The **Loudness** read-out says "measuring…" while the loudness is still running. Wait a moment and press again.
1049	
1050	## Check its gate by ear
1051	
1052	Enhance Voice sets the gate from the pauses it measured. On a voice with very soft word starts, the gate can bite into them, so listen to those words and lower the [gate](/audio/gate/)'s threshold if you need to.
1053	
1054	## Good to know
1055	
1056	- Applying the rumble cut also takes the EQ out of bypass if you'd bypassed it.
1057	- Every clip it enhances ends up with its limiter on, because the volume is solved through it.
1058	- Measuring takes time in proportion to the clip's length, and it waits for the clip's voice isolation to render first.
1059	- Two clips in a selection can end up with different settings, because each is measured on its own.
1060	
1061	## With an agent
1062	
1063	`enhance_voice` takes its own target rather than the **Normalize** row's. It reports what it measured for each clip, exactly which settings it wrote, and one sentence per rule saying why, so an agent can tell you what the button doesn't. Each skipped clip comes back with its reason. See [Tools: audio](/mcp/tools-audio/).

The three times use an [agent's time units](/mcp/units-and-ids/), not milliseconds. An empty `gate` turns it on at the defaults and `null` turns it off. 977	title: "Hum removal"
978	description: "Notch out mains hum at 50 or 60 Hz and its harmonics, and leave the voice between them alone."
979	---
980	
981	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
982	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
983	
984	Hum removal cuts the low electrical hum that mains power can leave on a recording. It places a narrow notch at the mains frequency and at each of its multiples, and leaves the sound between the notches alone.
985	
986	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Hum" tools="set_audio" />
987	
988	## Remove hum
989	
990	<Steps>
991	
992	1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **Hum** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
993	
994	2. Tick **Remove hum**. It starts at 60 Hz, 30 dB deep, with 4 harmonics.
995	
996	3. Set **Mains** to the frequency where the recording was made: 50 Hz in most of the world, 60 Hz in most of the Americas and parts of Asia.
997	
998	4. If you can still hear the hum, raise **Depth** or **Harmonics**.
999	
1000	</Steps>
1001	
1002	The other controls are dimmed until **Remove hum** is ticked. **Reset** in the section's header turns hum removal off.
1003	
1004	## The controls
1005	
1006	| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
1007	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
1008	| **Remove hum** | Turns hum removal on. | On or off | Off |
1009	| **Mains** | The mains frequency where the recording was made. | 50 Hz or 60 Hz | 60 Hz |
1010	| **Depth** | How far each notch turns the hum down. Quick values: 12, 24, 30 and 48 dB. | 6 to 60 dB | 30 dB |
1011	| **Harmonics** | How many notches: the mains frequency and its multiples. Quick values: 1, 2, 4 and 8. | 1 to 8 | 4 |
1012	
1013	At 60 Hz with 4 harmonics, the notches sit at 60, 120, 180 and 240 Hz.
1014	
1015	Each notch is about a tenth of the mains frequency wide, whatever its depth, so a notch at 60 Hz is about 6 Hz wide.
1016	
1017	## Good to know
1018	
1019	- Hum removal runs after the [EQ](/audio/eq/). Its notches appear in the EQ section's drawn curve, but the EQ's **Bypass** doesn't turn them off.
1020	- Hum removal only reaches the mains frequency and its multiples. For hiss, fans or other steady noise, use [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/), which comes after it.
1021	- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, these controls set where the action ends. **Depth** glides across the action. **Mains**, **Harmonics** and turning hum removal on or off change at the action's end, with no glide.
1022	- Hum removal set on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip has no effect. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
1023	
1024	## With an agent
1025	
1026	`set_audio` sets the same controls through `hum`, with `frequency`, `depth_db` and `harmonics`. An empty `hum` turns it on at the defaults and `null` turns it off. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#hum-removal).
1027

1034	title: J-cuts and L-cuts
1035	description: Let a shot's sound start before its picture, or run on under the next shot, by trimming the sound half of a linked pair.
1036	---
1037	
1038	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
1039	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1040	
1041	A J-cut brings in the next shot's sound before its picture. An L-cut lets a shot's sound run on under the next shot. Both soften a cut, and in Frame Job both come from trimming the sound half of a [detached clip](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
1042	
1043	<AtAGlance
1044	  keys={['W', 'E']}
1045	  where={["Timeline: drag a detached sound clip's edge", 'Timeline: ⌥⇧-drag an edge to roll']}
1046	  tools={['trim_start', 'trim_end', 'roll']}
1047	/>
1048	
1049	## Make a J-cut
1050	
1051	<Steps>
1052	
1053	1. Select the later shot and press <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd> to [detach its audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/#detach-audio).
1054	
1055	2. If the shot before it is detached too, drag this sound to a track of its own. See [Keep the sound off its neighbour](#keep-the-sound-off-its-neighbour).
1056	
1057	3. Drag the sound clip's start edge to the left.
1058	
1059	</Steps>
1060	
1061	The sound now begins before its picture. The picture stays where it is.
1062	
1063	## Make an L-cut
1064	
1065	<Steps>
1066	
1067	1. Select the earlier shot and press <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd>.
1068	
1069	2. If the next shot's sound is on the track the sound went to, drag this sound to a track of its own.
1070	
1071	3. Drag the sound clip's end edge to the right.
1072	
1073	</Steps>
1074	
1075	The sound now runs on after its picture has ended.
1076	
1077	## Keep the sound off its neighbour
1078	
1079	When two neighbouring shots are both detached, their sounds sit side by side on one track. Lengthening one into the other overlaps them, and an overlap on a track is a [cross dissolve](/audio/crossfades/), not a split edit. On a track of its own, the sound overlaps nothing.
1080	
1081	## How far the sound can go
1082	
1083	A trim can only reveal what's in the file. The sound stops at the first or last frame of its media, and at the start of the timeline. Choose a shot with spare sound before its in point for a J-cut, or after its out point for an L-cut.
1084	
1085	The sound has to keep at least one frame. If it runs into another clip on its track, Frame Job allows an overlap of up to half the shorter clip and won't go further.
1086	
1087	## Trim and roll a sound clip alone
1088	
1089	The half you grab decides what moves. An edit on the sound moves only the sound. An edit on the picture also moves the sound when their edges line up. A lead you've already made isn't lined up, so trimming that picture's start leaves the sound alone.
1090	
1091	Dragging is what lengthens a sound. <kbd>W</kbd> and <kbd>E</kbd> [trim to the playhead](/editing/trimming/#trim-to-the-playhead), so they only shorten it, and they do it to the sound alone. To roll the cut between two sound clips on one track, hold <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> and drag the edge between them. A sound on a track of its own has no cut to roll.
1092	
1093	See [Move a sound clip's edge alone](/editing/slip-and-roll/#move-a-sound-clips-edge-alone).
1094	
1095	## Good to know
1096	
1097	- Moving either half keeps the lead. When a drag would take the sound past the start of the timeline, both clips stop together.
1098	- A ripple edit that would push a leading sound past the start of the timeline doesn't happen.
1099	- Frame Job won't [attach](/audio/detach-and-attach/#attach-audio) a pair that no longer covers the same time. Trim the two to the same start and end first.
1100	- [Slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/#slip-a-clip) takes both halves, unless the other half is on a locked track.
1101	
1102	## With an agent
1103	
1104	In the app, a trim on a sound moves it alone. An agent has to ask for that: pass `alone: true` to `trim_start`, `trim_end` or `roll` on the sound. Without it, a trim on a sound whose edge lines up with its picture moves both. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/).
1105

1113	title: "The level meter"
1114	description: Read the two-row meter in the timeline bar to see how loud the mix is while it plays, and whether it reaches full scale.
1115	---
1116	
1117	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1118	
1119	The level meter shows how high the mix you're hearing sits while the timeline plays, and warns you when a sample reaches full scale, the loudest level digital sound can hold.
1120	
1121	<AtAGlance where="The timeline bar, left of the zoom controls" />
1122	
1123	## What it shows
1124	
1125	The meter shows what you hear: each clip's volume, fades, ducking, mute and solo, and the compressor and other effects. Press play and it moves. There's nothing to turn on.
1126	
1127	It has two rows, one per channel, with the left channel on top. A mono track shows in both rows, and a track with more than two channels shows only its first two.
1128	
1129	At normal speed it measures the mix itself, so two tracks playing the same sound read as one louder sound, and a sound and its inverse read as silence. At any other speed it adds up each track's level instead. That can read a little higher than the mix, and it can light the clip cell when the mix itself wouldn't reach full scale.
1130	
1131	## Read the meter
1132	
1133	Each row runs from −60 dB on the left to 0 dB on the right. The scale is even in dB, so the middle of a row is −30 dB. It has no tick marks.
1134	
1135	| Part | What it tells you |
1136	| --- | --- |
1137	| **Solid bar** | The average (RMS) level. It rises at once and falls at 24 dB a second. |
1138	| **Lighter wash** behind the bar | The instantaneous peak. It rises and falls the same way, and it's never shorter than the bar. |
1139	| **Peak-hold mark** | The highest recent level. It stays for about 1.2 seconds, then falls at 12 dB a second. |
1140	| **Clip cell** at the right end of each row | Lights for 2 seconds whenever a sample in that row reaches full scale. |
1141	
1142	A level above 0 dB fills the row and goes no further, so the clip cell is what tells you the mix went over.
1143	
1144	## When playback stops
1145	
1146	The bars fall back to the floor. The peak-hold mark stops waiting and falls with them, and a lit clip cell stays lit for the rest of its 2 seconds. The whole meter is at rest within about 3 seconds.
1147	
1148	## Good to know
1149	
1150	- The meter shows peaks and average level, not loudness. For LUFS and true peak, use [the Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/).
1151	- It shows the preview's mix. An export also goes through a master limiter, so what an export measures can differ. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/).
1152	- There's one meter for the whole app. With two projects open, the meter in both windows follows the one that's playing, and stopping one project doesn't blank the meter while the other plays on.
1153	- In a narrow window the meter gets smaller, and below 40 points wide it isn't drawn at all.
1154	- The recorder panel has its own meter for the microphone. See [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/).
1155	
1156	## Related

1160	- [Limiter](/audio/limiter/)

1017	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect"
1018	  tools="set_audio"
1019	  needs="Nothing. Apple's audio units render the effect on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
1020	/>
1021	
1022	## Choose an effect
1023	
1024	<Steps>
1025	
1026	1. Select the clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab.
1027	
1028	2. Open the **Voice Effect** section.
1029	
1030	3. Choose an effect from **Effect**. The list names each one with its group, such as **Space: Hall**.
1031	
1032	4. Set [Amount](#set-the-amount), and [Pitch](#set-the-pitch) for the three effects that use it.
1033	
1034	</Steps>
1035	
1036	Frame Job renders the effect in the background, and you hear it [when that's done](#when-you-hear-the-effect). Each effect keeps the clip at about the loudness it had, so switching between them doesn't jump in level.
1037	
1038	To take the effect off, choose **None**, or choose **Reset** in the section's header. The header shows the effect and its amount, such as "Space: Hall 100%", or "off".
1039	
1040	With several clips selected, a change applies to all of them. **Amount** and **Pitch** give every selected clip the first clip's whole effect, not only the value you changed. See [Edit several clips at once](/audio/sound-tab/#edit-several-clips-at-once).
1041	
1042	## The effects
1043	
1044	The figures here are at an Amount of 100 %.
1045	
1046	### Voice
1047	
1048	| Effect | What it does |
1049	| --- | --- |
1050	| **Voice: Pitch** | Shifts the voice up or down without changing its speed. It starts at 0 semitones, so it changes nothing until you set [Pitch](#set-the-pitch). |
1051	| **Voice: High** | Shifts the voice up 5 semitones, cuts the lows below 150 Hz and lifts the highs above 4 kHz by 3 dB, for a small, high voice. |
1052	| **Voice: Deep** | Shifts the voice down 5 semitones, adds 4 dB of low weight below 150 Hz and takes 3 dB off the highs above 5 kHz. |
1053	| **Voice: Robot** | Makes the voice metallic and buzzing, with a 60 Hz ring modulator and a short 8 ms delay. |
1054	
1055	### Tone
1056	
1057	| Effect | What it does |
1058	| --- | --- |
1059	| **Tone: Bass** | Boosts the lows below 200 Hz by 10 dB. |
1060	| **Tone: Treble** | Boosts the highs above 3 kHz by 10 dB. |
1061	| **Tone: Bright** | Lifts the presence with 4 dB around 3 kHz, and the air with 6 dB above 8 kHz. |
1062	| **Tone: Telephone** | Squeezes the sound into the narrow band of a phone line, 300 Hz to 3.4 kHz. |
1063	| **Tone: Radio** | Squeezes the sound into 400 Hz to 4.5 kHz and adds a radio tower's crackle. |
1064	
1065	### Character
1066	
1067	| Effect | What it does |
1068	| --- | --- |
1069	| **Character: Lo-Fi** | Limits the sound to 150 Hz to 6 kHz and crushes it, so it's gritty and dull, like a low-resolution recording. |
1070	| **Character: Distorted** | Overdrives the sound into heavy distortion. |
1071	
1072	### Space
1073	
1074	| Effect | What it does |
1075	| --- | --- |
1076	| **Space: Echo** | Repeats the sound every quarter of a second, each repeat darkened above 6 kHz. |
1077	| **Space: Room** | Puts the sound in a medium room, with a 35 % reverb mix. |
1078	| **Space: Hall** | Puts the sound in a large hall, with a 40 % reverb mix. |
1079	| **Space: Plate** | Adds a plate reverb, with a 35 % mix. |
1080	| **Space: Cathedral** | Puts the sound in a cathedral with a long tail, with a 45 % reverb mix. |
1081	
1082	## Set the amount
1083	
1084	**Amount** is how much of the effect you hear, from 0 to 100 %. It starts at 100 %, and its quick picks are 25, 50 and 100 %. It's greyed out until you choose an effect.
1085	
1086	Every boost, mix and shift scales with it, and the edges of a band move in from where they'd do nothing. At 50 %, **Voice: High** shifts 2.5 semitones and **Tone: Bass** boosts by 5 dB. At 0 the clip plays as it is.
1087	
1088	Choosing another effect keeps the Amount. Choosing **None** forgets it, so the next effect starts at 100 %.
1089	
1090	## Set the pitch
1091	
1092	**Pitch** is the shift in semitones, from −12 to 12. Its quick picks are −12, −5, 0, 5 and 12. It works only for **Voice: Pitch**, **Voice: High** and **Voice: Deep**, and it's greyed out for the rest.
1093	
1094	Choosing one of the three sets Pitch back to that effect's own: 0, +5 or −5. Amount scales the shift too, so a Pitch of 12 at an Amount of 50 % shifts by 6 semitones.
1095	
1096	## Read the status
1097	
1098	**Status** says where the effect's render has got to. With several clips selected it reads "—".
1099	
1100	| Status | What it means |
1101	| --- | --- |
1102	| Off | The clip has no effect, or one that changes nothing, such as an Amount of 0 or **Voice: Pitch** at 0 semitones. |
1103	| Rendering… | The effect is being worked out. Until it's done the clip plays without it. |
1104	| Ready | The clip plays with the effect. |
1105	| Plays without it at this speed | The clip has a speed change, a speed ramp or a freeze frame. An effect plays only at normal speed. |
1106	| Waits for the reversed copy | The clip is reversed and its [reversed copy](/speed/reverse/) isn't ready yet. |
1107	| Not rendered: and a reason | The render failed. The reason might be "its media cannot be found" or "its isolated voice was not rendered". |
1108	
1109	## When you hear the effect
1110	
1111	The effect is worked out once for each clip, in the background. Until it's ready the clip plays without it, and the editor switches over by itself when it is. A clip that isn't at normal speed plays without the effect, and [Status](#read-the-status) says so.
1112	
1113	Changing the effect, Amount, Pitch or the clip's [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) amount works it out again. So does trimming or slipping the clip, because the clip then plays a different part of its file. Moving the clip along the timeline doesn't.
1114	
1115	An export waits for every clip's effect, and its sheet reads "Preparing" and the file's name meanwhile, so a file is never written without one. If a render fails, the export stops and names the clip.
1116	
1117	## Where it sits in the chain
1118	
1119	The effect comes right after Voice Isolation and before everything else in the [Sound tab's order](/audio/how-audio-works/). An isolated clip's effect is made from its isolated voice, so it waits for that first. The channel choice, the EQ, noise reduction and the sections after them all work on the effected sound.
1120	
1121	## Good to know
1122	
1123	- A reverb or an echo stops at the end of the clip. It doesn't ring on into the next one.
1124	- A clip split from a take starts its effect fresh at the cut, so a reverb or echo doesn't carry across the join.
1125	- On a stereo file a reverb or an echo mixes the two channels together, so the [channel choice](/audio/channels/) picks from the effected pair, not from the original left and right.
1126	- The effect can't be animated. Voice Effect is marked ⊘ inside an [action](/audio/animate-sound/), and a change there still applies to the whole clip. It's also made from the clip's own Voice Isolation amount, not an animated one.
1127	- The waveform, the Loudness read-out and [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) hear the clip without its effect. [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode measures through it, and waits for the render first.
1128	- On a nest clip the effect does nothing. Open the [nest](/editing/nests/) and set it on the clips inside.
1129	
1130	## With an agent
1131	
1132	An agent sets the effect with `set_audio`'s `voice`: a `kind`, an `amount` from 0 to 1 (1 if left out) and, for `pitch`, `high` and `deep`, a `pitch` from −12 to 12. The kinds are the effects' names in lower case, with `lofi` for Lo-Fi. `{"voice": null}` takes the effect off.
1133	
1134	Changing the `kind` keeps a stored `pitch` unless the agent sends `pitch: null` with it, where choosing from the list always goes back to the effect's own. An agent can't read Status, though an export still waits for the render. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/).
1135

1153	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Isolation"

1158	## Isolate a voice
1159	
1160	<Steps>
1161	
1162	1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **Voice Isolation** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
1163	
1164	2. Tick **Isolate voice**. The Amount goes to 80 % and **Status** reads "Rendering…".
1165	
1166	3. Keep working. The clip plays without isolation until **Status** reads "Ready", then the editor switches over by itself.
1167	
1168	4. Listen, and change **Amount** if you need to.
1169	
1170	</Steps>
1171	
1172	Isolation also reduces room echo, so there's no separate control for reverb. The section reminds you with the line "Also reduces room echo" under **Status**.
1173	
1174	## The controls
1175	
1176	| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
1177	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
1178	| **Isolate voice** | Turns isolation on at 80 %, or off. | On or off | Off |
1179	| **Amount** | How much of the isolated voice replaces the clip's own sound. Quick values: 50, 80 and 100 %. | 0 to 100 % | 0 % (off) |
1180	| **Status** | What the isolated voice is doing. See [What Status says](#what-status-says). | | Off |
1181	
1182	Setting **Amount** above 0 also turns isolation on, and 0 turns it off. **Reset** in the section's header does the same as unticking the box.
1183	
1184	## Choose an amount
1185	
1186	Amount blends the isolated voice with the clip's own sound.
1187	
1188	- **At 80 %**, the pauses between words drop by about 14 dB and keep a little of the room, so the voice doesn't sit in dead silence. This is what the box turns on.
1189	- **At 100 %**, the pauses are silent.
1190	- **Below that**, more of the original sound comes through.
1191	
1192	Changing Amount takes effect at once. It doesn't need the isolated voice to be worked out again.
1193	
1194	## While it renders
1195	
1196	The isolated voice is worked out once for each clip, in the background, when you turn it on. Until it's ready the clip plays without it, and the editor switches over by itself.
1197	
1198	Trimming or slipping the clip works it out again, because the clip then plays a different part of its file.
1199	
1200	An export waits for every isolated clip to be ready, and its sheet reads "Preparing" and the file's name while it does, so a file is never written without isolation. If a clip's isolated voice can't be made, the export stops with "Clip 12's isolated voice could not be rendered:" and the reason.
1201	
1202	## What Status says
1203	
1204	| Status | What it means |
1205	| --- | --- |
1206	| Off | Isolation is off for this clip. |
1207	| Rendering… | The isolated voice is being worked out. The clip plays without it for now. |
1208	| Ready | The clip plays with isolation. |
1209	| Plays without it at this speed | The clip has a speed change, a ramp or a freeze frame. See below. |
1210	| Waits for the reversed copy | The clip is reversed, and its reversed copy isn't ready yet. |
1211	| Not rendered: and a reason | It failed. "Not rendered: its media cannot be found" means the clip's file has gone missing, so [relink it](/projects/relink-media/). |
1212	| — | Several clips are selected. |
1213	
1214	## Speed, ramps and freeze frames
1215	
1216	Isolation plays only at normal speed. A clip with a [speed change](/speed/change-speed/), a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) or a [freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) plays without it, and **Status** says so.
1217	
1218	A [reversed](/speed/reverse/) clip is isolated once its reversed copy is ready.
1219	
1220	## Good to know
1221	
1222	- Isolation comes first in the clip's sound, before the channel choice, the EQ, noise reduction and the compressor. You can use it with [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/), which then works on the isolated sound. A [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) is made from the isolated voice too. See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
1223	- Two clips cut from one take are isolated separately, so the sound at the join may differ slightly.
1224	- Isolation does nothing on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip, and its **Status** reads "Off". Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
1225	- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, **Isolate voice** and **Amount** set where the action ends, and the Amount glides across the action, from 0 when the clip's own Amount is 0. The isolated voice is still made for a clip whose own isolation is off.
1226	
1227	## With an agent
1228	
1229	`set_audio` sets the amount as `isolation`, from 0 to 1: 0 is off, 0.8 is what the box turns on, and 1 leaves silence between words. An agent can't read **Status**, because the render's state isn't in `get_project`, but an export still waits for it. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/).
1230

1238	title: "The volume line"
1239	description: See a clip's level over time on the timeline, drag it, and add points to shape it.
1240	---
1241	
1242	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
1243	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1244	
1245	The volume line is the thin white line over a clip's waveform. It shows how loud that clip plays over time, and you can drag it to change the level without leaving the timeline.
1246	
1247	<AtAGlance
1248	  keys="⌥-click"
1249	  where="On a clip's audio part in the timeline"
1250	  tools={['set_audio', 'add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_action']}
1251	/>
1252	
1253	## The line on a clip
1254	
1255	Every clip with sound draws the line, except a nest clip. It's the level you hear from that clip, with everything that shapes it folded in:
1256	
1257	- the clip's **Volume** and its volume actions
1258	- its fades and crossfades
1259	- ducking from other clips
1260	- the track's volume
1261	
1262	The top of the clip's audio part is +30 dB (3200 %) and the bottom is −60 dB or quieter. A clip at 100 % sits about a third of the way down.
1263	
1264	A clip you can't hear has its line along the bottom. That's a muted clip, one on a muted track, or one silenced by another track's solo.
1265	
1266	A small square in the action colour marks each action end that sets the volume. Those squares are the line's points.
1267	
1268	The line starts below the [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) and is only drawn where the audio part is at least 12 pt tall, so at the Small [track height](/timeline/track-height/) it may not show.
1269	
1270	## Drag the line
1271	
1272	Press within 3 pt of the line and drag up or down. The press selects the clip. The new level appears beside the pointer, such as "+2.5 dB", or "−∞ dB" at silence. One drag is one undo step, "Set Volume".
1273	
1274	What the drag changes depends on where you press:
1275	
1276	| You press | The drag changes |
1277	| --- | --- |
1278	| Inside an action that sets the volume | That action's end level |
1279	| After such an action | The end level of the last one before the point |
1280	| Anywhere else | The clip's own **Volume** |
1281	
1282	The drag is vertical only and relative to where you pressed. It moves in decibels, and it covers the whole scale over the height of the audio part, so a taller [track](/timeline/track-height/) gives you finer control.
1283	
1284	To go to silence, drag down to the very bottom of the audio part. Upwards, the level stops at 3200 %.
1285	
1286	The readout is the level you're setting, not the sum on the line. The line includes track volume and ducking, but a drag changes only the clip's own level, so on a silenced clip the line stays on the floor while the readout changes.
1287	
1288	## Add a point
1289	
1290	A point lets the level change partway through a clip.
1291	
1292	<Steps>
1293	
1294	1. Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> and click the line where you want the point.
1295	
1296	2. Keep the mouse down and drag to set its level, or let go and drag the line later.
1297	
1298	</Steps>
1299	
1300	A point is an [action](/motion/actions/), not a keyframe. Frame Job adds an action running from the end of the previous action, or the clip's start, up to where you clicked, ending at the volume the clip already has there. The click on its own changes nothing you hear. It's one undo step, "Add Volume Point".
1301	
1302	Inside an action that changes only the volume, the click splits that action in two at the point. Both halves keep its curve, so a linear action sounds the same until you drag, and an eased one eases again on each side of the point.
1303	
1304	The click beeps and adds nothing:
1305	
1306	- inside an action that doesn't set the volume, or that changes anything else as well
1307	- inside an action that runs past the clip's end, as one can after a trim
1308	- within one frame of the clip's start, the start of the action it's in, or the previous action's end
1309	
1310	## Move or remove a point
1311	
1312	To move a point in time, drag its action band. To remove one, select the band and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
1313	
1314	## Clicks that reach the clip instead
1315	
1316	Some presses on the line act on the clip, as they do anywhere else on it:
1317	
1318	| Press | What it does |
1319	| --- | --- |
1320	| <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click | Adds the clip to the selection or takes it out |
1321	| <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd>-drag | Slips the clip |
1322	| Double-click | Renames the clip |
1323	
1324	The fade handles, the action lane and the clip's edges take a press before the line does.
1325	
1326	## Good to know
1327	
1328	- The line doesn't respond on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/).
1329	- A clip with its [sound switched off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/) draws no line, and neither does one playing [too fast to have sound](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
1330	- Inside an open nest, the line is the nest's own mix. It doesn't include the volume, fades, mute or solo of the nest clip and the tracks outside it.
1331	
1332	## With an agent
1333	
1334	There's no separate tool for the line. A drag is `set_audio`, or `set_action_end` on the action that sets the level there, and a point is `add_action` then `set_action_end`, with `set_action` when it splits an action. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).
1335

1343	title: "Confident and weak matches"
1344	description: How Synchronize Audio grades a match, what the Weak match sheet asks you, and what to do when nothing matches.
1345	---
1346	
1347	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
1348	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1349	
1350	[Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) grades every match it finds. A confident match is applied straight away, a weak one is asked about first, and anything less moves nothing.
1351	
1352	<AtAGlance menu="Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio" tools="sync_audio" />
1353	
1354	Each possible offset, meaning how far a clip could move to line up, gets a **confidence**: a score for how far it stands out from every other offset Frame Job tried. A high score means one offset is clearly right. Frame Job keeps up to four candidates, each about a second or more from the others.
1355	
1356	Either grade must also pass [the waveform check](/audio/synchronize-audio/#the-waveform-check). A match that fails it isn't used, however high its confidence, which keeps two takes of the same words apart.
1357	
1358	## Confident matches
1359	
1360	A match is confident when its best candidate has a confidence of at least 10, and is at least 1.5 above the next candidate. A confident match is applied straight away.
1361	
1362	## The Weak match sheet
1363	
1364	A match is weak when no candidate is confident, but the best one within about 3 seconds of where the clip already sits has a confidence of at least 4. A weak match might be unrelated sound, so it's never applied without asking. A **Weak match** sheet appears:
1365	
1366	> Weak match: move “record.aifc” 0.80 s earlier (trimming 0.80 s off its head)?
1367	
1368	A clip that doesn't need to move, only to have its drift corrected, is asked about this way:
1369	
1370	> Weak match: play “record.aifc” at ×1.0004, correcting its drift?
1371	
1372	When several clips are weak, one sheet lists them all, separated by semicolons.
1373	
1374	Under the question, the sheet gives the anchor's name, each match's confidence and the rule it fell short of.
1375	
1376	| Choose | What happens |
1377	| --- | --- |
1378	| **Apply** (the default) | Makes all the changes as one undo step, including those for any clips that matched confidently. |
1379	| **Cancel** or <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Leaves everything as it is, including clips that matched confidently. |
1380	
1381	If you aren't sure, choose **Apply** and play the result. <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> takes all of it back in one step.
1382	
1383	If the project changed while the sheet was up, or an agent moved in or out of a nest, **Apply** moves nothing. Frame Job beeps and the inspector says to choose Synchronize Audio again.
1384	
1385	A weak match that wouldn't change anything isn't asked about.
1386	
1387	A weak match in the trimmed parts ends the search, and the whole files are searched only when the trimmed parts give neither a confident nor a weak match. So if you cancel a weak match, change the trims before trying again.
1388	
1389	## When nothing matches
1390	
1391	If no candidate is confident or weak, nothing moves. [The strip at the foot of the inspector](/getting-started/refused-edits/#the-refusal-strip) names the offsets Frame Job did find and their confidences, for example:
1392	
1393	> Refused: no matching sound found between clip 1 and clip 2: in the played windows, moving clip 2 by +0.77 s (confidence 4.31) or −12.40 s (3.90). A match applies on its own at…
1394	
1395	"The played windows" are the parts each clip is trimmed to, and "the whole files" are listed too when those were searched. A plus sign means later and a minus sign means earlier. Hover over the strip to read the whole message.
1396	
1397	To try again:
1398	
1399	<Steps>
1400	
1401	1. Pick the offset that looks right. You might know roughly where the clip belongs, or one figure may be well ahead of the others.
1402	
1403	2. Move the clip by about that much, so it sits within 3 seconds of the match.
1404	
1405	3. Choose **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio** again. A candidate near the clip with a confidence of at least 4 now comes up as a weak match, as long as it passes the waveform check.
1406	
1407	</Steps>
1408	
1409	If the message ends "too little room to compare their sound", Frame Job found no candidates at all. Check that both clips have enough sound to compare, and try longer trims.
1410	
1411	## With an agent
1412	
1413	An agent gets no sheet. A weak match moves nothing and the agent is told the move it would make, so it should ask you. It applies the match by calling `sync_audio` again with `accept_weak: true`, and only once you've agreed to that move. See [Tools: audio](/mcp/tools-audio/).
1414
